units.la: Quid est ista cupiditas [?] Concupiscentiae, cum ei ipse ecclie [?] sabeant modum. Tunc enim rapiunt, quando sitiunt, parum vero prodest cum senserint satietatem. Insatiabilis est sola avaritia diuitiarum, semper rapit, et nunquam satiatur, nec Deum timet, nec hominem reuerentur [?], nec patri parcit, nec matrem agnoscit, nec fratri obtemperat.
units.tr: What is this greed? Desires, when the things themselves have their own limit. For they snatch when they are thirsty, but it does little good once they have felt satisfaction. Only the greed for riches is insatiable: it always snatches and is never satisfied. It fears neither God nor respects man, it spares neither father nor acknowledges mother, and it obeys no brother.

units.la: NTER septem Mundi miracula, Templum Ephesium recensetur, Dianæ fictitiæ Deæ dicatum, postquam annis supra ducentos vicenis, à totâ Asiâ, incredibili sumtu extructum esset.
units.tr: Among the seven wonders of the world is counted the temple at Ephesus, dedicated to the fictitious goddess Diana, which was built at incredible expense by all of Asia over more than two hundred and twenty years.

units.la: Ego verò, nec structuræ magnificentiâ, nec summâ impensarum moveor, quò minùs inter omnia Templa alia, primas, & merito quidem, ei attribuam, quod non gentilium diis, commentitiis illis, sed Deo vero Opt. Max. Salomon (at quâtus Rex!) Hierosolymis, tum elegantiâ & splendore operis, tum sumtu stupendo ita exstruxit & instruxit, ut omnib. admirationi esset, nec facilè, opinor, inventus fuerit, qui mirabilem istam machinam absque stupore contemplaretur.
units.tr: But I am not moved, by the magnificence of its construction or by the vast sum of its cost, to refrain from giving it, and rightly so, first place among all other temples. It was not dedicated to the gods of the Gentiles, those fictions, but to the true God, the best and greatest. Solomon (what a king he was!) built and furnished it at Jerusalem with such elegance and splendour of workmanship, and at such stupendous cost, that it was an object of wonder to all. I suppose it would be hard to find anyone who could look upon that marvellous structure without amazement.

units.la: Sia. cum utroq; Templum, qp nunc produco, Jesuiticum, conferre libeat: Deum immortale, quam illi quidem similimum, & ex omni penè parte respondere, at ab hoc plane esse diversum, deprehendetur!
units.tr: Since I wish to compare with it the temple I am now bringing forward, the Jesuit temple, you will find, immortal God, that it is very like the other and in almost every part corresponds to it, and yet is plainly unlike it!

units.la: Priùs de hoc videamus. Hierosolymitanum Salomon aedificadum curavit, in quo verus & unus Deus, cui illud dicaverat, ad eum modum, nec aliter, quem ipse in verbo praescripserat, coleretur. Erat igitur templum istud Parochiae instar, ad quam gens universa Israelitica, statis & solennibus festis, conveniebat, ne cosensus in religione divelleretur. Neque igitur alibi, quam isthic offerre licebat Sacrificia. Nihilo tamen minus per Tribus omnes in urbibus & locis aliis frequentioribus Synagogae institutae erant, certae nimirum aedes coetibus sacris destinatae, ubi Sabbathi diebus populus auditum Legis & Prophetarum lectionem atq; expositionem, & ad preces publicas conveniret, ne religionis exercitium ullo modo negligeretur, & Legis divinae cognitio apud vulgus intercideret.
units.tr: Let us first look at the temple at Jerusalem. Solomon saw to its building, so that in it the true and only God, to whom he had dedicated it, might be worshipped in the manner, and in no other, which he had himself prescribed in his Word. That temple therefore served as a kind of parish church, to which the whole Israelite nation came at the set and solemn feasts, so that unity in religion might not be broken. Nor was it lawful to offer sacrifices anywhere else than there. Nevertheless, in all the tribes, in the towns and other more populous places, synagogues were set up, that is, certain buildings set apart for sacred assemblies, where on the Sabbath the people would gather to hear the Law and the Prophets read and expounded, and to join in public prayers, so that the exercise of religion should in no way be neglected and knowledge of the divine Law should not die out among the common people.

units.la: Etsi autem Prophetae Domini veram de Deo doctrinam fideliter tradebant, & cultus a Deo praeceptos diligenter exigebant; & veri Israelitae Deum verum, ad modum divinitus praescriptum sincere colebant: nox tamen a Satana Pseudoprophetae, postmodum Pharisaei, & id genus alii hierophantae, exsuscitati sunt, qui in sacrificia confidere, ac proinde ea accumulare jubebant;
units.tr: Although the prophets of the Lord faithfully delivered the true doctrine concerning God, and diligently required the worship that God had commanded, and although the true Israelites sincerely worshipped the true God in the manner divinely prescribed, yet false prophets, raised up by Satan, and afterwards the Pharisees and other hierophants of that kind, arose, who trusted in sacrifices and therefore ordered them to be multiplied;

units.la: Templum Domini, Templum Domini, Templum Domini in ore habentes, non veri Pastores, sed Mercenarii, quippe sei-psos, oviculis interim perfidiosè neglectis, pascentes.
units.tr: holding continually on their lips "The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord." They were not true shepherds but hired hands, who fed themselves while treacherously neglecting the little sheep.

units.la: Sic & Pseudoisraëlitę, quantum vis ex patre Israële essent, ne externo quidè cultu ex præscripto voluntatis divinæ defungebantur. Nam Baalem in terrâ sanctâ coluerunt, & lucos plantârunt, quin etiam ex gentilium ritibus & consuetudinibus numero non pauca, eáque nefanda, adjicere non erubuerunt.
units.tr: So too the false Israelites, however much they may have been sons of the patriarch Israel, did not even discharge the external worship according to the prescription of the divine will. For they worshipped Baal in the holy land, and planted groves; and moreover they were not ashamed to add to the rites and customs of the Gentiles, and those not few in number and unholy ones at that.

units.la: Pari ratione Pseudo-Judæi, contagione istâ Israëlitarum vicinorum & fratrum cõ-taminati, sub Achaso & Manasse Regibus, in ipsum Domini templū idola, aras, & si-milia intulêre, neq; uniso amplius templo cõtenti, præter istud, in locis amœniorib. montibus, collibus, sylvis, viis, pratis, & vallibus, quin locorū ubivis, Sacella ac delubra Deorū, & in his altaria sine numero extruxêre: & cùm Rex religiosorū omnium reli-giosissimus, magnus ille Josias, idololatriæ sustulisset; domi tamen suæ, ad postes & ostia ędium multi statuas & imagines habu-ere, quas cultu divino dignati sunt super-sticio.
units.tr: In the same way the false Jews, tainted by the contagion of their neighbours and brethren the Israelites, under the kings Ahaz and Manasseh introduced idols, altars and the like into the very temple of the Lord. Nor were they content with the one temple alone: besides it, they built altars without number on the pleasanter mountains, hills, woods, roads, meadows and valleys, indeed in every place, and shrines and sanctuaries of the gods. And although King Josiah, the most religious of all the religious kings, the great man, had removed idolatry, many of the people still kept statues and images at the doorposts and doors of their houses, and, superstitiously, paid them divine worship:

units.la: (·) 3 stitiosè miseri, & miserè supstitiosi. Quid? quòd præter lustralem aquam, per Mosen divinitus mandatâ, novos purificationum & ablutionum ritus ex suo cerebro finxe-runt, quos privatim domi suæ exercerent? Utriq; verò, partim Israëlitæ, partim Judæi, eò dementiæ ꝓgressi sunt, ut cœlorum etiam exercitui, imò Molocho sacra faciētes, nefario infantes charissimos sacro destinârint, subjectis illos prunis torrendo.
units.tr: wretchedly superstitious, and superstitiously wretched. And what of this? Besides the lustral water commanded by God through Moses, they invented from their own brains new rites of purification and washing, which they practised privately at home. And both parties, some Israelites and some Jews, advanced so far in madness that, sacrificing even to the host of heaven and indeed to Moloch, they wickedly consecrated their dearest infants to him, burning them on heaped coals.

units.la: Quid verò nostri Jesuitæ? Nostri, inquâ, si posthac in Christo, quod equidem opto, vix sperare tamè, ac ne vix quidem, ausim. Eos n. è Papistis præcipuè produco, quando ipso nomine teste, totius orbis sese profitentur Salvatores, doctoresq;. Quid igitur illi? Audiamus. Nõ ovum similius ovo, non oculo exactiús respondet oculus, atq; istis ipsis populi Dei Seductoribus. Jesuitæ: qui Deo vero & sincero cius cultu, maximam partè neglecto, sacris externi Copus operatum sermone barbaro vocant Scholastici) demereri præsumunt: qui pietatè potius in labris, quàm in fibris natam habent: qui Missæ sacrificium in Ecclesiâ urgent, & tanto quidem id cumulo, ut ipsos pro pace, lachrymis, pluviâ, serenitate, sapientiâ, pientiâ, loco stabili, incarceratis, contra sterilitate, pestem, tribulationes, pro agonizantib°, etiam pro jamdudum mortuis, Missas celebrare non pudeat: qui Templū Domini mirificè crepant: qui de sede Apostolicâ thrasonicè gloriantur: q; successione ordinariam ad quævis obtédunt: qui idola in Ecclesias introducere & exornare nō timent, veris interim &vivis Dei imaginib° turpiter neglectis ac crudeliter excarnificatis: qui deniq; parentib° persuadent, scholis istis cacolycis leētissimos liberos (at quàm pignus charum è charâ manu!) erudiendos committant; at consentire detrectantes vi minisq; adigere norunt, Plagiarii; vel hoc certè non improbant, si parentes Benedicto, Dominico, Francisco, & divis ceteris, liberos suos offerant, illos in Monachorū & Moniahum claustra detrudentes, ad ignem certissimum, ubi uruntur, contra præceptum Apostoli.
units.tr: And what of our Jesuits? Our Jesuits, I say, if indeed I may still call them ours in Christ, which I would gladly wish, though I hardly dare hope it, and scarcely dare to hope it at all. I bring them forward chiefly as Papists, since by their very name they profess themselves the saviours and teachers of the whole world. What then do they do? Let us hear. Nothing is more like an egg than an egg, nor one eye more exactly matches another, than these very seducers of the people of God. The Jesuits, who presume to win God's favour by external ceremonies, which for the most part neglect true and sincere worship of him (the Schoolmen call these ceremonies opus operatum, the work done, in barbarous speech); who have their piety on their lips rather than in their hearts; who press the sacrifice of the Mass upon the Church, and do so with such a heap of Masses that they are not ashamed to celebrate Masses for peace, for tears, for rain, for fine weather, for wisdom, for piety, for a steady place, for prisoners, against barrenness and plague and tribulations, for the dying, and even for those who died long ago; who loudly boast of the temple of the Lord; who vaunt about the Apostolic See, and claim ordinary succession for whatever they please; who do not fear to introduce and adorn idols in the churches, while the true and living images of God are shamefully neglected and cruelly butchered; and who, finally, persuade parents to entrust their most charming children (what a dear pledge from a dear hand!) to these wicked schools for instruction; but whoever refuses to consent they know how to force by violence and threats, the kidnappers that they are. Nor do they disapprove, at least, if parents offer their children to Benedict, Dominic, Francis and the other saints, thrusting them into the cloisters of monks and nuns, bound for a most certain fire where they are burned, contrary to the command of the Apostle.

units.la: Verùm enim verò, ne quid dissimulem, extant in Templis Jesuitarum non pauca, quæ ex Judaico illi mutuati sunt, quamvis ex merâ Res hoc ipsa loquitur, lector Christiane: quod nullo negotio deprehendes, sive structuram templi & hujus partes
units.tr: But, to conceal nothing, there are in the temples of the Jesuits not a few things borrowed from that Jewish worship, as the thing itself speaks plainly, Christian reader, even without any trouble on your part to find out. You will recognise this whether you look at the structure of the temple and its principal parts,

units.la: 1. Cor. 7. 5. Cum vero Sa lomonico con gruentes per χαχῶ ζηλίαν.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 7. 5. When indeed they agree with the Solomonic [temple] through evil zeal [κακῷ ζηλίαν].

units.la: partes primarias, atrium inquam, sive gre- mium, plebi obvium, tum deinde chorum seu presbyterium; sedem sacerdotum, ra- sæ istius familiæ; deniq; Sacrarium, (quo- cum hoc quidem Sanctô Sanctorum, quod soli Pontifici patebat; istud vero medium Sancto respondeat) à se invicem distinctas spectaveris, ut hac ratione à Clericis, ceu excellentioribus & longè sanctissimis scili- cet, Laici, & inter hos ipse etiam olim Im- perator, veluti minus sancti, siquidem non sacri, chrismate non inuncti, charactere be- stiæ non insigniti, separari queant: sive et- iam (ut in unum ista omnia fasciculum à me colligentur) ad templum pertinentia, Altaria dico, & quæ in his offeruntur, sa- crificia, una cum ornamentis variis atq; vasorum supellectile preciosissima, vestes itidem Pontificales, & Leviticas variega- tas, candelabra & lychnos, igne perpetuo ardentem, organa etiam musica, & aquam lustralem. Taceo consecrationem atque dedicationem templorum & altarium. Ta- ceo Sacrificulorum & Monachorum, atq; id genus aliorû, ordines distinctos. Ecquis enim, obsecro te, universa atq; singula ce- tera recenseat? quæ Judaismum ita sapiunt, ut nemo hoc, opinor, sanæ mentis, & quisensu omni orbatus non fuerit, facilè inficias ire ausit.
units.tr: that is, the courtyard, or nave, open to the common people, then the choir or presbytery, the seat of the priests, the shrine of that family; and finally the sanctuary (of which the one part corresponds to the Holy of Holies, which only the High Priest might enter, and the other to the Holy Place), each kept apart from the others, so that by this arrangement the laity may be separated from the clergy, as more excellent and far holier, and among the laity even the emperor himself, as less holy, since not consecrated, not anointed with chrism, not marked with the beast's character. Or you will see it if you gather all these things into one bundle, as I do here: the things pertaining to the temple, I mean the altars and the sacrifices offered on them, together with the various ornaments and the most precious store of vessels, the priestly and Levitical vestments embroidered in many colours, the candelabra and lamps burning with perpetual fire, the musical organs too, and the lustral water. I pass over the consecration and dedication of temples and altars. I pass over the distinct orders of the sacrificing priests and monks, and others of that kind. For who, I beg you, would list each and every one of the rest? They smell so strongly of Judaism that no one of sound mind and with any sense left, I think, could easily dare to deny it.

units.la: Neq; cogitant miseri, quin verius facere hoc recusant, ceremonias istiusmodi, ceu umbras & figuras, ac typos futurorum, servatoris nostri IESU Christi sacrificio in cruce peracto, abolitas fuisse. In cujus rei testimonium evidentius, templi velum, patiente Domino, scissum, & politia Judaica, unà cum templo ita excisa fuit, ut deinceps, etsi iterum id atq; iterum attentaretur, nunquam potuerit instaurari.
units.tr: Nor do these wretched men consider how much more truly they would act if they refused these ceremonies, since they were abolished as shadows and figures and types of things to come, when our Saviour Jesus Christ offered his sacrifice on the cross. As the clearest evidence of this, when the Lord suffered, the veil of the temple was torn, and the Jewish polity was cut off together with the temple, so that afterwards, although attempts were made again and again, it could never be restored.

units.la: Addo aliquid amplius. Cum illis, quæ in Scripturis expresse mandata atq; observata extant, è diametro pugnantia cōminiscei, atq; ea, quæ humana libido adinvenit, pro cultibus divinis venditare, & præter templa, in compitis & triviis, adeoque etiā in locis solitariis, ob somnia & revelationes aniles alias, sine sine & sine modo, sacella (capellas nominant) & monasteria extruere, inq; iis altaria ædificare, & his universis ac singulis reliquias Sanctorum recōdere, idola & imagines proponere, quæ publicè in Oratoriis prostent, & coram his Missas celebrare, lucernas seu candelas ad idola collocare, suffimenta iisdem accedere, & illis ipsis idolis sese incurvare, eaque adorare, & preculas Deo divisq; adnumerare, & peregrinationes ad Sanctorum limina instituere; id vero omne istiusmodi est, ut non nisi Pseudo illum Judaismum sapiat, qui a genuino illo procul (heu nimis procul!) recederat.
units.tr: I add something more. They have invented, against those things which are expressly commanded and observed in the Scriptures, and they puff up as divine worship what human lust has devised; and besides churches, at crossroads and in the byways, and even in solitary places, on account of old wives' dreams and other revelations, without end and without measure, they build shrines (which they call chapels) and monasteries, and erect altars in them; they deposit relics of the saints in all these, and set up idols and images, which stand publicly in the oratories; they celebrate Masses before them, place lamps or candles before the idols, approach them with incense, bow down before those very idols and adore them, add little prayers to God and the saints, and undertake pilgrimages to the thresholds of the saints. All this is of such a kind that it savours of nothing but that false Judaism which had departed far (alas, far too far!) from that genuine one.

units.la: Quam ob causam verus ille Messias, & populi Judaici Rex, a Hierosolymitano ingressu, Templum reformaturus, gravissime in Sacerdotes invehitur, qui nundinationes, quæstus sui causâ, introduci ferebant, & boves, oves, columbas, & quæ sacrificiis inservire poterant, alia, in templi atrio dividendi permittebant, ut ex eorum emtione aliqua lucri pars ad ipsos rediret, & plures alii ad sacrificandum allicerentur.
units.tr: Wherefore that true Messiah and King of the Jewish people, when he entered Jerusalem to reform the Temple, rebuked most severely the priests who allowed markets to be set up for their own profit, and who permitted oxen, sheep, doves and other things that could serve for sacrifice to be sold in the court of the Temple, so that part of the gain from the buying would come back to them and many more would be drawn to sacrifice.

units.la: Adeo autem indigne tulit hac ratione domum Domini turpiter prophanatam, & domum precationis in latronum speluncam commutatam; ut etiam ad flagella & verbera descendere non dubitarit.
units.tr: He took it so badly that the house of the Lord was thus shamefully profaned and the house of prayer turned into a den of robbers, that he did not hesitate to resort even to whips and blows.

units.la: Quod si hodie e cœlis is ipse Dominus Jesus ad nos reversus templum synagogasq; Jesuiticas ingrediatur, atq; abominandam istam prophanationem intueatur, ut dubium mihi nullũ est, quin rei indignitate motus, ad flagella Jesuitis parata, eos gravissimâ tali aut simili oratione sit objungaturus!
units.tr: But if today that same Lord Jesus were to return to us from heaven, enter the Jesuit temples and synagogues, and look upon this abominable profanation, there is no doubt in my mind that, moved by the outrage, he would address the Jesuits with the most grievous speech of this kind or similar, with whips ready!

units.la: Vos Jesuita, fures nominis mei, & latrones ovium mearum, vos, utut ovillâ pelle induti, lupi tamen rapaces, vos mercenarii & perfidi pastores estis, qui de domo precationis pietatisq; latronum facitis speluncâ. Ecquid enim, hypocrita, in vestris templis audio? ecquid in illis video? Haccine sit vera verum Deum colendi ratio? Vbi igitur sincera verbi divini prædicatio? ubi legitimus Sacramentorum usus? ubi Invotio ad solum Deum directa, & cultus alii, sincerâ fide Deo præstandi?
units.tr: You Jesuits, thieves of my name and robbers of my sheep, you who, though clothed in sheepskin, are nonetheless ravening wolves, you are hired and faithless shepherds, who make a house of prayer and piety into a den of robbers! For what, hypocrite, do I hear in your temples? What do I see in them? Is this the true way of worshipping the true God? Where, then, is the sincere preaching of the Word of God? Where is the lawful use of the sacraments? Where is invocation directed to God alone, and the other worship to be rendered to God in sincere faith?

units.la: Quid sibi vero volunt fabulæ aniles, & pura putá mendacia, qua Legeda vocatus Sanctorum, quorum vel ipsum Satanam pudeat? Quid de Scripturâ sacrâ, de Deo, de Angelis, de peccato, de Lege, de Liberi arbitrii viribus, de Evangelio, de Prædestinatione, de justificatione, de Bonis operibus, de Pœnitentiâ, de Ecclesiâ, de universis atque singulis doctrina Christiana capitibus aliis, errores execrandi?
units.tr: But what do the old wives' tales and downright lies mean, which are called the legends of the saints, at which Satan himself would blush? What of the execrable errors about Holy Scripture, God, the angels, sin, the Law, the powers of free will, the Gospel, predestination, justification, good works, repentance, the Church, and all and each of the other heads of Christian doctrine?

units.la: Quid vero horrenda Sacramentorum prophanatio? Quid enim in Baptismi sacrosancti administratione Exorcismus, salis et aquæ consecratio, insufflatio, crucis toties reiterata impressio, impuri Sacerdotis sputu, Chrisma seu Oleum salutis, infantuli per ætatem ad audiendum & loquendum adhuc inepti compellatio, denique vestis illa candida, & candela?
units.tr: And what of the horrible profanation of the sacraments? For what in the administration of holy Baptism are exorcism, the consecration of salt and water, the breathing upon the child, the cross impressed so many times, the spittle of the unclean priest, the chrism or oil of salvation, the addressing of the infant, who by reason of age is still unfit to hear and to speak, and finally that white garment and the candle?

units.la: Quid auricularis Confessio vestra? quâ ad enumerationem omnium delictorum, levissimorum etiam, erudelâ conscientiarum excarnificatores, sensu peccatorum
units.tr: What of your auricular Confession, by which, through the enumeration of all offences, even the very slightest, you cruelly butcher consciences and drive the afflicted into a sense of their sins?

units.la: {1} Doctrina corruptio. catorum afflictos cogitis, & vobis potestatem ipsissimam divinam, peccata, pro lubitu vestro, tam retinendi, quam dimittendi, praeter omnem Scripturam, arrogatis ipsi; Papae tamen uni gravissimis in casibus privilegio peculiari reservato: & scelerati, ad seditionem, ad veneficia, ad parricidia, subditorum animos, adversus legitimos suos Reges atq; Principes, in Confessione ista auriculari hostiliter instigatis, & sub minis excommunicationis Hispania tyranno obligare non veremini?
units.tr: Corruption of doctrine. And you claim for yourselves, beyond all Scripture, the very power of God to retain or forgive sins at your pleasure, though this power is reserved to the Pope alone, by a special privilege, in the gravest cases. And do you not hesitate, in this auricular confession, to incite the minds of your subjects, the wicked ones, hostilely to sedition, to poisonings and to parricides against their lawful kings and princes, and to bind them under threat of excommunication to the Spanish tyrant?

units.la: Quid Cœna sacra in actionem toto genere diversam transmutatio, & talis quaedam illa, ut nulla, vel levissima aliqua, de institutione prima, indicia amplius reliqua appareant? In ea namq; ubi panis verus, & huius fractio, ac in manus prabitio? Quid illius loco, Oblata, panes isti numulárii, Juda argenteos, proditionis mercedem (ridiculum!) representantes, una cum agni aut crucifixi impressione? Vbi vero calix? Heu sacrilegium! Quin Omnes ex eo bibere jussit? Qui itaq; soli illum vobis, sacrificí, at Laicis longè indigniores, adeoq; hominum malorum omnium, quotquot in orbe Christiano vivunt, pessimi, reservatis? etiam vinum cum aquâ miscentes?
units.tr: What of the Lord's Supper, changed into an action wholly different in kind, and transformed in such a way that no trace, or the very slightest, of the first institution remains? For where in it is the true bread, its breaking, and its being given into the hands? In its place, what are these "oblata", those money-changers' loaves, representing the silver of Judas, the reward of betrayal (how ridiculous!), together with the impression of a lamb or of the crucified one? And where is the cup? Alas, what sacrilege! Did not he order all to drink from it? Why do you reserve it for yourselves alone, as sacrificers, while laymen are far more unworthy, and so the worst of all the evil men living in the Christian world? Do you even mix wine with water?

units.la: Quid video autem praeter vestimenta Pontificalia & Levitica, gemmis & auro intertexta: praeter vasa aurea splendidissima) de ridiculis, partem etiam maximam superstitiosis, in theatri à Missa celebratione, Sacrificuli, ceu Mimi cujusdam, aut histrionis gesticulationibus? dum oculis profundè ad altare, ad illius autem medium duodecies, semelsaltem ad populum & leviter quidem se inclinat? novinovies osculum altari (semel tamen etiam libro) infi-git? manus & brachia multoties elevat & extendit? scurram se potius, quàm Ecclesiae ministrum probans? Signum etiam crucis reiterat? ab uno altaris cornu ad alterum hinc inde circumcurfitat, & agyrta persona induens, hac illac se vertit? insuper incenso benedicit? furfuraceum istud missaticum numen, neque panem tamen, sed panis spumam, sed illius fruftulum, in altum elevat? choro, Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus, acclamante? quòd campanula pulsatur, ubi tum protinus spectatores attoniti coram pane procumbunt, incurvat se vulgus miserrum, inflectunt se primarii etiam nobiles, & pectus tundunt, jusjurandum ex imo ducentes: Mi Domine, Mi Deus? Quòd organa musica operosa & theatrica adhibentur, tu- multuosis diversarum vocum garritus, dum tubis, lituis, fistulis ac sambucis omnia perstrepunt, et cum his certant hominum voces? Audiuntur amatoria foedaq; cantilena, ad quas scorta mimiq; saltitant cum tripudio. Lingua etiam ignota cantus omnes funditis, scilicet ut idiota ne quid intelligat, neq; illi AMEN pronuntiare liceat.
units.tr: What do I see besides the pontifical and levitical vestments, interwoven with gems and gold, besides the most splendid golden vessels? Of ridiculous things, and mostly superstitious ones at that, in the celebration of the Mass, like a theatre: the little sacrificers, like some mime or actor, with their gestures, while they cast their eyes deeply down at the altar, bow to its middle twelve times, and to the people once only, and that slightly? They kiss the altar nine times (once, however, the book as well), raise and stretch out their hands and arms many times, proving themselves a buffoon rather than a minister of the Church? They also repeat the sign of the cross, run hither and thither from one horn of the altar to the other, and, assuming the character of a mountebank, turn this way and that? Moreover, they bless with incense and lift on high that bran-like Mass deity, not bread but the foam of bread, or a fragment of it, while the choir cries out "Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus"? When a little bell is rung, the astonished spectators at once fall prostrate before the bread; the wretched crowd bows down, and even the leading nobles bend and beat their breasts, swearing from the depths of the heart: "My Lord, my God!" Elaborate and theatrical organ music is employed, and the tumultuous chatter of many voices, while everything resounds with trumpets, cornets, flutes and sackbuts, and human voices vie with them? Amorous and foul songs are heard, to which prostitutes and mimes dance with revelry. You pour out all your songs in a foreign tongue, of course so that the uneducated layman may understand nothing and not be allowed to say AMEN.

units.la: Porrò, quid audio, partim de transelementatione, partim de corporis minutuli inclusione, & in, cum, sub panis specie occultatione miraculosa, ac proinde in hostiae consecratione, magica corporis e coelo, vi prolationis verborum quinq;, H. e. e. c. m. quae cum habitu fiat, detractione, deniq; quae corporis ore, etiam a sceleratissimis fiat, veri illius corporis mei et quidem vestibus induti, manducatione, conjunctâ cum sensuali fractione & dentium attritione, (horrendum!) et more in ore ac ventriculo communicantis manßione, neque illa tamen diuturniore, quàm dum species panis per-maneat, ubi tum ab Angelis corpus (agnoscitis verba vestra) in cœlum reportari constet? Quid, quòd sa-crificuli, unicâ Missa lessiunculâ, se quavis scelera expiare posse, autumant? Quid panis ceu idoli ad-orationem, & in sacramentarias adiculas repositio-nem, & solennem circumgestationem, qua vicatim fit, commemorem? quid, quòd etiam mures, canes, & porci hostiam comedentes, verum istud corpus sus-cipiant, itaq; crudeliter laniandi, et cineres in sacra-rium reponendi sint? quid infinita alia, quorum vel solum modo meminisse horret animus?
units.tr: Further, what do I hear, partly of transelementation, partly of the enclosing of a tiny body and its miraculous concealment in, with and under the appearance of bread; and consequently, in the consecration of the host, of the magical drawing down of the body from heaven by the power of the five words spoken, H. e. e. c. m., which is done with the priestly vestments; and finally, that the body, even of the most wicked, is taken by the mouth, that is, the eating of that true body of mine, clothed in its garments, joined with sensual breaking and grinding of the teeth (horrible!), and with its remaining in the mouth and stomach of the communicant in the manner of a meal, yet not longer than while the appearance of bread remains; whereupon, it is agreed, the body is carried back to heaven by angels (you acknowledge your own words)? What of the priests who claim that by a single Mass-broth, a little boiled dish, they can atone for any crimes? Shall I mention the adoration of the bread as an idol, its placing in sacramental little shrines, and the solemn carrying about of it, which is done street by street? What of the fact that mice, dogs and pigs eating the host receive that true body, and so must be cruelly torn apart and their ashes placed in the sacristy? What of countless other things, which the mind shudders even to recall?

units.la: Quid? quòd oblationem & sacrificium peragere & offerre pro hominibus, quà vivis, quà etiam mor-tuis, atque adeò profuperis, pro terrestribus, pro infe-ris, & prater hos, etiam pro brutis, pro inanimatis, Missas celebrare non erubescitis? Ex quo fit, ut ho-micida, adulteri, fures, sufurarii perjuri & alii scele-rati, catervatim accurrant, qui sine ullo bono motu, externo cultu ibi defungantur.
units.tr: What? That you are not ashamed to celebrate Masses, to perform and offer an oblation and sacrifice for men, for the living, for the dead, and even for those above, for the earthly, for those below in the dead, and besides these even for brute beasts and inanimate things? From this it follows that murderers, adulterers, thieves, pilferers, perjurers and other wicked men flock to them in crowds, and there finish off, with no good motion of the mind, only by outward worship.

units.la: Quid vero sibi vult idololatrica & blasphema Angelorum & defunctorum Sanctorum hominum, quinetiam rerum inanimatarum invocatio? Quid myrias ista adinventionum, hoc est, traditionum humanarum? Templa dico, capellas, aras, idola, candelas ipsâ etiam meridie accensas, thymiamata, & alia infinita? quid bona vestra intentiones, di-vino mandato destitută?
units.tr: What, then, does the idolatrous and blasphemous invocation of angels, of dead saints, and even of inanimate things mean? What is that myriad of inventions, that is, of human traditions? I speak of temples, chapels, altars, idols, candles lit even at midday, incense, and countless other things. What of your good intentions, destitute of divine command?

units.la: Quid inter cetera nundinationes? Qui (ma-lum) non modò intra templorum ambitum merci-monia monia nefariè exerceri, ipsis præsertim encæniorum diebus feriatis, permittitis, loca sacrorum conventuum in mercaturas & nundinas commutando: sed etiam ubivis locorū omnia venalia exponitis? dum terram, si loco, ut arbitramini, quis sanctiore, pro precio numerati ratione, sepeliatur, aquam consecratam, aërem, ob nolarum sonitum, ignem, ob incensa, vel fumos verius, divenditis, & numos vobis aureos liberaliter solventibus, liberationem ex igni purgatorio liberaliter pollicemini? Qui ex ciborum discrimine pecuniam corradere, & libertatem ovorum ac butyri, etiam carnium, diebus jejunii, quos commenti estis, edendarum, concedere, & ex re quavis odorem habere gratum & captare lucrum non erubescitis?
units.tr: What, among other things, of the markets? Who (wretched!) not only permit trade to be carried on wickedly within the precincts of the temples, especially on the feast days of consecrations, turning the places of sacred assemblies into shops and markets, but also put everything up for sale everywhere? You sell earth, if someone is to be buried in a place you think holier, at a price counted out; holy water; air, because of the sound of the bells; fire, because of the incense, or rather the smoke; and while they generously pay you gold coins, you generously promise deliverance from the purgatorial fire. Who do not blush to gather money from the distinction of foods, to grant on the fast days you have invented the liberty of eating eggs and butter, and even meats, and to catch at any matter that gives a pleasing odour and seek gain from it?

units.la: Qui venalia apud vos exponuntur Sacerdotia, rasura, unctiones, pallia, etiam optimiores alia conditiones, neque tamen nisi pecunia redimantur? quin immò indignis quoque illa conferre soletis, dum boves & asinos in templa introducitis. Itaque vasa nunc quidem aurea preciosa, at ligneos Sacerdotes habetis, qui magnis quotidie boatibus, ventres obœsiores, & rudentes asini, sono intempestivo, Templa replent; (præter moniales, qua ea lingua, quam non intelligunt, Psalmos murmurando recitant) cum olim vasa in templis lignea, at aurei Sacerdotes inveniren- tur. Hinc etiam tot Missæ, & Sacramentorum tantus tumulus, quin cœlum, ipseque Deus venum a vobis datur. Vt recte dixerit, quicunque dixit: Venalia Roma,
units.tr: Do you not also sell for money the priesthoods, tonsures, anointings, palls, and other better positions that are offered among you, and grant them only in return for payment? Indeed, you are accustomed to bestow them even on the unworthy, while you lead oxen and asses into the temples. So now you have golden vessels, precious ones, but wooden priests, who fill the temples every day with loud bellowings, with bellies bulging and asses braying at untimely sound (apart from the nuns, who mutter the Psalms in a language they do not understand). Once, by contrast, the vessels in the temples were wooden, but the priests were golden. Hence also so many Masses and so great a bustle of sacraments. Indeed heaven and God himself are sold by you, as whoever said it rightly said: Rome sells everything.

units.la: Templa, sacerdotes, altaria, sacra, corona, Ignes, thura, preces, cœlum est venale, Deusque. Et quid tandem nominari queat, ex quo, negotiatores avarissimi, quaestum non faciatis longe uberrimum qui Papae, sacrosancti vestri Patris, vestigiis insistetes, aliorum hereditates intercipitis, & territoria pene atque integra regna hoc auctupio in potestatem vestram redigere, ac magnam opum vim colligere conamini? Qui deniq; adulteri, fornicationem cum idolis exercetis? & fures Deo gloriam surripitis? & mercenarii, sanguine pretioso redemtas oves vobis vendicatis? & latrones, tum falsa doctrina sectatorum vestrorum animas iugulatis, tum eorum corporibus & vita insidiamini, quos vobis contradicere intelligitis?
units.tr: Temples, priests, altars, sacred rites, crowns, fires, incense, prayers: heaven is for sale, and God too. And what can finally be named, you most greedy merchants, from which you do not make a very rich profit, you who tread in the footsteps of the Pope, your most holy Father, and seize the inheritances of others, and try to bring under your power, by this trade, whole territories and almost entire kingdoms, and to gather a great mass of wealth? Finally, you are adulterers who commit fornication with idols, and thieves who steal the glory from God; you are hired hands who claim as your own the sheep redeemed with precious blood; you are robbers who, by the false doctrine of your followers, cut the throats of their souls, and who lie in wait for the bodies and lives of those whom you perceive to be opposing you.

units.la: Repeto igitur hoc: Vos, Iesuitae male feriati, ex domo precationis fecistis latronum speluncam, indignum, qui in Ecclesia feramini! Haec & dubio procul longe duriora Iesuitis Dominus Iesus, si in terris obversaretur. Quid non dicturus ille fit, post tam diuturnae patientiae tempus, quando in ira sua illos compellaturus est, judex vivorum & mortuorum futurus severissimus?
units.tr: I repeat, then: you Jesuits, good-for-nothings, have made a den of robbers out of the house of prayer, unworthy of being counted in the Church! The Lord Jesus, if he were living on earth, would undoubtedly say things to the Jesuits far harsher than these. What will he not say, after so long a time of patience, when he is about to address them in his wrath, he who will be the most severe judge of the living and the dead?

units.la: Atque haec suffecerint de templo Salomonis. Quod si ego pergam cum Ephesino Iesuiticum templum conferre: Deum immortalem, quam amplus excurrendi campus offerretur! Non ratio, non oratio; sed dies me, sed clarta deficerent.
units.tr: Let these things suffice concerning the temple of Solomon. But if I were to go on and compare the Jesuit temple with the one at Ephesus, good God, what a wide field for digression would open up! Neither my reason nor my speech, but the day and my breath would fail me.

units.la: Si namq; Templorum & delubrorum, & in iis, quinetiam in aulis & curiis ipsis, altarialtarium multitudinem stupendâ, & quòd illa mortuis consecrata, quin & ignoto Deo, quòd ad altare thure supplicatum: Si imagines in templa, non hominum solummodò sed & bestiarum, & magno quidem numero introductas, & quòd praeter flores ac coronas, suffitu etiam vel incenso, cereis, sacrificiis, jejuniis, precum battologiis, anathematis, tabellas appendendo, in quibus morbi curati inscripti fuerint, & ex cera, hominis, vituli, ovis & gallinae, &c. imagunculas & oscilla efformata ad Divorum fana adferendo, atq; aliis divinis honoribus, religiosè venerabantur: Si aquam lustralem, quâ animi labes tollatur, & castimonia corporis praestetur, & quâ Sacerdos ad templi januas consistens, ingredientes aspergat: Si Baaliticos Sacerdotes, qui flagris ipsi se concidebant: Haec igitur, & multo plura si spectare, si recensere animus sit; quid erit, amabo te, in quo Ethnicos sibi non appponant, quos imitentur, Jesuitae?
units.tr: For if I were to recount the stupendous number of temples and shrines, and within them altars, even in the halls and courts themselves, and the fact that these were consecrated to the dead, and even to the unknown God, since incense was offered at the altar; if I were to recount the images brought into temples, not only of men but also of beasts, and in great numbers, and that, besides flowers and garlands, people reverently worshipped them with fumigation, incense, candles, sacrifices, fasts, babbling prayers, and votive offerings, hanging up tablets on which the cured diseases were inscribed, and bringing to the shrines of the saints little images and wax figures of a man, a calf, a sheep, or a hen, and other divine honours; if I were to recount the lustral water, by which the stain of the soul is removed and purity of body is secured, and with which the priest, standing at the doors of the temple, sprinkles those who enter; if I were to recount the priests of Baal who cut themselves with whips: then, if one wished to survey and list these things, and much more besides, what, I ask you, will there be in which the Jesuits will not have the heathen to imitate?

units.la: Quid? quòd Ethnicos ipsos, cognitionis verè veri Dei ignaros, à Papicolis superatos constat? Quanto enim horribilior horum superstitio, quòd aquam lustralem mortuorum sepulchris & tumbis lapideis pideis inspergunt, ut quæ mortuorum de⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠liētis expiandis serviat, & ardores Purga⁠torii restinguendo, cruciatus alioquin a⁠trocissimos, ipsis tolerabiliores reddat? Et, quòd eam, non nisi incantamentis priùs infecta fuerit, adhibeant: cum Ethnici il⁠la purissima, qualem viva fontis vel amnis scaturigo suppeditaret, uterentur? Quan⁠tò etiam horribilior superstitio, quòd in privatis quoq; ædibus, Sacella seu Capel⁠las, id quod apud Ethnicos interdictum & legibus probè cautum erat, ædificarunt? Quòd etiam Ossaria condiderunt, exem⁠plo novo, in quibus offa & crania, post⁠quam ex sepulchris fuerint effossa, ma⁠gno acervo reponantur, & ad incanta⁠tiones pro superstitiosâ plebeculâ asser⁠ventur?
units.tr: What of the fact that it is well established that the heathen themselves, ignorant of the true knowledge of the true God, have been surpassed by the Papists? For how much more horrible is their superstition, in that they sprinkle lustral water on the graves and stone tombs of the dead, as if it served to expiate the sins of the dead, and by quenching the fires of Purgatory makes the most atrocious torments more bearable for them! And in that they use this water only after it has been first infected with incantations, whereas the heathen used that purest water which a living spring or river stream supplied! How much more horrible is this superstition too, that they have built shrines or chapels even in private houses, which among the heathen was forbidden and carefully guarded by law! Also in that they have established ossuaries, a new kind of practice, in which bones and skulls, once dug up from the graves, are heaped up in great piles and kept for incantations for the superstitious common folk.

units.la: Sufficiat hic loci, & nunc temporis, libello isto, quem tibi, lector Christiane, damus, post Pezelianam Austriacæ Cate⁠cheseos utriusque, de Sanctorum invoca⁠tione, Salutatione Angelicâ, refutatione, horrenda idololatricæ istius, & in Deum blasphemæ ad Sanctos defunctos, etiam nonnullos ex illis commentitios, quin ad inanimata quoque directæ invocationis, in me-
units.tr: Let this suffice here and now for the little book which I give to you, Christian reader, after the Pezelian Catechism of Austria, in both its parts, on the invocation of the saints and the Angelic Salutation: a refutation of that horrible idolatry, blasphemous against God, of addressing the dead saints, including some of them fictitious, and even of directing invocation to inanimate things.

units.la: Scopus & summa libelli. Malè de Scop. Ioc. tracta-tionis. in medium produxisse, una cum appendi-ce, de magica & superstitiosa creaturarum consecratione: altera parte indicasse, quos Sanctos, quibus rebus Pontificii, more Ethnicorum, patronos, & Deos tutelares designarint: Postrema deniq; narratione de reliquiis sanctorum retexuisse, ex qua, meridiana luce clarius appareat, in quam horrenda & ridicula monstra Monachi Sanctos Dei homines converterint, ac pinde Christianam religionem adversariis propinârint deridendam.
units.tr: The aim and sum of the little book: I have brought forward in the middle the wrongful treatment of the topic, together with an appendix on the magical and superstitious consecration of creatures; in the other part I have indicated which saints, and by which things, the Papists, after the manner of the heathen, have designated as patrons and guardian gods; and finally, in the last narrative, I have unravelled the matter of the relics of the saints, from which it appears more clearly than the noonday light into what horrible and ridiculous monsters the monks have turned the holy men of God, and so have served up the Christian religion to its adversaries to be mocked.

units.la: Hoc nostrum studium, lectorbenevole, æqui boniqueconsules, & à nobis plura deinceps, cum Bono Deo expectabis.
units.tr: This study of ours, kind reader, you will accept and judge fairly, and you will look for more from us hereafter, God willing.

units.la: Quod reliquum est, ad vos, Jesuitæ, mea se convertat oratio. Inter omnes, quantumvis tædissimas Monachorum familias,
units.tr: As for what remains, let my speech now turn to you, Jesuits. Among all the most loathsome families of monks, however much...

units.la: Vos estis, Deus est testis, Teterrima pestis.
units.tr: You are, God is my witness, a most loathsome plague.

units.la: Liceat enim mihi id, quod de Monachis olim dici meministis, hic quoque de vobis, charissimis eorum fraterculis, usurpare.
units.tr: For I may be allowed to apply to you, their dearest little brothers, here as well, what you remember being said of the monks in the past.

units.la: Quæ res facit, ut mirari desinam, qua auda-
units.tr: This is what makes me cease to wonder at the

units.la: audacia, qua temeritate, & ut uno univer-sa verbo complectar, ut scientia vobis non defit, qua tamen conscientia, illa blasphe-ma, magica & ridicula impudentissimo-rum Monachorum commenta, vos, eo-rum fraterculi, & sedis Antichristi, vel ma-xime strenui assertores atq; vindices, tue-ri, & iis patrocinari non vereamini? Tan-tum enim abest, vos viva voce, vel scriptis publicis, cum alioqui plurimos teneat in-saziabile vestrum scribendi cacoethes, fa-bulis istis contradicere, ut etiam ad harum defensionem manum & stylum dare ausi-tis. Scilicet Diaboli vos filios probatis, qui mendax, qui homicida, Domino atte-stante.
units.tr: boldness and recklessness with which, to sum up in one word, you, the little brothers of those monks and the most vigorous champions and defenders of the seat of Antichrist, do not fear to uphold and patronise those blasphemous, magical and absurd inventions of the most shameless monks. You lack no knowledge, yet with what conscience you do it I cannot tell. Far from contradicting these fables in speech or in published writings, though your incurable itch for writing keeps many of you busy, you have dared to put your hand and pen to their defence. Clearly you prove yourselves sons of the Devil, who, as the Lord testifies, was a liar and a murderer.

units.la: Ecquis igitur vos quoque improbos Je-suitas, mendacii spiritu agitari neget, qui ea impudentissima mendacia, magicas su-perstitiones, & blasphemias horrendas, ad quae obstupescat cœlum, terra contremi-scat, tueri non erubescitis? qui turpissimã & sceleratam mentiendi artem, quam Æ-quivocationis titulo indigitatis, post-quam eam a patre Diabolo, & hujus filio Francisco Monacho foedissimo, vestro fra-terculo, didicistis, improbi Magistri & pa-fidiosi
units.tr: Who then would deny that you too, wicked Jesuits, are driven by the spirit of lying, you who are not ashamed to defend those utterly shameless lies, magical superstitions and horrible blasphemies, at which heaven would be astounded and earth would tremble? You who practise that most foul and wicked art of lying, which you call by the title of Equivocation, having learned it from the father Devil and his son, the most foul monk Francis, your little brother, you wicked masters and faithless

units.la: Hortum impudentia patrocinando Papatui. Ioh. 8. Filii Diaboli: 1. ob mendacia. fidiosi juventutis tenerae corruptores, discipulis miseris, in scholis vestris, cum lacte ipso materno sensim instillare pergitis. Si quis in vobis pudor, si hujus aliqua saltem scintillula, miror, qui vestrum & anilium istiusmodi fabularum, luce hac longe clarissima, vos tandem non pudeat?
units.tr: (marginal note: Defending the Papacy with impudence. John 8. Sons of the Devil: 1. because of lies) corrupters of tender youth, who in your schools keep instilling, bit by bit, into your wretched pupils with their very mother's milk. If you have any shame, if even a small spark of it, I wonder why you are not ashamed, in a light that is far the clearest, of such fables of yours and of old women.

units.la: Ecquis etiam vos homicidii reos neget, qui scilicet crudeles hypocritae, & hirudines, rem & sanguinem Fidelium sitientes, Pontificis Romani, quam Filius ille perditionis in tot martyrum sanctissimorum corpora exercuit tyrannidem, commendare non dubitatis? qui pacis publicae sacrosanctâ jurisjurandi religione sancitae ac confirmatae perturbatores, Catholicos, quos nominatis, Reges & Principes, ad crudelitatem in Evangelicos, classicum ipsi canentes, instigatis, & ruptis humanae societatis vinculis arctissimis, seditionum incendia, per Christianum orbem universum, sceleratissime excitatis? qui juventutem scholasticam & rudem plebeculam, & nobilitatis florem, in auriculari vestra commentitiâ confessione, & quâvis ansa occasione arreptâ, in axiomatibus heretica Jesuitici informatis: Licitum esse, quin ementitomeritorum, cuivis ex subditis, Principem vel Regem occidere, quantumvis Catholicum, si a Papa, vel hujus complicibus, id est, a Jesuitis, viris sapientibus & gravibus, pro tyranno habeatur. Et in isto: Omnes Evangelicos igni, ferro, veneno, pulvere tormentario, bellis, & aliis machinationibus opprimendos.
units.tr: Who would deny that you too are guilty of murder? You cruel hypocrites and leeches, thirsting for the wealth and blood of the faithful, do not hesitate to commend the tyranny of the Roman Pontiff, which that son of perdition exercised over the bodies of so many most holy martyrs. You are the disturbers of public peace, which was sanctioned and confirmed by the most sacred religion of an oath. You sound the trumpet for the Catholics, whom you name kings and princes, and urge them to cruelty against the Evangelicals. Having broken the closest bonds of human society, you most wickedly kindle the fires of sedition throughout the whole Christian world. You instruct the schoolboys, the simple common folk and the flower of the nobility in your whispered, fabricated confession, and on any occasion you seize you teach them these heretical Jesuitical axioms: "That it is lawful for any of the subjects, on whatever pretended ground, to kill a prince or king, however Catholic he may be, if he is regarded as a tyrant by the Pope or his accomplices, that is, by the Jesuits, wise and serious men." And in another: "That all Evangelicals are to be overwhelmed by fire, sword, poison, gunpowder, war and other machinations."

units.la: Hinc tot motuum in Suecia, in Polonia, in Livonia, in Germania, Belgio, Silesia, in regno item Bohemiae, & Moraviae marchionatu, & ubivis terrarum autores: tot seditionum in Gallia, in Transylvania, in Hungaria exsuscitatores: tot Regum ac Principum, Sebastiani Lusitaniae Regis, Mariae reginae Scotiae, Sigismundi Sueciae ac Poloniae regis, Demetrii magni Moscoviae Ducis, Ʒpditores: tot Sicariorū & parricidiarum, ut Carolus Hispaniæ princeps, Johanna Albretana Navarrae regina, Wilhelmus Auraicus Princeps, Henricus III, Galliae Rex, & Stephan’ Potskay Princeps Transylvaniae, e medio tollerentur; ut Henrici IIII. Galliae regis, & Elizabethae reginae Angliae, & Jacobi VI. Angliae ac Scotiae regis, & familiae totius regiae, & Mauritii Principis Auraici, vitae insidiae struerentur, instigatores: tot exiliorum in Austria utraque, in Styria, in Carinthia, in locis aliis vicinis, suasores: tot piorum & innocentissimorum martyrum, in laniena Parisienfi crudelissimâ, excarnificatores: tot denique caedium injustissimarum intentatores, vos Jesuitae exstitistis.
units.tr: Hence you Jesuits have been the authors of so many uprisings in Sweden, Poland, Livonia, Germany, Belgium, Silesia, the kingdom of Bohemia and the margraviate of Moravia, and everywhere on earth; the instigators of so many seditions in France, Transylvania and Hungary; the promoters of the deaths of so many kings and princes: Sebastian, King of Portugal, Mary, Queen of Scots, Sigismund, King of Sweden and Poland, and Demetrius, the so-called Grand Duke of Muscovy. You have been the contrivers of so many assassinations and parricides: that Charles, Prince of Spain, Joan of Albret, Queen of Navarre, William of Orange, Henry III, King of France, and Stephen Bocskay, Prince of Transylvania, should be removed from the midst; that plots against the life of Henry IV, King of France, Elizabeth, Queen of England, James VI, King of England and Scotland, with the whole royal family, and Maurice, Prince of Orange, should be laid. You have been the advisers of so many exiles in both Austrias, in Styria, in Carinthia and in other neighbouring places. Finally, you have been the butchers of so many pious and most innocent martyrs in the most cruel slaughter at Paris, and you have been the planners of so many most unjust killings.

units.la: Utinam vero, utinam dies iste nobis illucescat, quo, (si resipiscere porro denegaveritis; quod, ut Deus à vobis avertat, ex animo precor) ut hactenus eundem cum Templariis fortunam secundam, coacervando ingentes thesauros, & potentiâ omnibus penè formidabili excellendo, experti estis: sic eandem quoque cum illis adversam experiamini: & si non Pontifex ipse; at Catholici alii moderati Reges atque Principes, de secta vestrâ crudelissimâ, & omnium aliarum toti humano generi pestilentissimâ, extirpandâ, consilia inter se ineant: ut, vobis turbatoribus & hostibus pacis publicae è medio sublatis, exoptatissima Ecclesiae & Reip. Christianae pax charitasq; redeat!
units.tr: Would that indeed, would that that day might dawn for us, on which (if you persist in refusing to repent, which God forbid, as I earnestly pray) you may experience the same fate as the Templars, whose good fortune until now you have shared, heaping up vast treasures and excelling in a power that is almost feared by all. So may you likewise experience the same adverse fate as they. And if not the Pontiff himself, then other moderate Catholic kings and princes may take counsel among themselves to root out your most cruel sect, the most pestilential of all sects to the whole human race. Thus, with you disturbers and enemies of public peace removed from the midst, the most longed-for peace and charity of the Church and of the Christian commonwealth may return!

units.la: Namque vos Jesuitae, (repeto hoc) nisi resipiscitis, quod iterum opto;
units.tr: For you Jesuits (I repeat this), unless you repent, which I again wish for,

units.la: Vos estis,Deus est testis,Teterrima pestis.
units.tr: You are, God is witness, a most loathsome plague.

units.la: Quia omnis boni ordinis perturbatores.
units.tr: Because you are disturbers of all good order.

units.la: At tu Lector pie, vale in Domino, & ardenter precare, ut pacem largiatur pacificis; at dissidia volentes perdat. E nostro museo, 1. Mart. anno 1610.
units.tr: But you, pious reader, farewell in the Lord, and pray earnestly that he may grant peace to the peaceable, and destroy those who desire discord. From our study, 1 March, in the year 1610.

units.la: JOACHIMUS URSINUS, Anti-Jesuita.
units.tr: JOACHIM URSINUS, Anti-Jesuit.

units.la: ODE IONICA A MINORE, IN ÆQUIVOCATIONEM JESUITICAM, ET OMNIA SECTÆ illius InstitutA vitæ.
units.tr: IONIC ODE FROM THE MINOR, AGAINST JESUITICAL EQUIVOCATION, AND ALL THE INSTITUTED WAY OF LIFE OF THAT SECT.

units.la: NOvus ordo Monachorum, genitore Sathanâ Principe gentis malesuadæ Malè nati, quasi vis ultima Nervi genitalis Hecates ex coitu; Dein sub eodem Operosoq; magistro maleduṍti, Et iidem mage mortalibus altû sapientes.
units.tr: A new order of monks, with Satan as father, prince of the evil-minded race, badly born, as it were the ultimate force of the genital nerve of Hecate's coupling; then, under the same laborious and evil-hearted master, the same men, wiser than mortals in deep cunning.

units.la: Etiam nomine Jesu malè abusi, Erebi nocte coacti tacitâ umbrâ, Statui pessum eunti Latii consiliantes; Repererunt simulandi genus, olim Neq; Christo, neq; Paulo, neq; cuiquam Subeunti mala mortis, mala damni, manifestum.
units.tr: Also badly abusing the name of Jesus, driven by the night of Erebus in silent shade, they plotted the ruin of Latium as it went to its destruction. They discovered a kind of pretending, unknown of old to Christ, to Paul, or to anyone who suffers the evils of death and the evils of loss.

units.la: Fuit istis eadem forma loquendi Ut erat res, Ita, vel Non; neque in ore Magis ac in penetrali genita illa omnia cordis.
units.tr: These men had the same form of speech: as the thing is, so, yes or no. Nor were all those things born in their mouth any more than in their inmost heart.

units.la: Quia Iova est sine vano, jubet esse Similes nos, sine fuco, sine fraude; Neq; fingi, neq; pingi sua verba & nequa nostra.
units.tr: Because Jove is without deceit, he bids us be like him, without paint, without fraud. Our words should be neither feigned nor painted, neither his nor ours.

units.la: Repetantur licet exempla vetusta, Nihil almæ simile Urbis dabit ætas, Eadem quæ faciebant ꝑ psitebantur aperté; Nec honesta est ratio omnis minuendi Inimici sibi visa aut properata, Procul istæ procul artes, superarunt magis armis.
units.tr: Old examples may be repeated, but the age will give nothing like the nourishing City. The same things were done and openly punished. Nor is every method of diminishing an enemy honourable, whether seen or hurried. Far off are those arts, far off; they have prevailed rather by arms.

units.la: Fuerant hæc; sed ab occaso adeò, ajunt, Nova lux sole refulsit. Nebulones, Quasi Græci locuive Annibalis, scita refi- gunt Fidei veriloquæ; cujus ab ore Simul ac latere abscessimus, eheu. Quibus errat labyrinthis vaga quis vita periclis!
units.tr: These things were so; but from the west, they say, a new light has shone like the sun. Scoundrels, like Greeks or the men of Hannibal, resist the decrees of the Faith that speaks the truth. As soon as we have withdrawn from its mouth and side, alas, in what labyrinths does life wander, in what dangers!

units.la: Et in hæc sacra malum omen, mala fatâ, Et in urbes & in urbem velut undant Fluvii, agros simul omnes sine pausâ ra- pientes.
units.tr: Into these sacred things, an evil omen and evil fates, and into the cities and into the city they pour like rivers, snatching up all the fields without pause.

units.la: Alia veste, alio nomine, vultu, Mala pestis, seges iræ, tuba Martis, Variantur quasi Proteus, imitando facim omnem.
units.tr: In another garb, another name, another face, an evil plague, a crop of wrath, a trumpet of Mars, they change like Proteus, imitating every form.

units.la: Ut in aras penetrent ac ut in arcas Vel Iobi pietatem simulabunt; Sera nulla est satis auro, patet ædes animorum.
units.tr: So they penetrate to the altars and to the strongboxes, or they feign the piety of Job. No gold is ever enough for them, and the house of minds lies open.

units.la: Ubi victa est popularis priûs aura, Inhiant mox penetrali Dominantum, Ibi ovant tempora lauro obsidionis redimiti.
units.tr: Where the popular breeze has first been defeated, they soon gape at the inner sanctum of the lords; there they exult, their temples wreathed with the laurel of a siege.

units.la: Ita Leno insidiosus lucra captat;Ita pellex ad amores, ad avesque estAvis illix; ita noctis latro servat vafer umbras.
units.tr: So the treacherous pimp hunts for gain; so the mistress hunts for lovers, the bird-lure for birds; so the sly thief guards the shadows of night.

units.la: Tua res est, Tibi Rex Galle, Britanne,Tibi Germana cavendum melior pars,Velad exemplum aliorum misera morte cadetis,
units.tr: The matter concerns you: for you, King of France, Britain; for you, Germany, the better part must beware, or like the others you will fall to a wretched death,

units.la: Vel avitas dare sedes peregrinisAgitati solida vi, sine jure,Juga collo ingenuo dura ferociis miserandi.
units.tr: or give up your ancestral seats to strangers, shaken by brute force and without right, and yokes hard on free necks, pitiable to the fierce.

units.la: Bone Princeps ubicunque es, vigilabis,Sine fronte est genus infidum, adit astu,Licitum credit, agit, quod jubet insana libido.
units.tr: Good Prince, wherever you are, be watchful. The faithless race has no shame; it approaches with cunning, thinks whatever it does lawful, and does what its mad lust commands.

units.la: Aliquam semper habebant rationisSpeciem, cur tua nex non videaturNimis injusta; tyrannum patriae pernicie-emque
units.tr: They always had some appearance of reason why your killing should not seem too unjust, complaining that a tyrant was ruining the fatherland,

units.la: Querulantes; sine causa foret ulla,Papa solus fieri quod volet est fas,Tibi ademtum dabitur cui ille jubebit diadema.
units.tr: and without some cause there would be none. That the Pope alone may do whatever he wishes is lawful; the diadem will be taken from whomever he orders.

units.la: Sibi sumunt nova regnis dare jura,At in ipsos neque jus est neque poenaSceleratos, homicidas, probra saecli bene culti.
units.tr: They take to themselves the power to give new laws to kingdoms, yet against themselves there is neither right nor punishment for the criminals, the murderers, the disgrace of a well-cultivated age.

units.la: Modo totis satagunt viribus, irasOdiorumque perennes ferere aestus,Et acerbis populos funeribus vertere, Reges.
units.tr: Now they labour with all their strength, bearing the perpetual heat of hatreds and resentments, and they turn peoples and kings into bitter deaths.

units.la: Medio aufferre venenis, modò ferro &Sine justâ malè committere liteGladiantes, animos aut inimicos agitantes.
units.tr: They remove men by poison, now by iron, and without just cause they wickedly set gladiators against one another, stirring up spirits or enemies.

units.la: Reliquum nil faciunt denique pensi,Genus audax scelera in cuncta nefanda,Nisi cœlum, & polus, & Dis sibi cedat pater ipse.
units.tr: In the end they leave nothing unweighed: a bold race for every unspeakable crime, unless heaven, the pole, and the Father of the gods himself give way to them.

units.la: Orere ô lux, ubi acuto Deus ictuAdigat fulminis in viscera terræ,Vel in æquor, volitantes in Iberis simul omnes
units.tr: Arise, O light, where God with a sharp stroke of lightning drives into the bowels of the earth, or into the sea, all of them flying together in Spanish ships,

units.la: Ratibus, cum Duce; vel corpora fœtisCanibus projiciens, pestiferam auramAnimarum populante stygio ventilet igni.
units.tr: with their leader; or, throwing their bodies to the dogs, let him blow the pestilential air of souls with Stygian fire and lay waste.

units.la: Ibi tum Pax oleæ instar revirescet,Sua cives retinebunt habitacla,Sua Cleri sacra salva & sua Reges tabulata.
units.tr: Then Peace will green again like the olive; the citizens will keep their dwellings, the clergy their sacred things safe, and the kings their floors.

units.la: Ubi grex & gregis omnis scabiosiLœiola periit spes; Parasiti,Homicida, genus audax scelera in cuncta nefanda.
units.tr: Where the flock, and every scabby sheep of the flock, has perished, the hope is lost: parasites, murderers, a bold race for every unspeakable crime.

units.la: AD LECTOREM.
units.tr: TO THE READER.

units.la: ODen istam Ionicam, cùm ante- hac saltem tentandi generis, quo Horatius semel usus, causâ fecissem; postea incideram in Scaligerum, qui autumat, eo olim agitatos fuisse adulteros, meretrices, proditores, lenones, ebrios: gavisus equidem & gratulatus mihi fui, quòd ipsa Nemesis, ut auguror, τὸ πεῖτον mihi suggesserit. Nam hoc profecto genus Balatronum dicam an Latronum, omninò inter illud est connumerandum & tandum ad laqueos, si essent Archilochi aut saltem Archi.
units.tr: I had written this Ionic ode before, though only as an experiment in a kind of verse that Horace used once. Later I came across Scaliger, who claims that adulterers, prostitutes, traitors, pimps and drunkards were once lashed by such verse. I was glad of this and felt encouraged, since Nemesis herself, as I guess, suggested the very thing [τὸ πεῖτον] to me. For this kind of buffoon (should I call them buffoons or thieves?) must certainly be counted among those, and at last be brought to the noose, if they were Archilochuses, or at least Archilochus-like satirists.

units.la: Benedictus de Clarômonte.
units.tr: Benedictus de Clarômonte.

units.la: EPIGRAMMA ALIUS POETÆ AUSTRASII De Jesuitis.
units.tr: Another epigram of the Austrasian poet, On the Jesuits.

units.la: EST monachis, qui se Jesu sub nomine vendunt, Non Jesus, verum dúxq; caputq; Sathan. Nam mundi sectantur opes, sectantur honores, Et claras condunt, magnificásq; domos. Plebejas opplent phaleratu vocibus aures, Nec nisi Pontificum somnia vana crepant. Humanas leges, divinásq; jura prophanant, Nec scelus est, quod non clàm ve palámve patrent. Pro lubitu, contra vetitum, connubia conflant, Ac solvunt initam Numine teste fidem. Cæde magistratus perimunt, regésq; potentes, Quósq; sub Hispano non juvat esse jugo. Servit ad hoc ipsis pulvis nitratus, & enses, Quaq; ferunt celerem dira venena necem. Hac neq; sunt jussis Christi, degener ordo facit, Qua Jesuvita Christi nec, consona factis, Rectè igitur secta hæc Jesu contraria vita Dicta est, quòd Jesu non imitetur iter.
units.tr: There are monks who sell themselves under the name of Jesus, yet they are not Jesus but rather the leader and head of Satan. For they pursue the riches of the world, they pursue honours, and they build bright and magnificent houses. They fill the ears of the common folk with showy words, and they utter nothing but the empty dreams of the Popes. They profane human laws and divine rights, and there is no crime they do not commit openly or in secret. At their pleasure, and against what is forbidden, they contract marriages, and they dissolve a pledge once made with God as witness. They destroy magistrates by slaughter, and powerful kings, and anyone who does not care to live under the Spanish yoke. Nitrated powder serves this purpose, and swords, and the deadly poisons that bring swift death. A degenerate order does these things, and they are not commanded by Christ. The Jesuit is not one of Christ, since his deeds do not agree with Christ's commands. Rightly, therefore, this sect is called contrary to the life of Jesus, because it does not follow the way of Jesus.

units.la: De I. Libri parte, QUAE SOLIDAM IDOLOLATRICAE SANCTORUM INVOCATIONIS REFUTATIONEM complectitur.
units.tr: On the first part of the book, which contains a solid refutation of the idolatrous invocation of saints.

units.la: PRODIIT annis superioribus, & editione quidem illa reiterata, libellus, sub hoc titulo: Institutiones Christianae pietatis, seu parvus Catechismus Catholicorum, auctore Doctore Petro Canisio Societatis Jesu Theologo.
units.tr: Some years ago there appeared a little book, in a reprinted edition, under the title Institutiones Christianae pietatis, or parvus Catechismus Catholicorum, by Doctor Peter Canisius, theologian of the Society of Jesus.

units.la: Iste libellus PARVI CATECHISMI nomine, ad Majoris Jesuiticae Catecheseos differentiam indigitatur, quae alicubi sine autoris mentione edita est, alicubi ejusdem Petri Canisii nomen praefixum habet, & Summa doctrinae Christianae inscripta, privilegium Ferdinandi Regis tum Romanorum, procemii loco praemissum continet.
units.tr: This little book is called the SMALL CATECHISM, to distinguish it from the Greater Jesuit Catechesis. The latter is published in some places without any mention of its author, and in others bears the name of the same Peter Canisius, is entitled Summa doctrinae Christianae, and has by way of preface a privilege of Ferdinand, then King of the Romans.

units.la: In illo privilegio hoc in genere dicitur: Ad hujusmodi Catholicum opus conscribendum non dubia fidei & doctrinae viros delectos: conscriptum{?} eorum, quos non solum sacrosanctae Theologiae scientia, verum etiam vitae innocentia & integritate perspicuos esse constiterit, judicio & censura iura subjectum fuisse. Mandatur etiam ibidem, iis, qui nomine & loco Regis, juris & justitia administrationem in provinciis Austriae inferioris, & Goritiae Comitatu exercent, ac in magistratu constituti sunt, ut hunc Catechismum solum, nullumq; alium per Ludimagistros, Praeceptores ac Paedagogos, pueris in scholis publice aut privatim proponi, pralegi, edisci endumque tradi magnopere curent, atq; omnino efficiant.
units.tr: In that privilege the following is said in general terms: For writing this kind of Catholic work, men were chosen who are not doubtful in faith and doctrine, and whose writings, since they are known to be conspicuous not only for their knowledge of most sacred theology but also for the innocence and integrity of their lives, have been made subject to judgment and censure. It is also commanded there: To those who, in the name and place of the King, exercise the administration of law and justice in the provinces of Lower Austria and the county of Gorizia, and who hold office in the magistracy, that they diligently see to it and altogether bring about that this Catechism alone, and no other, be proposed to boys in the schools, publicly or privately, by schoolmasters, tutors and pedagogues, be read aloud to them, learned by heart, and handed down to them.

units.la: In iis libellis horribilia commenta Papistica a Jesuitis mira Sophistica & fuco splendido pinguntur, atq; opera datur maxima, ut teneris tenerae adolescentiae animis venenum istud exitiale, cum ipso pene materno lacte, probe instilletur.
units.tr: In these little books the horrible Papist fictions are painted by the Jesuits with wondrous sophistries and a splendid veneer, and the greatest effort is made that this deadly poison be thoroughly instilled into the tender minds of tender youth, almost with the mother's milk itself.

units.la: Inter alia minus ferendum est, quod tanta Evangelii luce affulgente, Idololatricam & in Deum blasphemam Sanctorum invocationem audacter tueri nō dubitent. Quo vel uno documento satis superq; probant, quid iis praeceptoribus scientiae sit, quid conscientiae.
units.tr: Among other things, it is less tolerable that, with the light of the Gospel shining so brightly, they do not hesitate to boldly defend the idolatrous invocation of saints, which is blasphemous against God. By this one proof alone they show well enough and more than enough what learning and what conscience these teachers have.

units.la: Ut autem ambo isti Catechismi Jesuitici per quaestiones conscripti sunt: sic nos etiam (ut omnia sint clariora magisque perspicua) quaestionib. distinctis notationes praecipuorum errorum, & horum solidam ex verbo divino refutationem complectemur.
units.tr: Just as both of these Jesuit catechisms are composed in questions, so we too (so that everything may be clearer and more perspicuous) will set out, under distinct questions, notes on the principal errors and their solid refutation from the divine Word.

units.la: Partis hujus primæ, de Idololatrica Invocatione pontificia, duo membra cõstituemus. Horum unum erit, Enarratio præcepti primi & secundi, inq; primis de cultu & invocatione Sanctorum, ac de statuis & imaginibus : alterum, de salutatione Angelica, quam velut precationem Jesuitæ affluunt Orationi dominicæ.
units.tr: We will set up two parts of this first section, on the idolatrous papal invocation. One of these will be an explanation of the first and second commandments, and above all of the worship and invocation of saints, and of statues and images; the other will be on the Angelic salutation, which the Jesuits attach to the Lord's Prayer as if it were a prayer of its own.

units.la: Ex his pius lector nullo negotio cognoscere poterit, quàm graviter ab adversariis in primum Christianæ Religionis atq; etiam tertium caput, Decalogum inquam & Dominicam precationem, impingatur.
units.tr: From these the pious reader will be able to recognize without any difficulty how gravely the adversaries assail the first head of the Christian religion, and also the third, namely the Decalogue and the Lord's Prayer.

units.la: De I. membro:
units.tr: On the first member:

units.la: DE ENARRATIONE PRÆCEPTI PRIMI ET SECUNDI IN CATECHISMIS JESUITICIS, inprimisq; de Cultu & Invocatione Sanctorum, ac de Statuis & Imaginibus.
units.tr: On the Explanation of the First and Second Precepts in the Jesuit Catechisms, especially on the Worship and Invocation of the Saints, and on Statues and Images.

units.la: Quid in enarratione primi, quod sie nominant, præcepti, tradunt Catechismi Jesuitici?
units.tr: What do the Jesuit catechisms teach in explaining what they call the first precept?

units.la: Primò parvus Catechismus Jesuiticus hoc modo primum præceptum explicat:Prohibet ac damnat idololatriam seu cultum falsorum Deorum, artem magicā vel divinatoriam, observationes superstitiosas, omnem denique cultum impium. E diverso autem requirit, ut unum Deum Opt. Max. credamus, colamus & invocemus.
units.tr: First, the Small Jesuit Catechism explains the first precept in this way: It forbids and condemns idolatry, or the worship of false gods, the magical or divinatory art, superstitious observances, and, in short, every impious worship. On the other hand, it requires that we believe in, worship and invoke the one God, the best and greatest.

units.la: Atque hæc quidem recte ac vere dicuntur, sic quidem, ut inde universa idololatria & superstitio, quam plurimis in rebus exercet Papistæ, evidenter refelli ac refutari possint. Suntq; similia, quæ in Catechesi Austriaca dicuntur, sub hac quæstione:
units.tr: These things are indeed rightly and truly said, and in such a way that all the idolatry and superstition which the Papists practise in very many matters can be plainly confuted and refuted by them. Similar things are said in the Austrian Catechism, under this question:

units.la: Quid complectitur in se primum Præceptum?
units.tr: What does the first Precept comprehend?

units.la: Prohibet ac damnat idololatriam, observationes superstitiosas, ipsum etiam artis magicæ & divinatoriæ. Rursus docet atq; exigit, ut nullam prorsus
units.tr: It forbids and condemns idolatry and superstitious observances, and the magical and divinatory art itself. Again, it teaches and requires that we should in no way

units.la: Primi præcepti Jesuiticæ enarratio. prorsus creaturam, quantumvis excellentem, pro Deo habeamus: solum autem unum, verum, aeternum, immensumq; Deum credamus & confiteamur. Huic uni tribuatur summus & singularis ille cultus, quem Graeci λατρείαν appellant. Hoc fit, ut super omnia colamus, invocemus, adoremus summum illud bonum, optimum, maximum, creatorem, redemptorem, salvatorem, unum & immortalem Deum, qui est super omnes, & per omnia, & in omnibus nobis.
units.tr: The Jesuit explanation of the first precept. In no way hold any creature, however excellent, to be God; but believe and confess that God alone is one, true, eternal, immeasurable. To this one alone let that supreme and singular worship be given, which the Greeks call latreia. This is done so that we worship, invoke and adore above all things that supreme good, best and greatest, the creator, redeemer, saviour, the one and immortal God, who is above all, and through all, and in all of us.

units.la: Haec etiam recte dicuntur sic: etsi, ut post- ea monebimus, latebrae quaeruntur in voce λατρείας, quam Jesuitae distinguunt à δουλείας & ὑπερδουλείας.
units.tr: These things too are rightly said in this way; yet, as we will warn afterwards, there is a hidden trick in the word latreia [λατρείας], which the Jesuits distinguish from douleia [δουλείας] and hyperdouleia [ὑπερδουλείας].

units.la: Mox vero quaestio haec de Sanctorum cultu & invocatione sequitur, repugnans his, quae in explicatione superioris quaestionis à Jesuitis ipsis sunt propositae. Sic enim parvus Catechismus:
units.tr: But soon this question about the worship and invocation of the saints follows, which contradicts what the Jesuits themselves have proposed in the explanation of the earlier question. For the Small Catechism says:

units.la: Licetne Sanctos colere & invocare?
units.tr: Is it lawful to worship and invoke the saints?

units.la: Licet: non ad eum quidem modum, quo jubemur Deum colere, & invocare, tanquam creatorem, & redemptorem, & largitorem bonorum omnium: At longe inferiori gradu, nimirum veluti dilectissimos Dei amicos, nostrosque apud ipsum intercessores, & patronos.
units.tr: It is lawful, not indeed in that manner in which we are commanded to worship and invoke God, as creator, redeemer and giver of all good things; but in a far lower degree, namely as the most beloved friends of God, and our intercessors and patrons with him.

units.la: Multo autem prolixius & astutius ista inculcat Catechesis Austriaca: quae ut justae refutationis materiam nobis praebeant, verbotenus recitanda sunt. Sic igitur Catechesis illa:
units.tr: The Austrian Catechism inculcates these things much more lengthily and craftily; and so that they may give us matter for a just refutation, they must be quoted word for word. The Catechism says this:

units.la: Quomodo præter Deum Sanctos colimus & invocamus?
units.tr: In what way do we worship and invoke the saints besides God?

units.la: Respondet Augustinus (inquit,) Populus Christianus memorias martyrum religiosa solennitate concelebrat, & ad excitandam imitationem, & ut meritis eorum consocietur, atq; orationibus adjuvetur. Quod autem hic de martyribus dicitur, ad omnes etiam Sanctos cū Christo regnantes spectat: non illos quidem, uti Deos Ethnicorum more colendos, neq; perinde ac Deum sanctum sanctorum: sed longè inferiore modo & gradu, utpote velut amicos, filios, haeredesq; Dei, & coharedes Christi lectissimos atque beatissimos, venerandos: qui praterea nostra salutis eò studeant, faventq; impensius, quò sunt in omni charitate, in omni virtute ac coelesti gloria perfectiores, quam hic esse in carne potuissent.
units.tr: Augustine answers (it says): The Christian people celebrate the memories of the martyrs with religious solemnity, both to stir up imitation and so that they may be joined to their merits and aided by their prayers. What is said here of the martyrs, however, applies also to all the saints reigning with Christ: not indeed that they are to be worshipped as the gods of the heathen, nor in the same way as God, the holy of holies; but in a far lower manner and degree, as friends, sons, heirs of God and most choice and most blessed co-heirs of Christ, to be venerated; who moreover strive all the more for our salvation and favour us the more eagerly, the more perfect they are in all charity, in all virtue and heavenly glory, than they could have been while in the flesh.
