units.la: Sicuti ergo infra Deum, illos plus quam ullos in terra mortales rectè amamus, ita eosdem tali tantáq; dignitate auctos honoramus etiam, atq; pro Christiana pietate invocamus. hac tamen cautione semper addita, ut summus honor, summusq; cultus, quem λατρείαν esse diximus, summo Deo & Mediatori Christo debitus, integrè conservetur.
units.tr: Therefore, just as below God we rightly love those mortals more than any others on earth, so we also honour and, according to Christian piety, invoke those who have been raised to such and so great a dignity. Yet with this caution always added, that the highest honour and highest worship, which we have said is latreia, due to the highest God and to Christ the Mediator, be kept whole and entire.

units.la: Quod autem hunc in modum Sanctos invocamus: adeò Christi Salvatoris & Domini nostri gloriam gloriam non obscurat, ut etiam magis ac magis illustret, amplificet, augeatque. Hic enim eximia Christi mediatoris virtus splendescit ac gloria, quod is non in se tantum, sed in Sanctis etiam suis est, apparetque potens, gloriosus, mirabilis: quod eosdem honorat ipse, nimisque honorari vult in caelo & in terra: quod per hos itidem & propter hos multa largitur, & parcit saepe immerentibus, ut in Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, David, Jeremia cernimus, qui etiam defuncti vivis profuisse leguntur.
units.tr: Moreover, that we invoke the saints in this manner does not so obscure the glory of Christ our Saviour and Lord, but rather makes it more and more illustrious, enlarged and increased. For the outstanding virtue of Christ the Mediator shines forth and is glorious in this, that he is present not only in himself but also in his saints, and appears powerful, glorious and wonderful; in that he himself honours them, and wishes to be greatly honoured in heaven and on earth; in that through them and for their sake he bestows many gifts and often spares the undeserving, as we see in Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, David and Jeremiah, who are also read to have helped the living after their death.

units.la: Unde Patres, cum de Sanctis loquuntur, suffragatores eos & intercessores, patronosque nostros frequenter appellant. Nec immerito sane, quod Sanctorum suffragia, cum humiliter & pie in Christi nomine implorantur, experientia teste, multis opitulentur. Haec fuit jam olim Ecclesia orthodoxa, sicut & nunc est, erga Sanctos constans pietas, hanc doctrinam velut per manus ad nos transmissam, & sacris itidem Synodis patrum concordibus sententiis & indubitatis exemplis confirmatam, retinent Catholici: Obstrepant licet Vigilantiani jam olim condemnati. Hactenus Catechesis Austriaca.
units.tr: Hence the Fathers, when they speak of the saints, often call them our intercessors, advocates and patrons. And not undeservedly, for the saints' intercession, when it is humbly and piously implored in the name of Christ, is, as experience bears witness, of help to many. This has been the steadfast piety of the orthodox Church towards the saints from of old, as it is now; the Catholics retain this doctrine as if handed down to us by hand, and confirmed by the holy synods of the Fathers in their agreeing opinions and undoubted examples; let the Vigilantians, long since condemned, cry out against it as they may. Thus far the Austrian Catechism.

units.la: Estne tantum momentii in hac disputatione (in qua agitur de cultu & invocatione Sanctorum, inferiori gradu, quam Deus coelestis & invocandus sit) ut hac de causa discedendum fuerit a Romana Ecclesia?
units.tr: Is there so much weight in this dispute (in which it is a question of the worship and invocation of the saints, in a lower degree than the heavenly God is to be worshipped and invoked) that for this reason one ought to have departed from the Roman Church?

units.la: DE IDOLOLATRICA
units.tr: On Idolatrous Invocation

units.la: Una res est omnium maxima, Invocatio Dei: quæ proprie discernit Ecclesiam Dei a cæteris gentibus. Multi sunt enim & fuerunt ignari Dei, qui tamen aliis civilibus virtutibus omnibus præditi fuerunt; ut Aristides, Scipio, Pomponius Atticus: sed hæc virtus eis defuit. Invocatio Dei, Necesse est igitur in Ecclesia doctrinam de Invocatione purissimam extare. Deinde, vera invocatio præcipuum præsidiū est piarum mentiū, in tantis ærumnis vitæ communis; ut dicitur a Salomone: Arx firmissima est nomen Domini; justus ad hanc confugiens, liberabitur. Præterea, cultus Dei præcipuus est invocatio, quæ fit in spiritu & veritate, juxta dictū: Invoca me in die tribulationis. Non igitur exi-stimandum est, de re levi dimicari, cùm de invocatione disceritur. Ad quam corrumpendam inde ab initio generis humani Diabolus variis modis semina errorum spargit, & semper sparget. Itaque nos vigilantiores esse, & majore cura retinere oportet modum invocationis, propositum in verbo Dei: non miscere alios modos, pugnantes cum voce divina, aut qui nullo exemplo probato in Scripturis confirmati sunt.
units.tr: The invocation of God is the greatest matter of all, for it especially distinguishes the Church of God from the other nations. Many people have been, and still are, ignorant of God yet endowed with all the civic virtues, such as Aristides, Scipio and Pomponius Atticus; but this virtue was lacking in them. It is therefore necessary that the purest doctrine of invocation be found in the Church. Then, true invocation is the chief safeguard of devout minds amid the great hardships of common life, as Solomon says: "The name of the Lord is a most firm stronghold; the righteous man who flees to it shall be set free." Moreover, the chief worship of God is invocation, which is made in spirit and in truth, according to the saying: "Call upon me in the day of trouble." It should not be thought, therefore, that we are contending over a trivial matter when we dispute about invocation. The devil has sown the seeds of error to corrupt it in various ways from the beginning of the human race, and he always will. Therefore we ought to be more watchful and to keep with greater care the manner of invocation set out in the Word of God, and not to mix in other modes that conflict with the divine voice or that are confirmed by no approved example in the Scriptures.

units.la: Multi negligunt invocationem: quia non cogitant, nullam virtutem majorem, nullam consolationem efficaciorem, nullum cultum Deo gratiorem esse, quàm veram invocatiocationem. Alii non discernunt invocatione suam ab Ethnica, ac ne cogitant quidem, quid alloquantur; de quib inquit Dominus Joh.4. Vos adoratis, quod nescitis. Vult autem eodem in loco Dominus Ecclesiam cogitare, quid alloquatur, inquiens: Nos adoramus, quod scimus. Multi non cogitant, an & quare exaudiantur. Recitant precationes, & dubitant tamen; cum scriptum sit: Postulet in fide, nihil dubitans. Jacob. 1. De his materiis alibi dicitur copiosius; sed breviter hic attingenda ista fuerunt, ut sciamus, hoc loco jure & merito taxari hanc corruptelam Ethnicam, quod defenditur consuetudo alloquentium homines, qui ex hac vita discesserunt; a quibus, ut Jesuitae volunt, intercessio: ut alii Pontificii, etiam auxilium petendum sit.
units.tr: Many neglect invocation, because they do not consider that no virtue is greater, no consolation more effective, and no worship more pleasing to God than true invocation. Others do not distinguish their invocation from the heathen one, and do not even consider whom they address; of these the Lord says in John 4: "You worship what you do not know." Moreover, in the same place the Lord wishes the Church to consider whom it addresses, saying: "We worship what we know." Many do not consider whether and why they are heard. They recite prayers and yet doubt, although it is written: "Let him ask in faith, nothing doubting." James 1. These matters are treated more fully elsewhere, but they have been touched on briefly here so that we may know that this heathen corruption is rightly and justly censured in this place, the custom being defended of addressing men who have departed from this life; to whom, as the Jesuits wish, intercession, and, as other Papists also say, help is to be sought.

units.la: Talis invocatio aberrat a modo invocationis sancito a Christo: Quicquid petieritis in nomine meo, dabit vobis. Transfert gloriam soli Deo debitam ad creaturas, quibus efficaciam divinam tribuit. Relinquit mentes in dubitatione: cum hic cultus nusquam comprobatus sit verbo Dei. Deniq; abduxit oculos ab unico mediatore Christo, & labefactat fidem, id est, fiduciam hujus mediatoris, quae in invocatione lucere potissimum debet. Nec dubium est, superstitiosa illius invocationis sanctorum comites esse,
units.tr: Such invocation departs from the manner of invocation enjoined by Christ: "Whatever you ask in my name, he will give you." It transfers to creatures the glory due to God alone, to whom it attributes divine efficacy. It leaves minds in doubt, since this worship has nowhere been approved by the Word of God. Finally, it draws the eyes away from the one Mediator, Christ, and weakens faith, that is, trust in this Mediator, which ought above all to shine forth in invocation. Nor is there any doubt that blindness of mind and the other punishments, by which God avenges contempt of himself, accompany this superstitious invocation of the saints,

units.la: Ioan. 14. cæcitatem animorum, & alias pœnas, quibus contemptum sui Deus ulciscitur.
units.tr: John 14.

units.la: Quæ sunt argumenta præcipua, quibus refutanda est invocatio Sanctorum?
units.tr: What are the principal arguments by which the invocation of the saints is refuted?

units.la: Primum argumentum est: Creaturis tribuere omnipotentiam, est impietas. Nam omnipotentia tantum tribuenda est æterno Patri, & Filio ejus Domino nostro Jesu Christo, & Spiritui sancto.
units.tr: The first argument is this: To ascribe omnipotence to creatures is impiety. For omnipotence is to be ascribed to the eternal Father, to his Son our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the Holy Spirit alone.

units.la: Invocatio creaturæ, quæ est extra hanc vitæ consuetudinem, tribuit ei omnipotentiam: quia tribuit ei, quod intueatur omnium corda, & discernat gemitus veros à simulatis.
units.tr: The invocation of a creature who is outside the customs of this life ascribes omnipotence to him, because it ascribes to him the power to see the hearts of all and to discern true groans from feigned ones.

units.la: Quare nequaquam instituenda est invocatio, vel ad angelos, vel ad sanctos, qui ex hac vita discesserunt, neque ut auxiliatores, neque ut intercessores.
units.tr: Therefore invocation must in no way be instituted, whether to angels or to saints who have departed this life, neither as helpers nor as intercessors.

units.la: Secundum argumentum est: Nulli creaturæ licet extra & præter verbum Dei instituere cultum Deo placentem; ut Christus inquit ex Isaia: Frustra colunt me mandatis hominum. Nullum est autem mandatum in verbo Dei, quod doceat, velle Deum coli invocatione hominum, qui non cernuntur oculis.
units.tr: The second argument is this: It is not lawful for any creature to institute, outside and beside the Word of God, a worship pleasing to God; as Christ says from Isaiah: "They worship me in vain, teaching the commandments of men." There is, however, no commandment in the Word of God teaching that God wishes to be worshipped by the invocation of men who are not seen by the eyes.

units.la: Non est igitur hic cultus invocationis Sanctorum tolerandus in Ecclesia.
units.tr: Therefore this worship of invoking the saints is not to be tolerated in the Church.

units.la: Tertium argumentum est: Irrita est invocatio
units.tr: The third argument is this: Invocation without faith is vain

units.la: catio sine fide; ut dicitur: Quomodo invocabunt, si non credunt?
units.tr: without faith; as it is said: "How shall they call upon him, if they do not believe?"

units.la: Invocatio hominum beatorum in coelo fit sine fide: Quia nusquam extat testimonium in verbo Dei de tali invocatione, quòd sit efficax.
units.tr: The invocation of blessed men in heaven is made without faith, because nowhere in the Word of God is there any testimony that such invocation is effective.

units.la: Est igitur irrita invocatio, hoc modo accedere ad Sanctum aliquem mortuum: Invoco te, sed dubito, utrùm me audias? an intercessio tua mihi prosit? an mihi opem feras?
units.tr: Invocation is therefore vain when one approaches some dead saint in this way: "I invoke you, but I doubt whether you hear me? Whether your intercession will profit me? Whether you will bring me help?"

units.la: Quartum argumentum. Illustre testimonium est divinitatis Messiae, quòd Prophetae jubent eum invocari, sive cernatur oculis, sive non cernatur: & hac proprietate discernitur Messias à caeteris doctoribus missis ad Ecclesiam.
units.tr: The fourth argument. It is a distinguished testimony to the divinity of the Messiah that the prophets command him to be invoked, whether or not he is seen by the eyes; and by this property the Messiah is distinguished from the other teachers sent to the Church.

units.la: At si transferatur invocatio ad homines sanctos, obscuratur & labefactatur hoc gravissimum testimonium.
units.tr: But if invocation is transferred to holy men, this most weighty testimony is obscured and weakened.

units.la: Quamobrem consuetudo invocandi alios homines improbanda est.
units.tr: Wherefore the custom of invoking other men is to be condemned.

units.la: Quintum argumentum. Expressè scriptum est 1. Tim. 2. Unus est mediator Dei & hominum, homo Christus Jesus. Hunc in omni invocatione intueri nos oportet: & doctrinam Evangelii de eo nosse; Quòd nemo accedere ad Deum possit, nisi fiducia hujus mediatoris, qui simul interpellat pro nobis: ut ipse inquit, Joh. 14. Nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi
units.tr: The fifth argument. It is expressly written in 1 Timothy 2: "There is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus." In every invocation we ought to look to him, and to know the doctrine of the Gospel concerning him: that no one can come to God except by trust in this Mediator, who at the same time intercedes for us; as he himself says in John 14: "No one comes to the Father except

units.la: Rom. 10. nisi per Filium, & jubet ipse nos ad se confugere, inquiens Matth. 11. Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis, &c.
units.tr: Rom. 10. except through the Son;" and he himself bids us to flee to him, saying in Matthew 11: "Come to me, all you who labour," etc.

units.la: Hanc doctrinam de Mediatore obscurari & corrumpi manifestum est, cum confugiunt homines ad alios mediatores vel intercessores.
units.tr: It is plain that this doctrine concerning the Mediator is obscured and corrupted when men flee to other mediators or intercessors.

units.la: Sextum argumentum est. In Ecclesia primorum patrum, Abrahæ, Isaac, Jacob, Prophetarum, Apostolorum, non fuit consuetudo invocandi homines, qui non cernuntur oculis. Nusquam enim in sacris literis fit compellatio talis: Exaudi me Abraham, vel Exaudi me Deus propter Abraham. Imo diserte clamat Esaias cap. 64. Tu es pater noster, & Abraham nescivit nos, & Israel ignoravit nos. Tu Domine, Pater noster, redemptor noster, à seculo nomen tuum. Fit igitur in sacris literis compellatio ad verum Deum, qui se patefecit misso filio. Et statuitur hoc fundamentum precu, Fiducia officii ac beneficiorum Christi, propter quem jubemur à Deo petere, ut recipiat, exaudiat & salvet nos propter filium, ut Daniel cap. 9. orat: Exaudi nos propter Dominum. Saepe etiam conjungitur expressa compellatio ad patrem & filium simul. 2. ad Thessal. 2. Ipse Dominus noster Jesus Christus, & Deus & Pater noster, qui dilexit nos, & dedit consolationem aeternam, & spem bonam in gratia, confirmet vos in omni opere & sermone bono. Et Gen. 48. nominat Jacob Deum & Mediatorem filium, cùm ait: Deus, coram quo ambulaverunt Patres mei, & Angelus, qui eripuit me de cunctis malis (id est, promissus Salvator) benedicat pueris istis. Et quia cum Patre & Filio Spiritum sanctum quoq; constat Deum esse, hunc etiam recte compellamus in invocatione.
units.tr: The sixth argument is this. In the Church of the first fathers, of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, the prophets and the apostles, there was no custom of invoking men who are not seen by the eyes. For nowhere in the sacred writings is there any such address as: "Hear me, Abraham," or "Hear me, God, for the sake of Abraham." Indeed Isaiah clearly cries out in chapter 64: "You are our Father, for Abraham does not know us, and Israel is ignorant of us. You, Lord, are our Father, our Redeemer; your name is from everlasting." Thus in the sacred writings the address is made to the true God, who revealed himself by sending his Son. And this foundation of prayer is laid down: trust in the office and benefits of Christ, on account of whom we are commanded to ask God to receive, hear and save us for the sake of the Son, as Daniel prays in chapter 9: "Hear us for the Lord's sake." Often, too, an explicit address to the Father and the Son together is joined: 2 Thessalonians 2: "Our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace, comfort your hearts and establish you in every good work and word." And in Genesis 48 Jacob names God and the Mediator Son together, when he says: "God, before whom my fathers walked, and the Angel who has redeemed me from all evils (that is, the promised Saviour), bless these boys." And since it is agreed that with the Father and the Son the Holy Spirit is also God, we rightly address him in invocation as well.

units.la: Quid respondes vero ad ea, quæ pro tuenda invocatione Sanctorum, paulo ante recitata sunt ex utraq; Catechesi Jesuitica?
units.tr: But what do you answer to those arguments, cited a little while ago from both Jesuit catechisms, in defence of the invocation of the saints?

units.la: Primùm contradictio est manifesta, cùm in parvo Catechismo dicitur: Primum præceptum requirit, ut unum Deum Optimum Maximum credamus, colamus & invocemus. Et cùm mox additur: Licet etiam Sanctos colere & invocare.
units.tr: First, there is a plain contradiction, since in the Small Catechism it is said: The first commandment requires that we believe in, worship and invoke one God, the best and greatest. And soon after it is added: It is also lawful to worship and invoke the saints.

units.la: Si enim unus Deus est invocandus, qui est optimus maximus: Quomodo Sanctos invocare licebit, qui non sunt Deus?
units.tr: For if the one God who is best and greatest is to be invoked, how will it be lawful to invoke saints, who are not God?

units.la: Similis est contradictio in Catechesi Austriaca, cùm dicitur: Primum præceptum exigit, ut solum, unum, verum, æternum, immensumq; Deum credamus & confiteamur. Postea vero cùm mox nova additur quæstio: Quomodo PRÆTER Deum Sanctos colimus & invocamus? Si solus, unus, verus, æternus, & immensus Deus invocandus est: Cur de modo do quaeritur, quo praeter Deum Sancti sunt invocandi? Cum immotum ac aeternum decretum sit primi praecepti: Non habebis Deos alienos praeter me.
units.tr: The contradiction is similar in the Austrian Catechism, where it is said: The first commandment requires that we believe in and confess the one, only, true, eternal and immeasurable God. But afterwards, when a new question is soon added: How do we worship and invoke the saints BESIDE God? If the sole, one, true, eternal and immeasurable God is to be invoked, why is it asked in what manner saints are to be invoked beside God? Since the decree of the first commandment is fixed and eternal: "You shall have no other gods before me."

units.la: Deinde argumenta, quae a Iesuitis afferuntur pro stabilienda Sanctorum invocatione, vere sunt funiculi contexti ex arena; ut de haereticorum argumentis Irenaeus dicere solebat. De quo ordine deinceps videbimus.
units.tr: Next, the arguments the Jesuits bring forward to establish the invocation of the saints are truly ropes woven from sand, as Irenaeus used to say of the arguments of the heretics. We shall see in what follows how this holds.

units.la: Estne admittenda haec distinctio, quae ponitur in parvo Catechismo?
units.tr: Is this distinction, which is laid down in the Small Catechism, to be admitted?

units.la: Iubemur Deum colere & invocare, tanquam largitorem bonorum omnium. At Sanctos invocamus longe inferiori gradu, nimirum ut nostros apud Deum intercessores & patronos.
units.tr: We are bidden to worship and invoke God as the giver of all good things. But we invoke the saints in a far lower degree, namely as our intercessors and patrons with God.

units.la: Resp. Mera haec sophistica est, quod fingunt Iesuitae, licere, ut colantur & invocentur Sancti: sed non ad eum modum, quo iubemur Deum colere & invocare.
units.tr: Answer: This is mere sophistry, which the Jesuits invent: that the saints may be worshipped and invoked, but not in the same manner in which we are bidden to worship and invoke God.

units.la: Nam si simpliciter atque in universum Scriptura soli Deo assignat invocationem (utpote cui soli atque uni congruit omnipotentia, ut iudicare motus cordium, & exaudire preces possit) quis docuit Iesuitas facere modos diversos cultus & invocationis religiosae? Quis item docuit eos, ad Sanctos, qui ex hac vita discesserunt, dirigere precationem? cum nequaquam sint scrutatores cordium neque preces nostras audire atque percipere possint.
units.tr: For if Scripture assigns invocation simply and universally to God alone (since omnipotence belongs to him alone and to no other, so that he can judge the motions of hearts and hear prayers), who taught the Jesuits to make different modes of worship and of religious invocation? Who likewise taught them to direct prayer to the saints who have departed this life, since they are by no means searchers of hearts, nor can they hear and perceive our prayers?

units.la: Deinde, cur Sanctos mortuos volunt, ut intercessores & patronos nostros, invocari? cum non sint constituti à Deo mediatores, & solus Christus in sua pro nobis deprecatione applicare nobis merita sua possit?
units.tr: Again, why do they want the dead saints to be invoked as our intercessors and patrons, since they have not been appointed by God as mediators, and since Christ alone can apply his merits to us by his intercession on our behalf?

units.la: Postremò, protestatio est contraria facto, cum negant Iesuitæ, Sanctos à Pontificiis invocari, ut largitores bonorum: cum in medio sint, atque inter manus & oculos versentur, quæ in Ecclesia Romana, & ante hæc facta sunt, & adhuc quotidie fiunt. Intueatur enim quis formas precum, quæ publica authoritate in communi praxi Romanæ Ecclesiæ usitatæ fuerunt, atque etiamnum sunt. An non sonorâ voce clamant illæ: Beneficia omnia, quibus indigemus, Beatis in cœlo collata esse à Deo, ut ipsi implorati dent, largiantur & distribuant nobis, quæcunque ad gratiam in hac vita, & ad gloriam in futura vita pertinent, quæque ad externa quoque & temporalia beneficia spectant?
units.tr: Lastly, their profession is contrary to their practice. The Jesuits deny that the saints are invoked by the Papists as givers of good things, yet these things are before our eyes and in our hands, both in the Roman Church and in what has been done before and is still done every day. For let anyone look at the forms of prayer which, by public authority, have been and still are in common use in the practice of the Roman Church. Do they not cry out with a loud voice: That all the blessings we need have been bestowed by God upon the blessed in heaven, so that they, when implored, may give, grant and distribute to us whatever pertains to grace in this life and to glory in the life to come, and whatever also pertains to external and temporal blessings?

units.la: An verò etiam ignotum est, quòd diserte invocant Pontificii Sanctos, ut donatores & largitores beneficiorum spiritualium & corporalium, & ut auxiliatores, praservatores, custodes & liberatores in periculis & malis, tam spiritualibus, quàm corporalibus? Ipsos denique Sanctos expresse nominant refugium, præsidium, tutelam, vitam, & salutem nostram: in quorum gratia, miseriæ cordia, ope, auxilio, fiducia & spes nostra collocata.
units.tr: Or is it really unknown that the Papists expressly invoke the saints as donors and givers of spiritual and bodily benefits, and as helpers, preservers, guardians and deliverers in dangers and evils, both spiritual and bodily? Indeed they expressly name the saints themselves our refuge, protection, defence, life and salvation: in whose grace, mercy, help, aid, trust and hope our hope is placed.

units.la: catá catafit. Haec negare fuisse in usu Ecclesiae Romanae hactenus, atque etiamnum esse, quid aliud est, quàm si negare quis velit, denique nostram fuisse in Ægypto? cùm per totum triduum tantae fuerunt tenebrae, ut hominum nemo hominem agnosceret alterum.
units.tr: To deny that these things have hitherto been in use in the Roman Church, and still are, is nothing other than to deny, in effect, that there was ever darkness in Egypt, when for three whole days there was such darkness that no one could recognise another.

units.la: Quibus argumentis utitur Catechismi Jesuitici, ad Sanctorum invocationem stabiliendam?
units.tr: What arguments do the Jesuits' catechisms use to establish the invocation of the saints?

units.la: I. Cùm illud demum liceat, quod jure licet, ostendendum Jesuitis erat, ubi Scriptura hoc licere doceat, ut Sancti invocentur. At nullum plane testimonium ex sacris literis allegant in Catechismis suis, quo certò probent atque confirment, Sanctos, qui ex hac vita discesserunt, invocandos esse. Sciunt enim, nullam in tota sacra scriptura sententiam exstare, quae Sanctorum invocationem doceat: nullum mandatum in sacris literis legi, quod praecipiat Sanctis mortuis exhibere preces: nullam praeterea promissionem à Deo traditam esse, quòd invocatio Sanctorum Deo sit grata & efficax: nullum etiam exemplum probatum in Scriptura recitari, quòd Sancti mortui sint invocati à fidelibus: deniq; nullam comminationem, neq; exemplum poenae in sacris literis reperiri contra illos, qui non invocant Sanctos mortuos. Haec cum Jesuitae nullo apice ex Scriptura canonica demonstrare
units.tr: I. It was for the Jesuits to show, first of all, where Scripture teaches that it is lawful to invoke the saints, since only what is lawful by right is permitted. Yet in their catechisms they allege not a single clear testimony from the sacred writings by which they might certainly prove and confirm that the saints who have departed this life are to be invoked. For they know that there is no sentence in the whole of Holy Scripture that teaches the invocation of the saints; that no command is read in the sacred writings that bids us offer prayers to dead saints; that no promise has been given by God that the invocation of the saints is pleasing and effective to him; that no approved example is recounted in Scripture of dead saints being invoked by the faithful; and finally that no threat, nor any example of punishment, is found in the sacred writings against those who do not invoke the dead saints. Since the Jesuits cannot demonstrate these things from canonical Scripture with the least stroke of a pen,

units.la: strárē ftrare possint:& aut mutilata, autambigua atque dubia dicta Patrum, & Pseudosynodi Nicenæ auctoritatem, & pravam atque inve-teratam consuetudinem allegent: Re atque facto ipso ostendunt, sine Scriptura receptam esse Sanctorum invocationem: imò verò & contra Scripturam.
units.tr: they are unable to establish them, and so they allege either mutilated or ambiguous and doubtful sayings of the Fathers, the authority of the pseudo-synod of Nicaea, and a corrupt and long-standing custom. By the very fact and deed they show that the invocation of the saints has been received without Scripture, indeed even against Scripture.

units.la: Non debet autem in Ecclesia dogma ullum vel proponi, vel recipi, de quo nulla in Scriptura canonica extent certa, firma & perspicua testimonia: ac multo minùs vel proponendum, vel recipiendum est dogma pugnans cum Scriptura: præsertim verò invocatio nulla vel introducenda vel toleranda est in Ecclesia vera, quæ verbo Dei, id est, mandato ac promissione divina destituitur. Hoc enim verbum Dei ubi deest, nulla potest esse fides sive fiducia, quòd aut placeat talis invocatio, aut quòd exaudiatur: sicut Paulus expressè dixit ad Rom. cap. 10. Quo-modo invocabunt, in quem non crediderunt? Et habet hic etiam locum aphorismus ille ejusdem Apostoli: Quicquid non est ex fide, peccatum est.
units.tr: Nor ought any dogma to be proposed or received in the Church for which there are no certain, firm and clear testimonies in canonical Scripture; and much less ought a dogma that conflicts with Scripture to be proposed or received. Above all, no invocation is to be introduced or tolerated in the true Church which lacks the word of God, that is, the command and promise of God. For where this word of God is lacking, there can be no faith or confidence that such an invocation pleases or that it is heard. As Paul expressly said in Romans 10: How shall they call upon him in whom they have not believed? And that aphorism of the same Apostle also applies here: Whatever is not of faith is sin.

units.la: Quid de Augustini loco sčtiedum est, quem citat Austriaca Catechesis ex lib. 20. adversus Faustum, cap. 21?
units.tr: What is to be said about the passage of Augustine which the Austrian Catechism cites from book 20 against Faustus, chapter 21?

units.la: Resp. Non citant Jesuitæ bona fide eum locum, quia particulam saltem excerpunt, omisomissis iis, quæ sequuntur; & eam ipsam particulam perperam detorquent ad invocationem Sanctorum stabiliendam, de qua nullum verbum est in eo Augustini loco. Locus ergo Augustini integer hic est: Christianus Populus, (inquit) memorias Martyrum religiosa solennitate concelebrat, & ad excitandam imitationem, & ut meritis eorum (id est, præmiis) consocietur, atque orationibus adjuvetur: ita tamen, ut nulli martyrum, sed ipsi Deo martyrum (quamvis in memoriam Martyrum) constituamus altaria. Quis enim Antistitum in locis sanctorum corporum assistens altari, aliquando dixit: Offerimus tibi Petre, aut Paule, aut Cypriane: sed quod offertur, offertur Deo (qui martyres coronavit) apud memorias eorum, quos coronavit, ut ex ipsorum locorum admonitione major affectus excitetur, ad acuendam charitatem, & in illos, quos imitari possumus, & in illum, quo adjuvante possumus. Colimus ergo martyres eo cultu dilectionis & societatis, quo & in hac vita colunter Sancti homines Dei, quorum cor ad talem pro Evangelica veritate passionem paratum esse sentimus. Sed illos tanto devotius, quanto securius, post incerta omnia superata: quanto etiam fidentiori laude prædicamus jam in vita feliciore victores, quàm in ista adhuc usque pugnantes. Hæc Augustinus. Nam quæ de λατρεία sequuntur, ea suo loco postea considerabimus.
units.tr: Answer: The Jesuits do not cite that passage in good faith, for they excerpt only a part of it, leaving out what follows, and they twist that very part to establish the invocation of the saints, of which there is not a word in that passage of Augustine. The passage of Augustine, then, in full, is this: The Christian people, he says, celebrates the memories of the martyrs with religious solemnity, both to stir up imitation and so that they may be joined with their merits (that is, their rewards) and aided by their prayers. Yet we set up altars not to any martyr, but to God himself, the God of the martyrs, though in memory of the martyrs. For who of the bishops, standing at the altar in the places of the holy bodies, has ever said: We offer to you, Peter, or Paul, or Cyprian? Rather, what is offered is offered to God, who crowned the martyrs, at the memorials of those whom he crowned, so that from the very admonition of those places a greater affection may be stirred up, to sharpen charity both towards those whom we can imitate and towards him with whose help we can imitate them. We honour the martyrs, then, with that cult of love and fellowship with which holy men of God are also honoured in this life, whose heart we perceive to be ready for such suffering for the truth of the Gospel. But we honour them the more devoutly the more securely, now that all uncertainties have been overcome; and we proclaim them with the more confident praise as victors now in their happier life, than while they were still fighting in this one. Thus Augustine. But what follows about latreia [λατρεία] we shall consider later in its proper place.

units.la: Quis est scopus Augustini in hoc dicto?
units.tr: What is Augustine's aim in this saying?

units.la: Resp. Objecerat Faustus Manichæus Christianis: Idola vertistis in Martyres, quos votis suis similibus colitis: defunctorum umbras vino placatis & dapibus. Huic respondens Augustinus: Memorias quidem Martyrum concedit a Christiano populo celebrari; sed diserte negat, apud Christianos vel altaria constitui, vel sacrificia offerri Martyribus. Est autem inter sacrificia spiritualia, tum invocatio, tum gratiarum actio, quæ soli Deo debentur. Quare cum sacrificari Martyribus Augustinus negat, eo ipso refutat Manichæorum calumniam, qui Martyres similibus votis coli apud Christianos objiciebant, quibus idola apud Gentes coluntur.
units.tr: Answer. Faustus the Manichaean had objected to the Christians: You have turned idols into martyrs, whom you worship with vows like your own; you appease the shades of the dead with wine and feasts. Answering him, Augustine says: Indeed he grants that the memories of the martyrs are celebrated by the Christian people; but he plainly denies that altars are set up among Christians, or sacrifices offered, to the martyrs. Among the spiritual sacrifices, however, are both invocation and thanksgiving, which are due to God alone. So when Augustine denies that sacrifice is offered to the martyrs, he by that very fact refutes the Manichaean slander, which charged that the martyrs were worshipped among Christians with vows like those by which the idols are worshipped among the Gentiles.

units.la: Deinde, quia ritum Eucharistiæ sive Cœnæ dominicæ falso interpretabantur de placatione beatorum spirituum, quæ fieret vino & dapibus: citat Augustinus in hoc ipso capite ex Psalmo 50. dictum illud, quod de sacrificio spirituali loquitur: Sacrificium laudis glorificabit me, & illic via est, ubi ostendam illi salutare meum. Et hujus sacrificii, inquit, caro & sanguis ante adventum Christi per vi-itimas similitudinum promittebatur: In passione Christi. ne Christi per ipsam veritatem reddebatur: Possit ascensum Christi per Sacramentum memoriae celebratur.
units.tr: Next, because they misinterpreted the rite of the Eucharist, or the Lord's Supper, as an appeasing of the blessed spirits by wine and feasts, Augustine in this same chapter cites the words of Psalm 50 about the spiritual sacrifice: The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me, and there is the way on which I will show him my salvation. He says that the flesh and blood of this sacrifice were promised before the coming of Christ through the victims of likenesses: In the passion of Christ the truth itself was rendered; after the ascension of Christ it is celebrated through the sacrament of memory.

units.la: Sed & alibi, ut lib. 10. de civit. Dei, cap. 19. tanquam paria ponit cultum invocationis, ac gratiarum actionis, & sacrificium Eucharistiae, his verbis: Sicut orantes atque laudantes, ad eum dirigimus voces, significantes, cuius res ipsas, quas significamus, offerimus: ita sacrificantes (id est, celebrantes Eucharistiam in ipsa cœna dominica) non alteri visibile sacrificium (id est, sacra symbola) offerendum esse noverimus, quam illi, cuius in cordibus nostris invisibile sacrificium nos ipsi esse debemus.
units.tr: But elsewhere too, in book 10 of The City of God, chapter 19, he places the worship of invocation and of thanksgiving on a par with the sacrifice of the Eucharist, in these words: Just as, praying and praising, we direct our voices to him, signifying that we offer to him the very things whose signs we are, so, when we sacrifice (that is, celebrate the Eucharist in the Lord's Supper itself), we know that a visible sacrifice (that is, the holy symbols) is to be offered to no one but him, in whose hearts we ourselves ought to be an invisible sacrifice.

units.la: Quid nominat Augustinus memorias martyrum, quarum mentione Austriaca Catechesis Sanctorum invocationem stabilire conatur?
units.tr: What does Augustine mean by the memories of the martyrs, by mention of which the Austrian Catechism tries to establish the invocation of the saints?

units.la: Resp. Cùm initio collectionis Ecclesiæ ex gentibus magnam sævitiam tyranni exercerent, & multi Christiani propter cœlestis doctrinæ confessionem passim interficerentur, & Ecclesiæ opus esset crebris adhortationibus ad præstandam constantiam in confessione: paulatim mos introductus fuit, ut, quoties populus Christianus ad rem divinam faciendam, hoc est, ad conciones sacras audiendas, ad preces, & gratiarum actiones, & ad Cœnam nam dominicam convenisset, non solum nomina sanctorum Martyrum, qui constantes fuerant, ante celebrationem communionis recitarentur, sed etiam agones horum, & tristia certamina, & robur fidei & vitæ innocentia, & cæteræ virtutes commemorarentur: ut talibus exemplis alii quoque ad imitationem fidei, pœnitentiæ & aliarum virtutum, inprimisque ad similem constantiam in confessione præstandam exsuscitarentur: & simul Deo gratio agerentur, quòd ejusmodi lumina Ecclesiæ, Doctores & Confessores dedisset, & Spiritu suo animasset: denique ut & votis ardentibus peteret à Deo, ut superstites quoque organa salutaria efficeret, & similibus Spiritus sancti donis ornaret ac confirmaret. Paulatim verò invaluit consuetudo, ut corpora seu exuviæ Sanctorum iis in locis, ubi communio celebrabatur, reponerentur, itemq; ut ad sepulchra Sanctorum sequentibus temporibus etiam templa & altaria exstruerentur: quæ tamen, ut Augustinus expresse Scribit, non ipsis sanctis, sed Deo constituebantur.
units.tr: Answer. When at the beginning of the gathering of the Church from the Gentiles tyrants inflicted great cruelty, and many Christians were being killed everywhere for confessing the heavenly doctrine, and the Church needed frequent exhortations to show constancy in confession, a custom gradually came into use: whenever the Christian people had assembled to perform the divine service, that is, to hear the sacred sermons, for prayers and thanksgivings, and for the Lord's Supper, not only were the names of the holy martyrs who had remained steadfast read out before the celebration of communion, but also their contests, their sad struggles, the strength of their faith and the innocence of their lives, and their other virtues were recalled. The aim was that by such examples others too might be roused to imitate their faith, repentance and other virtues, and above all to show a similar constancy in confession; and at the same time God was thanked that he had given such lights of the Church, teachers and confessors, and had animated them with his Spirit; and finally that with fervent vows they might ask God to make the survivors also instruments of salvation and to adorn and strengthen them with similar gifts of the Holy Spirit. Gradually, however, the custom prevailed that the bodies or relics of the saints were placed in those places where communion was celebrated, and that in later times churches and altars were built over the tombs of the saints too. Yet, as Augustine expressly writes, these were set up not to the saints themselves but to God.

units.la: Hæc omnia uno nomine complectitur Augustinus, cùm memorias Sanctorum nominat. Quæ etsi postea in superstitionem converse sunt, tamen initio eas sine superstitione usurpatas fuisse, intelligi potest ex Hierarchia Dionysii Ecclesiastica, cap. 3. ubi refert, in administratione Eucharistiæ recitata fuisse ex sacris tabulis nomina eorum, qui pie sanctéque vixissent, & in Domino obdormivissent, idque his de causis.
units.tr: Augustine comprehends all these things under one name when he names the memories of the saints. Although these practices were afterwards turned into superstition, it can be understood that at first they were used without superstition from the Ecclesiastical Hierarchy of Dionysius, chapter 3, where he reports that in the administration of the Eucharist there were read from the sacred tablets the names of those who had lived piously and holily and had fallen asleep in the Lord, and this for these reasons.

units.la: I. Ut viventes ad imitationem provocarentur, & ad exemplum beatorum sanctè vivere, & pie in Domino mori docerentur.
units.tr: I. So that the living might be stirred up to imitation, and be taught to live holily after the example of the blessed, and to die piously in the Lord.

units.la: II. Et ut sancti illi prædicarentur esse non mortui, sed vivi, ut qui ex morte ad vitam verè divinam & coelestem translati jam essent.
units.tr: II. And so that those saints might be proclaimed not to be dead but alive, as those who had already been transferred from death to life truly divine and heavenly.

units.la: III. Et ut ostenderetur, eos esse in memoria apud Deum & Ecclesiam fidelium.
units.tr: III. And so that it might be shown that they are in memory before God and the faithful Church.

units.la: IV. Inprimis verò, quando altaribus suna impositæ venerabilia symbola, per qua signatur & sumitur Christus: Statim, inquit Dionysius, adest descriptio Sanctorum, ut indicetur individua ipsorum conjunctio, & sacratissima cum Christo unio.
units.tr: IV. Above all, when the venerable symbols, by which Christ is signified and received, have been placed upon the altars, straightway, says Dionysius, there is a recital of the saints, so that their inseparable union and the most holy union with Christ may be shown.

units.la: Extat etiam apud Eusebiū, lib. 4. hist. Eccl. Epist. Smyrnensis Ecclesiæ, in qua narratur, Gentiles atque Judæos apud præfectum instituisse, ne corpus Polycarpi Christianis traderetur, neque relicto crucifixo, Polycarpum colere inciperent. At ignorant, inquit Smyrnensis illa Epistola, quod neque Christum, qui pro salute eorum, qui in toto mundo salvandi sunt, passus est, unquam relinquere, neque aliquem alium colere poterimus.
units.tr: There is also in Eusebius, book 4 of the Church History, the letter of the Church of Smyrna, which relates that the Gentiles and Jews persuaded the prefect not to hand over the body of Polycarp to the Christians, lest they should begin to worship Polycarp instead of the crucified one. But they do not know, says that letter from Smyrna, that we can never abandon Christ, who suffered for the salvation of those who are to be saved in the whole world, nor worship anyone else.

units.la: Et postea: Christum tanquam Dei filium adoramus. eramus: Martyres vero tanquam discipulos & imitatores Domini diligimus, sicut dignum est propter insuperabilem erga regem & praeceptorem benevolentiam, quorum & nos consortes & discipulos fieri optamus. Et rursus: Celebramus diem natalitium Polycarpi (sic vero diem natalem seu natalitia vocabant annuum Martyrii diem, eo quod quasi in vitam vectam per mortem regeniti essent) ad memoriam eorum, qui certamen suum jam decertarunt, & ad sequentium exercitationem & praeparationem, sive ut Ruffini paraphrasis habet, ut sequentium animi ad precedentium viam insignibus exemplis suscitentur, audientes ipsos a certamina celebrari, et jam coronâ incorruptionis ornatos, ac bravio incoparabili donatos esse.
units.tr: And afterwards: We adore Christ as the Son of God. But the martyrs we love as disciples and imitators of the Lord, as is fitting, because of their unsurpassable goodwill towards the King and Teacher, of whom we too wish to be companions and disciples. And again: We celebrate the birthday of Polycarp (they called the yearly day of martyrdom their birthday or natalitia, because they had been born again into a life, as it were, carried over through death), in memory of those who have already finished their contest, and for the training and preparation of those who will follow; or, as the paraphrase of Rufinus has it, so that the minds of those who come after may be stirred up by notable examples to walk the path of those who went before, hearing that these have been celebrated in their contests and are now crowned with the crown of incorruption and given the incomparable prize.

units.la: Atqui in Augustini dicto consociationis meritorum quoque fit mentio, & orationum, quibus juvemur a Sanctis?
units.tr: But does Augustine's saying not also mention the fellowship of merits, and of the prayers by which we are helped by the saints?

units.la: Resp.
units.tr: Reply.

units.la: Primùm quod ad consociationem attinet, Augustinus idem intelligit, quod Epistola Smyrnensis dicit, ὥν γένοιτο καὶ ἡμᾶς συγκοινωνούς γενέσθαι: videlicet, ut Ecclesia in hac vita militans, virtutum illarum, quae in Martyribus celebrantur, consors reddatur, acceptis a Deo similibus virtutum donis, utque consors aliquando fiat, & socia praemiorum, quorum in vita aeterna marmartyres jam compotes facti sunt. Utrumque enim, id est, virtutes & praemia harum, vocabulo Meriti veteres intelligunt.
units.tr: First, as regards fellowship, Augustine means the same thing that the Smyrnaean letter means when it says "that we too may be made partakers with them" [ὥν γένοιτο καὶ ἡμᾶς συγκοινωνούς γενέσθαι]. That is, the Church, still militant in this life, may be made a partaker of those virtues which are celebrated in the martyrs, receiving from God similar gifts of virtue, and may at some point become a sharer and partner in those rewards which the martyrs already enjoy in eternal life. For the ancients understood both, that is, the virtues and their rewards, by the word "merit."

units.la: Deinde, quod de adjumento orationum Augustinus addit, ex eo nequaquam sequitur, Sanctos esse invocandos.
units.tr: Next, what Augustine adds about the help of prayers does not at all follow that the saints are to be invoked.

units.la: Hanc enim consequentiam falsam esse, multis aliis in locis Augustinus ipse ostendit. Sic vero loquitur, secundum consuetudinem sui temporis, quo recepta erat opinio, quanquam sine Scripturae authoritate, quod cum apud memorias martyrum Deus invocabatur, simul animae martyrum una Deum comprecarentur.
units.tr: Augustine himself shows in many other places that this inference is false. He speaks thus, however, according to the custom of his time, when the received opinion was (although it lacked the authority of Scripture) that when God was invoked at the memorials of the martyrs, the souls of the martyrs at the same time joined in praying to God.

units.la: Rectene objicitur Potificiis, quod idololatriam committant in cultu Sanctorum mortuorum: cum profitentur Catechesis Austriaca, Sanctos cum Christo regnantes, non ut Deos, Ethnicorum more, colendos, neque perinde ac Deum sanctum sanctorum, sed longe inferiori modo & gradu?
units.tr: Is it rightly objected to the Papists that they commit idolatry in the worship of dead saints, when the Austrian Catechism professes that the saints reigning with Christ are not to be worshipped as gods after the manner of the heathen, nor in the same way as God the Holy of Holies, but in a far lower mode and degree?

units.la: Resp. Uni & soli Deo Patri, Filio & Spiritui sancto, debetur cultus invocationis. In hoc cultu nulli gradus fingendi sunt, sive superiores, sive inferiores: sed simpliciter retinendus est unicus ille modus invocationis prapræscriptus in his dictis: Deut. 6. Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, & illi soli servies. Et Psalmo 50. Invoca me in die tribulationis, & eripiam te, & tu glorificabis me. Et Hebr. 4. Habentes Pontificem magnum, qui penetravit cœlos, Iesum filium Dei, accedamus cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ ejus, ut misericordiam consequamur & gratiam inveniamus in auxilio opportuno. Non potest igitur ab idololatria excusari, ne quidem inferior ille modus, quem comminiscuntur Iesuitæ, quo infra Deum sanctum sanctorum dicunt invocandos esse Sanctos in cœlo regnantes cum Christo: cum nulli prorsus creaturæ, neque æqualis, neque gradu aliquantum inferiori, cultus invocationis competat.
units.tr: Reply: the worship of invocation is owed to the one God alone, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. In this worship no degrees are to be imagined, whether higher or lower. Rather, that single mode of invocation prescribed in these sayings must simply be retained: Deut. 6: "You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone." And Ps. 50: "Call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me." And Heb. 4: "Having a great high priest who has passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us draw near with confidence to the throne of his grace, that we may obtain mercy and find grace to help us in time of need." Therefore they cannot be excused from idolatry, not even by that lower mode which the Jesuits devise, by which they say the saints reigning in heaven with Christ are to be invoked below God the Holy of Holies, since the worship of invocation belongs to no creature whatever, neither an equal nor one somewhat lower in degree.

units.la: Deinde inter idololatriam gentium, & culum atque invocationem sanctorum apud Pontificios, nihil interest, nisi nominum sive appellationum diversitas: illis quidem idola sua Deos nominantibus; his vero sanctos suos divorum nomine appellantibus.
units.tr: Next, between the idolatry of the nations and the worship and invocation of the saints among the Papists there is no difference except in the names or appellations: the heathen call their idols gods, while the Papists call their saints by the title of the divi.

units.la: Constituerunt autem inter gentes quoq; pleriq; sapientes unum summum Deum, cui alia numina inferiora subjecerunt: quòd putarent supremi illius numinis majestate subli-miorem esse, quàm ut vel singulas mortalium res curare velit, vel à miseris atque indignis hominibus adiri posset; inferiores vero Deos aditu faciliores esse, & cura humanarum rerum magis affici: &c, quia apud summum illum Deum authoritate valeant, posse eos illa, quibus indigent homines, conficere, impetrare, atque largiri petentibus.
units.tr: Moreover, many of the wise among the nations also set up one supreme God and subordinated to him lesser deities. They thought that the supreme God was too exalted in his majesty to care for each single mortal matter, or to be approached by wretched and unworthy men, whereas the lesser gods were more accessible and more concerned with human affairs; and because they had influence with that supreme God, they could bring about, obtain and bestow on petitioners what men need.

units.la: Cum his prorsus congruunt illa Papistarum commenta, qui Deum quidem supra Sanctos collocant, & tamen per hos aditum ad Deum quaerunt, eorumq; gratiam & opem implorant.
units.tr: Those Papist inventions agree entirely with these. They indeed place God above the saints, and yet seek access to God through them, and implore their grace and help.

units.la: Neq; minor divorum apud Pontificios multitudo & varietas est, quam Deorum illorum Ethnicorum, quorum triginta millia, sicut & Joves trecentos apud diversas gentes numerari potuisse, Augustinus ex Varrone refert.
units.tr: Nor is the multitude and variety of divi among the Papists less than that of those heathen gods, of whom, as Augustine reports from Varro, thirty thousand could be counted, just as three hundred Jupiters could be counted among different nations.

units.la: Hanc tantam multitudinem Deorum idem Varro divisit in Deos certos & incertos. Et illos quidem sic vocavit, de quibus dubitari non posset, ut solem, lunam, coelum, & terram, &c.
units.tr: The same Varro divided this great multitude of gods into certain and uncertain gods. Those he called certain, about whom there could be no doubt, were such as the sun, the moon, heaven and earth, etc.

units.la: Hos vero, quorum certa ratio reddi non potest, qui sint: ut & in Actis Apostolorum Dei ignoti apud Athenienses fit mentio. §. Alii insuper Dii coelites dicti sunt ab Ethnicis, quae superiori aethere, ad Solem usque se demittant, & caularum latentiu arcana componant: Alii aute secundi Dei, a Sole ad Lunam usque, quae vaticiniis, somniis, & prodigiis, caeterisque, similibus rebus praesse credebantur. §. Fuerunt & Dii inter Ethnicos, alii majorum gentium habiti, & majores Dii dicti fuerunt, mares sex, & foeminę (ex, quos Martian his fib. copiex est: luno. Iuno, Vesta, Minerva, Ceres, Diana, Venus, Mars, Mercurius, Iovis, Neptunus, Vulcanus, Apollo.
units.tr: Those whose nature cannot be given any certain account, who they are, were uncertain; as also mention is made in the Acts of the Apostles of the unknown God among the Athenians. §. Other gods were called heavenly by the heathen, who come down from the upper air as far as the sun and arrange the hidden secrets of things. Others again were called second gods, from the sun down to the moon, who were believed to preside over prophecies, dreams, portents and similar things. §. There were also gods among the heathen, some regarded as of the greater nations, and these were called the greater gods, six male and six female (from whom Martianus in his book gives the list): Juno, Vesta, Minerva, Ceres, Diana, Venus, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Neptune, Vulcan, Apollo.

units.la: Alii minuti, qui & minores, & minorū gentiū vocabantur, qui ex hominibus in Deorū numerū translati erant, qui & asscriptitii dicebantur, & Dii Novenfiles, quasi novissimi in Deorum numerum recepti, id est, novissime five nuper salientes, atq; in nomen Deorū ascendentes. ¶ Sic autē & Pontificii in numerum Sanctorū reponunt, non modo illos, de quibus testimonia certa haberi possunt, vel ex sacris literis, vel aliis historiis fide dignis, ǫ certis temporibus in his terris vixerint, & à Deo testimonia pietatis suę habuerint: sed etiam alios, quib. Romani Pontifices honorem istū decreverunt, sua illa ἀνακήρυξις (seu canonisatione, quæ ex medio gentilismo defluxit. Et horū quidè alios eminentiores ac potentiores, alios inferiores nominant, singulis certa quasi procuratione assignata: Prorsus ut inter Deos illos Ethnicos distributa fuit per certas procurationes administratio universi, & singulis mundi partib⁹, alii atq; alii peculiariter præfecti fuerunt: alii terræ, mari, sylvis, montibus, vallibus: Item regionibus, provinciis, civitatibus, familiis, domibus, frugibus, pecoribus, opibus, morbis, artibus, opificiis. &c. Ut ex opere Lilii Giraldi, quod de Diis gentium inscripsit, cognosci copiose potest. Similī ratione apud Pontificios singulæ regiones, singulæ familiæ, singulæ domus,
units.tr: The others were the lesser gods, also called minor gods and gods of the lesser nations. They had been transferred from among men into the number of the gods. They were also called adscript gods, and Novensiles gods, as it were the newest received into the number of the gods, that is, those who had lately sprung up and ascended into the name of gods. ¶ In the same way the Papists also place in the number of the saints not only those of whom certain testimony can be had, either from Holy Scripture or from other trustworthy histories, who lived in these lands at certain times and had testimony of their piety from God, but also others to whom the Roman Pontiffs have granted this honour by their own proclamation (or canonization), which flowed out of the midst of heathenism [ἀνακήρυξις]. Some of these they name more eminent and powerful, others inferior, each assigned a certain quasi-office. Just as among those heathen gods the government of the universe was distributed through fixed offices, and different gods were set peculiarly over the separate parts of the world: some over land, sea, woods, mountains and valleys; likewise over regions, provinces, cities, families, houses, crops, flocks, wealth, diseases, skills and trades, and so on. This can be learned in abundance from the work of Lilius Giraldus, which he wrote On the Gods of the Nations. In a similar way among the Papists each region, each family, each house,

units.la: {a} in distributione, curationes & tutelarum. singuli homines, singuli status, singulæ artes, singuli morbi, &c. peculiarem Sanctum, velut numen quoddam tutelare habuerunt. De quo exempla aliqua juventutis monendæ causâ paulò pòst in medium proferre, haud alienum ab hoc loco fuerit: ex quibus luce meridiana clarius appareat, qui ex Sanctis provinciarum, urbium, artificum, animantium patroni, qui averruncatores malorum, qui bonorum largitores habiti fuerint.
units.tr: {a} in the distribution of cures and guardianships. Each individual, each condition, each art, each disease, and so on, has a particular Saint, as a kind of guardian deity. Concerning this it will not be out of place at this point to bring forward some examples, for the instruction of young people, from which it will appear clearer than midday light which saints were held to be patrons of provinces, cities, craftsmen and animals, which were held to be averters of evils, and which were held to be dispensers of blessings.

units.la: Quid dicam vero, quòd in honorem & cultum Deorum Ethnicorum olim extructa atque usurpata fuerunt tot templa, delubra, sacella, altaria, aræ, sacrificia, simulachra, vota, preces, gratulationes, festa, celebritates, feriæ, suffitus thuris, candelæ, faces, supplicationes, & lectisternia, quæ ad templa & pulvinaria Deorum, vel ob lætitiam, vel ad avertendam Deorum iram peragebantur: Ambarvalia item, ad arva & segetes lustrandas; & Amburbalia, quoties urbs lustrabatur.
units.tr: What shall I say, moreover, that in honour and worship of the heathen gods there were once built and used so many temples, shrines, chapels, altars, hearths, sacrifices, images, vows, prayers, thanksgivings, festivals, celebrations, holy days, offerings of incense, candles, torches, supplications and lectisternia, which were performed at the temples and couches of the gods, either out of joy or to turn away the anger of the gods; likewise the Ambarvalian rites, for purifying the fields and crops, and the Amburbalian rites, whenever the city was purified?

units.la: Prorsus autem similia in Papatu fiunt in cultu Sanctorum mortuorum. Habent enim isti quoque templa sua, sacella, columnas, altaria. Habent dies festos, vigilias, jejunia, cereos, suffitus. Habent Missas peculiariter singulis consecratas. Litaniæ & preces omnes, tam publicæ, quam privatæ personant Sanctorum invocatione: Juramenta ipsis nominatis fiunt. Statuæ eis ponuntur auro, argento, serico exornatæ. Hæ adorantur, aut certè genibus ad eas flexis preces recitantur: ad has vota, & oblationes, ac peregrinationes fiunt. Et audent tamen boni illi Iesuitæ negare, se Ethnicorum more Sanctos suos colere? cùm non ovum ovo, neque lac lacti simile sit, quàm cultus Sanctorum apud Pontificios, & idolorum apud Ethnicos.
units.tr: Certainly similar things are done in Papacy in the worship of dead saints. For they too have their temples, shrines, columns and altars. They have feast days, vigils, fasts, wax candles and incense. They have Masses consecrated particularly to individual saints. All litanies and prayers, both public and private, resound with the invocation of the saints; oaths are sworn by them by name. Statues are set up for them adorned with gold, silver and silk. These are adored, or at least prayers are recited with knees bent before them; vows, offerings and pilgrimages are made to them. And do those good Jesuits dare to deny that they worship their saints in the manner of the heathen, when egg is no more like egg, nor milk like milk, than the worship of saints among the Papists is like the worship of idols among the heathen?

units.la: Quid de hoc Sophismate Catechescos Austriacæ judicandum est?
units.tr: What is to be judged about this sophism of the Austrian Catechism?

units.la: Sancti venerandi sunt, velut amici, filii, hæredes Dei, & cohæredes Christi, & sanctissimi atque beatissimi: qui praterea nostra saluti eò studient favéntque impensiùs, quò sunt in omni charitate, in omni virtute, ac cœlesti gloria perfectiores, quàm hìc esse in carne potuissent.
units.tr: The saints are to be venerated as friends, sons, heirs of God, co-heirs of Christ, and most holy and most blessed. Moreover, they devote themselves all the more eagerly and favour our salvation, the more they are perfect in all charity, all virtue, and heavenly glory, beyond what they could have been while in the flesh here.

units.la: Ergò ut infra Deum illos plus quàm ullos in terra mortales recte amamus: ita eosdem (tali tantaq; dignitate auctos) honoramus etiam, atq; pro Christiana pietate invocamus.
units.tr: Therefore, just as we rightly love them more than any mortals on earth, though below God, so we also honour them (raised to such and so great a dignity) and, in Christian piety, invoke them.

units.la: Resp. Plus est in consequenti, quàm fuit in antecedente. Nequaquà enim Christianæ pietatis est invocare Sanctos: neque vel amoris erga Sanctos mortuos, vel honoris, qui eis debetur, pars est precatio directa ad ipsos, vel ut intercessores, vel ut auxiliatores. Cùm autem omnes suas superstitiones, atque adeò etiam cultus Sanctorum idolatricos, prætextu textu honoris ac venerationis, quæ debetur Sanctis, occultent Pontificii (nam si Sancti sunt venerandi: mox inferunt: Ergo invocandi: Ergo suffragia, patrocinia, merita, protectiones, auxilia Sanctorum imploranda sunt) paulò copiosius de Sanctorum mortuorum honore, ac veneratione dicendum nobis erit, ut intelligatur, etsi aliquis honos debeatur Sanctis, tamen non omnem eis honorem competere.
units.tr: Reply: There is more in the conclusion than there was in the premise. It is by no means a part of Christian piety to invoke the saints, nor is direct prayer to them, whether as intercessors or as helpers, a part either of love for the dead saints or of the honour due to them. Since the Papists hide all their superstitions, and indeed their idolatrous worship of the saints, under the pretext of the honour and veneration due to the saints (for if the saints are to be venerated, they immediately infer: therefore they are to be invoked; therefore the suffrages, patronage, merits, protections and aid of the saints are to be implored), we shall have to speak rather more fully about the honour and veneration of the dead saints, so that it may be understood that, although some honour is due to the saints, not every kind of honour belongs to them.

units.la: Quod igitur Catechesis Austriaca hic primo loco dicit: Sancti sunt amici, filii & hæredes Dei, & Christi coharedes, Rom. 8. 1. Cor. 6. Joh. 8. Joh. 10.
units.tr: What the Austrian Catechism says first here, then, is that "the saints are friends, sons and heirs of God, and co-heirs of Christ": Rom. 8. 1 Cor. 6. John 8. John 10.

units.la: Respondeo, hos titulos atque hæc elogia congruere etiam fidelibus in hac vita, ut Chrysostomus inquit enarrans Psalmum 71. Benedictus Deus, qui fecit mirabilia solus, qui fecit universa: Ecce libertatis serenitate perfruntur, qui tenebantur paulo ante captivi: Et cives Ecclesiæ sunt, qui fuerant in peregrinationis errore: Et justitia in sorte versantur, qui fuerunt in confusione peccati. Non enim tantum sunt liberi: Sed & Sancti. Non tantum Sancti, sed & justi, Non solum justi sed & filii: non solum filii, sed & hæredes Dei: non solum hæredes, sed & fratres Christi: non tantum fratres Christi, sed & coharedes: non solum coharedes, sed & membra Christi: non tantum membra, sed et templum: non tantum templum, sed & organon Spiritus Santus Sancti. Vides quot sint baptismatis largitates, & non nulli deputant caelestē gratiam in peccatorum tantum remissione consistere. Nos autem honores computavimus decem. Haec Chrysostom.
units.tr: I answer that these titles and praises belong also to the faithful in this life, as Chrysostom says in expounding Psalm 71: "Blessed be God, who alone does wondrous things, who made all things. Behold, those who a little before were held captive now enjoy the serenity of liberty; and those who were wandering in the error of the way are now citizens of the Church; and those who were in the confusion of sin now dwell in the lot of righteousness. For they are not only free, but also saints; not only saints, but also just; not only just, but also sons; not only sons, but also heirs of God; not only heirs, but also brothers of Christ; not only brothers of Christ, but also co-heirs; not only co-heirs, but also members of Christ; not only members, but also a temple; not only a temple, but also an instrument [ὄργανον] of the Holy Spirit. You see how many are the gifts of baptism, and some reckon heavenly grace to consist only in the remission of sins. But we have counted ten honours." Thus Chrysostom.

units.la: Quis vero dixerit? Fideles propterea invocandos esse: quos tamen & amamus & honoram etiam, & alios aliorū saluti studere atq; favere persuasum habemus, propter eam, quia inter se communionem habent cū Deo Patre & Filio ejus Dn. nostro Jesu Christo. 1. Joh. 1.
units.tr: But who would say that the faithful are therefore to be invoked? Yet we both love and honour them, and we are persuaded that they also devote themselves to, and favour, one another's salvation, because they have fellowship with God the Father and his Son our Lord Jesus Christ. 1 John 1.

units.la: Deinde, quod addit Catechesis Austriaca: Sanctos in statu beatitudinis esse, & saluti nostrae eo favere impensius, quo sunt in charitate, virtute, gloria caelesti perfectiores: Ideoq; plus amare dosse, quam ullos in terra mortales, itemq; tali tantaq; dignitate auctos, honorandos atq; invocandos esse. Nos quidem nihil de perfectione beatitudinis, virtutum, gloriæ Sanctorum decrevimus, postea quam ex carne mortali animæ illorum liberatæ, atque in caelestes sedes receptæ sunt, ubi coram Deo luce, sapientia, justicia, vita, lætitia divina.
units.tr: Next, the Austrian Catechism adds that the saints are in a state of blessedness, and favour our salvation all the more, the more they are perfect in charity, virtue, and heavenly glory; and therefore that they are to be loved more than any mortals on earth and, raised to such and so great a dignity, are to be honoured and invoked. We, for our part, have decided nothing about the perfection of the blessedness, virtues, and glory of the saints, since their souls, freed from mortal flesh and received into the heavenly seats, are where they are before God in light, wisdom, righteousness, life and divine joy.

units.la: Agnoscimus etiam a nobis, dum in vitæ hujus exilio, atq; in hac lachrymarum valle, peccato & morti adhuc subjecti sumus, illam Pauli Apostoli querelam jure ac merito usurpari: Infelix ego homo, quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus? Et quod Johannes ait: Nunc filii Dei sumus: sed nondum apparuit, quid quid erimus. Scimus autem, quoniam cum apparuerit, similes erimus, quoniam videbimus eum, sicut est. Et omnis, qui habet hanc spem in eo, sanctificat se, sicut & ille sanctus est.
units.tr: We also acknowledge that, while we are still subject to sin and death in this exile of life and this valley of tears, that lament of the Apostle Paul rightly and deservedly becomes ours: "Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from the body of this death?" And what John says: "Now we are the sons of God, but it has not yet appeared what we shall be. We know that when it appears we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is. And everyone who has this hope in him sanctifies himself, as he also is holy."

units.la: Plus igitur venerandos, plus honorandos esse fatemur Sanctos illos in triumphanti Ecclesia: utpote vere & perfecte beatos: sed non invocamus, quia huic honorem, neque expetunt illi a nobis, neque nos eis debemus.
units.tr: Therefore we confess that those saints in the triumphant Church are to be venerated and honoured the more, as truly and perfectly blessed; but we do not invoke them, because they do not seek this honour from us, nor are we obliged to give it to them.

units.la: DE VERO HONORE Sanctorum.
units.tr: ON THE TRUE HONOUR OF THE SAINTS.

units.la: Alius est autem honos, quem Scriptura Sanctis tribuit: juxta haec dicta. Psal. 112. In memoria aeterna erit justus. Proverb. 10. Memoria justi erit in benedictione, quod & Syracides repetit c. 45 Cujus memoria est in benedictione. Et cap. 46. Sit memoria illorum in benedictione. Qua forma verborum adhuc hodie utimur in elogiis praestantium virorum. Quod Sapientiae 4. dicitur: Immortalis est memoria ejus, quoniam & apud Deum nota est, & apud homines. Et cap. 8. Relinquet posteris memoriam perpetuam. Et Maria in cantico sup, Luc. 1. Ecce beatam me dicent omnes generationes. Quin & Christus Marc. 14. Ubicunque praedicabitur Evangelium in universo mundo, etiam hoc, quod fecit haec mulier, narrabitur in memoriam ejus. Non igitur vel leviter sentiendum, vel contumeliose loquendum est de iis, qui ut Paulus 2. Tim. 4. de se loquitur, bonum certamen certarunt, fidem servarunt, cursum confummarunt: quiq; jam præsentes sunt apud Dominum, ut Philip. 1. & 2. ad Corinth. 5. scriptum est.
units.tr: There is, however, another honour which Scripture gives to the saints, according to these sayings: Psalm 112, The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance. Proverbs 10, The memory of the just is blessed, which Ecclesiasticus also repeats in chapter 45: Whose memory is in blessing. And in chapter 46: Let their memory be in blessing. We still use this form of words today in the eulogies of distinguished men. In Wisdom 4 it is said: Her memory is immortal, because it is known both with God and with men. And in chapter 8: She shall leave an everlasting memory to posterity. And Mary in her song, Luke 1: Behold, all generations shall call me blessed. Indeed Christ himself, Mark 14: Wherever the gospel is preached throughout the whole world, this also that she has done shall be told in memory of her. Therefore we should neither think nor speak lightly or contemptuously of those who, as Paul says of himself in 2 Timothy 4, have fought the good fight, have kept the faith, have finished the course, and who are now present with the Lord, as is written in Philippians 1 and 2 Corinthians 5.

units.la: Nec desunt exempla in sacris literis, ubi memoria piorum honorifice celebratur. Ostendit enim Psalm. 105. & 106. etiam in publicis Ecclesiæ conventibus laudes Sanctorum decantatas fuisse. Et celebrat memoriam Patriarcharū Christus, Joh. 8. cùm Abrahæ fidem & opera prædicat. Et Matth. 22. cùm inquit, Deū esse Deum vivorum; & Deū Abraham, Isaac, & Jacob. Sic & Johannis Baptistę viventis ac mortui memoriam celebrat Christus Matth. 11. & 14. & Joh. 5. Paulus quoq; Abrahamum prædicat Rom. 4. & Stephanus Act. 7. longum catalogum texit Sanctorum veteris testamenti, Et ad Heb. 11. ceu panegyricus quidam λόγος Sanctorum fidelium contexitur.
units.tr: Nor are there lacking examples in the sacred letters where the memory of the godly is honourably celebrated. For Psalms 105 and 106 show that the praises of the saints were sung even in the public assemblies of the Church. Christ too honours the memory of the patriarchs, John 8, when he commends the faith and works of Abraham; and Matthew 22, when he says that God is the God of the living, and the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Likewise Christ celebrates the memory of John the Baptist, both living and dead, Matthew 11 and 14 and John 5. Paul also extols Abraham, Romans 4, and Stephen, Acts 7, recounts a long catalogue of the saints of the Old Testament. And Hebrews 11 is woven together like a certain panegyric discourse on the faithful saints.

units.la: Apud Syracidem quoq; à cap. 44. ufq; ad finem libri prolixè celebrantur Sancti Dei homines. Denique & in Apocalypsi passim ostenditur, Sanctos esse in precio apud Deum post hanc vitam.
units.tr: In Ecclesiasticus, from chapter 44 to the end of the book, the holy men of God are celebrated at length. Finally, the Apocalypse everywhere shows that the saints are held in honour with God after this life.

units.la: Verum nō quōslibet honores Sanctorū D. Deo gratos & sanctis acceptos esse, eadem sa cra scriptura docet. Recusat enim Angelus Apoc.19. & 22. adorationem. Et Petrus Act.10. Cornelium coram ipso procidente adoradi caussa, manu sua elevat, inquiens: Surge, nam & ego homo sum. Et Paulus ac Barnabas Act. 14. cum sacrificare ipsis Lystrensesinstituerent: conscissis vestibus suis exsiliunt in turbas, clamantes: Quid haec facitis? Et nos mortales sumus, similes vobis homines. Reprehendit & Christus Pharisaeos Matth. 23. aedificantes sepulchra Prophetarum, & ornantes monumenta justorum: cum doctrina ab illis traditam pala persequerentur. Et Moyse, cujus memoriam Judaei honorifice celebrabat, cum doctrinam ejus non sequerentur, ait accusaturu ipsos. Joh. 5. Sicut & 8. c. exprobrat eis: Quod cum filios Abrahae se esse jactarent, opera tamen Abrahae non facerent. Hoc modo cum Scriptura doceat in honorandis Sanctis saepe & facile peccari: attente considerandum est, qui sint gradus veri honoris Sanctorum, qui vere & citra Dei contumeliam eis competant.
units.tr: But that the sacred Scripture teaches that not every honour paid to the saints is pleasing to God and acceptable to them, is also clear. For the angel refuses adoration, Revelation 19 and 22. And Peter, Acts 10, when Cornelius fell down before him to worship, raised him up with his hand, saying: Rise, for I too am a man. And Paul and Barnabas, Acts 14, when the Lystrans were preparing to sacrifice to them, tore their garments and leapt among the crowd, crying out: Why do you do these things? We too are mortal men, like you. Christ also rebukes the Pharisees, Matthew 23, who build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous, while they persecute with their hands the teaching handed down by them. And Moses, whose memory the Jews honoured with praise, they did not follow his teaching, and he will be their accuser, John 5. Just as in chapter 8 he rebukes them: though they boasted that they were the sons of Abraham, yet they did not do the works of Abraham. Since in this way Scripture teaches that in honouring the saints one often and easily sins, we must consider carefully what are the degrees of the true honour of the saints, which properly and without insult to God belong to them.

units.la: Est autem primus gradus: ut Deus ipse in Sanctis celebretur: Quemadmodum Paulus ad Galatas 1. recitata vocationis & conversionis suae historia, inquit: Glorificabant in me Deum. Sic igitur vere honoratur Sancti, cum Deo agimus gratias, quod per eos se patefecit, quod doctrinam suam per eos tradidit, quod
units.tr: The first degree is that God himself be celebrated in the saints, as Paul, in Galatians 1, after recounting the story of his calling and conversion, says: They glorified God in me. Thus the saints are truly honoured when we give thanks to God that he has made himself known through them, that he has delivered his teaching through them, that

units.la: {1} Dei celebratio. quòd edidit evidentia testimonia per ministerium eorum, quòd Ecclesiam subinde per aliquos instauravit, quòd dona diversa in Ecclesia distribuit. Haec opera Dei celebranda sunt, & laudandi sunt ipsi Sancti, quòd donis Dei fideliter usi sunt: Quae tamen laus vero ad Deum pertinet, ut dicitur;
units.tr: {1} The celebration of God: that he has published clear testimonies through their ministry, that from time to time he has restored the Church through certain men, that he has distributed various gifts in the Church. These works of God are to be celebrated, and the saints themselves are to be praised because they faithfully used the gifts of God. Yet this praise truly belongs to God, as it is said:

units.la: Quos ego cum laudo, laus ea tota Dei est.
units.tr: When I praise them, all the praise is God's.

units.la: In quam sententiam & 1. ad Cor. 15. Paulus inquit: Gratia Dei sum id, quod sum. Non fuit enim in me gratia ejus vacua, sed abundantius illis omnibus laboravi. Non ego autem, sed gratia Dei, quae mecum est.
units.tr: To the same effect Paul says, 1 Corinthians 15: By the grace of God I am what I am. For his grace toward me was not in vain, but I laboured more abundantly than they all. Yet not I, but the grace of God which is with me.

units.la: Alter gradus honoris est confirmatio fidei nostrae: ut cum genus doctrinae cōsideramus, quod Sancti professi sunt, & pro quo certamina subierunt, & cum hujus doctrinae testimonia intuemur: Item cum cogitamus exempla divinae misericordiae, quae Deus ostendit receptis lapsis: cumq; exempla colligimus, quae docent exaudiri preces nostras in periculis, & vere impetrare liberationes: talibus exemplis confirmanda est fides nostra, & exuscitanda invocatio ad Deum. Sic 2. Pet. 1. scriptum est: Dabo operam, ut post meum obitum horum omnium memoriam habeatis: Non enim doctas fabulas secuti sumus, cum nota fecimus vobis Domini nostri Jesu Christi virtutem et praesentiam: sed speculatores fuimus, &c. Et Paulus exemplum suae receptionis gratui-
units.tr: The second degree of honour is the confirmation of our faith: when we consider the kind of doctrine which the saints professed, and for which they underwent their struggles, and when we look at the testimonies to this doctrine; likewise when we reflect on the examples of divine mercy which God has shown to those who have fallen and been received back; and when we gather the examples which teach that our prayers are heard in dangers and that deliverances are truly obtained. By such examples our faith is to be strengthened and our invocation of God is to be stirred up. So it is written in 2 Peter 1: I will take care that after my death you have the memory of all these things. For we did not follow cunningly devised fables when we made known to you the power and presence of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses, and so on. And Paul sets forth his own example of gratuitous reception:

units.la: € 2 gratuitæ proponit. 1. Tim. 1. Fidelis sermo, & omni acceptione dignus, quod Christus Iesus venit in hunc mundum peccatores salvos facere: Quorum primus ego sum. Sed ideo misericordiam consecutus sum, ut in me primo ostenderet Christus Iesus omnem patientiam, ad exemplum iis, qui credituri sunt in eum ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: Gratuitous. 1 Timothy 1: This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the first. But for this reason I obtained mercy, that in me first Christ Jesus might show forth all patience, as an example to those who will believe on him unto eternal life.

units.la: David etiam exemplum liberationum suarum proponit toti Ecclesiæ, inquiens Psal. 34. Accedite ad eum, illuminamini, & facies vestræ non confundentur. Iste pauper clamavit ad Dominum, & de omnibus tribulationibus ejus salvavit eum.
units.tr: David also sets forth the example of his deliverances to the whole Church, saying in Psalm 34: Draw near to him, and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be confounded. This poor man cried to the Lord, and he saved him out of all his tribulations.

units.la: Tertius honoris gradus est Imitatio. Primo fidei, deinde cæterorum virtutum, quibus excelluerunt sancti, quos imitari pro sua quisque vocatione debet.
units.tr: The third degree of honour is imitation: first of faith, then of the other virtues in which the saints excelled, which each person ought to imitate according to his own calling.
