O sanctitatis speculum divinae legis aemulis Augustine, per seculum hunc rege gregem Christi, ut te sequatur sedulus ad gaudia perennia, quo jam praeisti.
units.tr: Gradual: Augustine, flower of prelates, who unlocked what was closed, who gave us to drink the cup of sacred teaching and condemned heresies, visit us, raise us up, you who preached life. Hallelujah. Hail, flower and light of teachers, cleanse us, who are foul with the mire of vices, O blessed Augustine. Hallelujah. O mirror of holiness, rival of the divine law, Augustine, rule the flock of Christ through this age, so that it may follow you eagerly to the everlasting joys to which you have already gone before.

units.la: SEQUENTIA.
units.tr: SEQUENCE.

units.la: Ergo pater Augustine tua normam disciplina sequentes vernaculos | Juva semper, ut seramus Hic in terris, quos metamus In coelis manipulos.
units.tr: Therefore, Father Augustine, following the rule of your discipline, always help us, that here on earth we may sow, and in heaven reap the sheaves.

units.la: Offertorium: Preces & hostias tibi dicatas, Domine, quaesumus, venerandus Confessor tuus & Pontifex Augustinus conciliet, quem Ecclesiae tuae & doctrinae Salutaris speculum & turrim fidei inexpugnabilis praerogasti.
units.tr: Offertory: May the venerable confessor and bishop Augustine, whom you, O Lord, have set forth as the mirror of your Church and of saving doctrine and the unconquered tower of faith, win favour for the prayers and sacrifices dedicated to you, we beseech you.

units.la: Communio: Sumta mysteria, Domine, quaesumus, gloriosus confessor tuus & Pontifex Augustinus salutaria nobis imploret, qui fidelis talenti dominici dispensator Ecclesiam tuam magnifice roboravit, docuit, & ornavit.
units.tr: Communion: Having received the mysteries, O Lord, we beseech you, may your glorious confessor and bishop Augustine plead for us what is salutary, he who, a faithful steward of the Lord's talent, magnificently strengthened, taught and adorned your Church.

units.la: De eodem: Inclyti doctoris laudes intonent ient Christiani. Augustini, qui oves lapsas reduxit patri, verbo docens peccatores. Mors & vita conflixere mirando errore, mortuus dum fit vivus. Dic nobis, quo pie tanta tibi sophia? Sub ficu jacens dum flebam, tolle, lege, cantus audiebam. Ad coelicam vocem aperui codicem. Mox luxit Christus spes mea infusa veri luce serena. Credendum est magis tuae doctrinae, quam perfidorum sectae fallaci. Scimus Christum te sumsisse ad superos vere, Tu nobis Pater Dux, miserere. Amen.
units.tr: On the same: Let Christians sing the praises of the renowned teacher Augustine, who led the fallen sheep back to the Father, teaching sinners by his word. Death and life met in a wondrous conflict: he was made alive while dead. Tell us, pious one, from what wisdom came so great a gift to you? As I lay weeping beneath the fig tree, I heard a voice singing: "Take up and read." At the heavenly voice I opened the book. Straightway Christ, my hope, shone with the clear, serene light of truth poured into me. We must believe your teaching rather than the deceitful sect of the faithless. We know that Christ took you up to the heavens in truth. You, our Father and Leader, have mercy on us. Amen.

units.la: Alia: Per quem (Augustinum) sisti Christi regno ut mereamur, ipsum supplices precamur. Fac Augustine dive nos gratos maiestati piae, memor exulum. Tu Dux, tu luxque praesulum. Amen.
units.tr: Another: Through him (Augustine) we suppliants pray that we may be counted worthy to be brought into the kingdom of Christ. O divine Augustine, make us pleasing to the pious majesty, mindful of exiles. You are our Leader and the light of prelates. Amen.

units.la: ALIA:
units.tr: ANOTHER:

units.la: Lumen Doctor Augustine Apotheca medicina Nubes roris gratia Pro filiis pater ora, Aegris gratiam irrora, Cum fructu justitiae, Fac nos in fide Christi Capere, quae docuisti Tenaci memoria. Sic ut tecum sine fine Felix pater Augustine Laetemur in gloria. Amen
units.tr: Light, teacher Augustine, medicine of the storehouse, cloud of dew, grace: for your sons, Father, pray; sprinkle grace on the sick, with the fruit of righteousness. Make us, with tenacious memory, to grasp in the faith of Christ what you taught, so that, with you, happy Father Augustine, we may rejoice in glory without end. Amen.

units.la: Iterum:
units.tr: Again:

units.la: Gaude praesul Augustine: Audi nos te rogantes Et post mortem te ovantes Duc ad regna caelica.
units.tr: Rejoice, prelate Augustine: hear us who ask you, and, exulting in you after death, lead us to the heavenly kingdoms.

units.la: Q. Dē
units.tr: Q. Dē

units.la: DE TRANSLATIONE
units.tr: ON THE TRANSLATION

units.la: S. Augustini.
units.tr: OF S. AUGUSTINE.

units.la: Oratio: Deus, qui translatisti patres nostros per mare rubrum, sanctissimi tui doctoris Augustini corpus supra marinos vertices transferri voluisti, & in loco tibi placito collocari, concede quaesumus, nos de morte ad vitam transire, cujus hodie translationem celebramus.
units.tr: Prayer: O God, who led our fathers through the Red Sea, and who willed that the body of your most holy teacher Augustine be carried over the crests of the sea and laid in a place pleasing to you, grant, we beseech you, that we may pass from death to life, whose translation we today celebrate.

units.la: Complenda. Beatri patris nostri Augustini, Confessoris tui atque Pontificis, Domine, precibus confidentes, quaesumus, clementiam tuam, ut per ea, quae sumsimus, aeternae vitae remedia capiamus, cujus venerandam translationem celebramus.
units.tr: Postcommunion: Lord, trusting in the prayers of blessed Augustine, our father, your confessor and bishop, we beseech your clemency, that through the things we have received we may obtain the remedies of eternal life, whose venerable translation we celebrate.

units.la: ET EX MISSALI ROMANO.
units.tr: AND FROM THE ROMAN MISSAL.

units.la: Augustine lux Doctorum, Firmamentum Ecclesiae, Malleus haereticorum, Summum vas scientiae, Pro tuis fidelibus, Roga tuum Deum, quaesumus.
units.tr: Augustine, light of the Doctors, firmament of the Church, hammer of heretics, highest vessel of knowledge, pray to your God for your faithful, we beseech you.

units.la: DE S. LEONHARDO, EPISCOPO Lemovicensi (alii, Novicensi.)
units.tr: ON ST LEONARD, BISHOP OF LIMOGES (others say of Noyon)

units.la: 9. Novembris.
units.tr: 9 November.

units.la: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui beati Leonhardi Confessoris tui meritis & precibus, cunctis ejus auxilium invocantibus, in carceribus, seu in quibuslibet catenarum nexibus xibus constrictis, ereptionis pia remedia cō-tulisti, concede nobis, indignis famulis tuis, ut intercessione ipsius veneranda, à quacun-que molestiâ corporali, & ab omnibus vin-culis peccatorum mereamur per tuæ miseri-cordiæ solitam clementiam liberari.
units.tr: Almighty and everlasting God, who through the merits and prayers of your blessed Confessor Leonard granted the pious remedy of deliverance to all who invoke his help, whether they were held in prison or bound in any fetters of chains, grant to us, your unworthy servants, that through his venerable intercession we may deserve, by your accustomed mercy and clemency, to be freed from every bodily affliction and from all the chains of sin.

units.la: DE S. MARTINO, EPISCOPO Turonensi. 11. Novembris.
units.tr: ON ST MARTIN, BISHOP OF TOURS. 11 November.

units.la: Sacerdotem Christi Martinum, cuncta p-orbem canat Ecclesia pacis Catholica. Atqz illius nomen omnis hæreticus fugiat pavidus. Pannonia lætatur genitrix talis filii. Italia exultat alitrix tanti suvenis. Et Galliæ tri-na divisio sacro certat litigio, cujus esse de-beat præsul. Sed pariter habere se patrem omnes gaudeant, Turoni soli ejus corpus fo-veant. Huic Francorum atque Germaniæ plebs omnis plaudat. Quibus videndum invexit Dominum infuâ veste. Hic celebris est Ægypti partibus, Græciæ quoque cun-ctis sapientibus. Qui impares se Martini meritis sentiunt, atque medicamine. Nam febres sedat, dæmonesque fugat, paralytica membra glutinat, & mortuorum suâ pre-ce trium. Hic ritus sacrilegos destruxit, & ad Christi gloriam dat ignibus idola. Hic nudis mysteria brachiis conficiens, præditus est cœlesti lumine. Hic oculis ac manibus in cœlum & toris viribus suspensus, terrena cuncta respuit. Ejus ori nunquam Christus defuit, sive inscientiâ, vel quicquid ad veram vitam pertinet. Igitur te cuncti poscimus ô Martine, ut qui multa mira hic ostendisti, etiam de cœlo gratiam Christi supplicatu tuo semper infundas. Amen.
units.tr: Let the Catholic Church of peace sing of Christ's priest Martin throughout the whole world. Let every heretic flee from his name in fear. Pannonia rejoices in such a son who bore her; Italy exults in the nurse of so great a youth. And the threefold division of Gaul contends in holy strife over which of them ought to have him as its bishop. But let all rejoice that they alike have him as their father, and let Tours alone cherish his body. Let the whole people of the Franks and of Germany applaud him. He was shown to those who were to see the Lord, clothed in an unwoven garment. He is famous in the regions of Egypt, and among all the wise of Greece as well. Those who feel themselves unequal to Martin's merits are healed by his remedy. For he calms fevers and drives out demons, restores the paralysed limbs to health, and raises the dead by his prayer. He destroyed sacrilegious rites, and by his doing for the glory of Christ, idols were given to the flames. Carrying out the mysteries with bare arms, he was endowed with heavenly light. With eyes and hands lifted to heaven and suspended by the strength of his body, he spurned all earthly things. Christ was never absent from his mouth, whether in ignorance or in whatever pertains to the true life. Therefore we all beseech you, O Martin, that you who have shown here so many wonders, would also pour down the grace of Christ from heaven, by your supplication, always. Amen.

units.la: DE EODEM:
units.tr: ON THE SAME:

units.la: Martinus quoniam vota fidelium attendit, tribuens cuncta salubria, confert hic famulis, rite canentibus, stellis aureola ferra micantibus
units.tr: Since Martin attends to the prayers of the faithful, bestowing all good things, he grants them here to his servants who sing duly, gleaming with golden haloes like stars.

units.la: AD HORAS CANONICAS, IN EIUS solennitate hymnus.
units.tr: HYMN FOR THE CANONICAL HOURS, ON HIS SOLEMNITY.

units.la: Martinus autem prævius, | Hic nos per undas seculi Fac ut sit horis omnibus, | Clavo gubernet prospero, Ne Dæmonum fallacia | Ne forte nostram spumea Pes nostcr intactus ruat. | Puppim charybdis sorbeat. Hic arma nobis cœlica, | Hic nos triumpho nobili, Instante pugna conferat, | Et laureatos mystice, Hoc praliante cominus | Aptet tuis conspectibus, Hostis fugetur noxius. | Junctos supernis civibus.
units.tr: Martin, going before us, let him steer our ship with a prosperous tiller through the waves of this age, so that the deceits of demons may not overturn it, nor Charybdis with its foaming waters swallow it. In every hour, may he supply us with heavenly arms; and when battle is at hand, may he bring us to victory, that we may be crowned with laurel in his sight, joined to the heavenly citizens, while the harmful enemy is put to flight by his fighting at close quarters.

units.la: IN TRANSLATIONE S. Martini.
units.tr: AT THE TRANSLATION OF ST MARTIN.

units.la: Nos audi, tua festa colentes annua mundo celebria.
units.tr: Hear us, who celebrate your feast each year, a festival famous throughout the world.

units.la: Tu pro nobis, spes nostra, Martine, Deo supplica. Cæcis das viam : mutisque loquelam : Tu nos adjuva.
units.tr: You, Martin, our hope, pray to God for us. You give the way to the blind and speech to the dumb: help us.

units.la: Mundans immundos, qui fugas dæmonia, nos hìc libera.
units.tr: You who cleanse the unclean and drive out demons, free us here.

units.la: Qui suscitator trium mortuorum fueras, laxa nostræ mentis vincula.
units.tr: You who raised three dead men, loosen the bonds of our minds.

units.la: Qui infirma jam curasti corporum plurima, sana nostræ mentis vulnera.
units.tr: You who have already healed very many infirm bodies, heal the wounds of our minds.

units.la: Qui Christum tuâ chlamyde partitâ tectum videra snocte secundâ, fac prece, crimi-num ut solvat nobis debita, Christi gratia.
units.tr: You who saw Christ covered by your divided cloak on the second night, by your prayer may the grace of Christ loose for us the debts of our crimes.

units.la: Laus tua Christus erat, quem tota semper mente colebas, hunc pro nobis implora.
units.tr: Christ was your praise, whom you always honoured with your whole mind; implore him for us.

units.la: Ut lapsis remedia tribuat, præstans, culpis veniam, hæc precibus impetra.
units.tr: That he may grant remedies to the fallen and pardon to sins, obtain this by your prayers.

units.la: Lux super te effulsit angelica, dum libas mystica: Nos per te protegat Christi dextera.
units.tr: An angelic light shone upon you while you offered the mystical sacrifice: may the right hand of Christ protect us through you.

units.la: Mortis metam qui tuis prædixeras, nihil mortem trepidans, à morte animæ tu nos libera.
units.tr: You who foretold the end of life to your followers, fearing nothing in death, free us from the death of the soul.

units.la: Ad eundem Martyrum:
units.tr: To the same Martyr:

units.la: Mane nobiscum in æternum.
units.tr: Abide with us for ever.

units.la: DE S. NICOLAO EPISCOPO Myrensi. 6. Decembris.
units.tr: ON ST NICHOLAS, BISHOP OF MYRA. 6 December.

units.la: Credo pie, Sancte Nicolae, tuis me precibus esse salvandum: ideo ad te clamo, & te precibus meis licet indignis, pulsare non desisto.
units.tr: I piously believe, St Nicholas, that I am to be saved by your prayers. Therefore I cry out to you, and, though unworthy, I do not cease to knock at you with my prayers.

units.la: Q 3] denuo, ut te intercedente ab imminentibus periculis, à peccatis & offensionibus meis, quibus quotidie affligor, merear liberari. Salva me supplicem famulum tuum, amice Dei Nicolae, de praesentibus angustiis & tribulationibus, quia in te confidit anima mea, ut per te me salvet, qui te sibi elegit.
units.tr: again, that through your intercession I may deserve to be freed from impending dangers and from my sins and offences, by which I am afflicted every day. Save me, your suppliant servant, friend of God Nicholas, from present distresses and tribulations, because my soul trusts in you, that through you He may save me, who chose you for himself.

units.la: ETIAM:
units.tr: ALSO:

units.la: Ergo pie nos exaudi,Assistentes tua laudi,Ne subdamur hostis fraudi,Nobis fer auxilia. (di,
units.tr: Therefore, pious one, hear us, who attend upon your praise. Lest we be subjected to the enemy's deceit, bring us help.

units.la: Nos ab omni maleducas,Via recta nos conducas,Post hanc vita nos inducasAd aeterna gaudia. Amen.
units.tr: Free us from all evil. May you lead us along the straight way. After this life, lead us into eternal joys. Amen.

units.la: IN EJUSDEM LAUDEM.
units.tr: IN PRAISE OF THE SAME.

units.la: O venerande Pontifex,Pius nec tardus opifex,Cunctis, qui corde creduloTe quaerunt in periculo:
units.tr: O venerable Pontiff, pious and not slow craftsman, to all who with a believing heart seek you in danger:

units.la: Aufer mortis dispendia,Confer vitae stipendia,Quo post carnis exilia,Tecum simus in gloria.
units.tr: Take away the losses of death, bestow the rewards of life, so that after the exiles of the flesh we may be with you in glory.

units.la: ITERUM:
units.tr: AGAIN:

units.la: Plebs fidelis jucundetur,Et a Deo veneretur,Praesulis memoriaNicolai, cujus vita,Mundo fuit inaudita,Odit transitoria. &c.
units.tr: Let the faithful people rejoice, and be honoured by God: the memory of the prelate Nicholas, whose life was unheard of in the world, and who hated transitory things. etc.

units.la: Ergo pater sancte, audi,Nicolae tua laudiAstanti & impetra,Et qui te fecit beatum,Nobis prabeat ducatum,Ubi pax & gaudium, Amen.
units.tr: Therefore, holy father, hear your praises, Nicholas, standing by and obtaining them, and may He who made you blessed grant us a guide, where there is peace and joy. Amen.

units.la: ALIA.
units.tr: ANOTHER.

units.la: Nicolaus eremitaIn aeterna tenens vitaFulgentem aureolam.Gaude, quia meruistiInvenire, quem quaesisti,
units.tr: Nicholas the hermit, holding in eternal life a shining aureole. Rejoice, because you have deserved to find him whom you sought,

units.la: In coelo Empyro.Ejus namque celsitudo,Et amoena pulchritudo,Sub solari radio Assumendo te locavit,Collaudando approbavitVitam tuam regulam.
units.tr: in the heaven of the Empyrean. For his loftiness and lovely beauty, under the sun's ray, taking you up, has placed you; praising, he has approved your life as the rule.

units.la: Regem celsa majestatisOra Pater, cum beatisNobis ut det patriam.
units.tr: Pray, Father, to the King of lofty majesty with the blessed, that he may give us the fatherland.

units.la: ALIA:
units.tr: ANOTHER:

units.la: Iam à fine seculorumVita duce & lumen morumNicolaum providisti.Nicolaus verus FraterVere bonus noster PaterHodie resplenduit, &c.Salus, lux & refugiumEt morborum simul omniumCurator eximius.Caci vident, claudi pergunt,In pfundu mala merguntPu per hunc cœlibem.Audiunt surdi, muti fantur,Mortui surgunt, & lataturHoc divino munere.Omnes gentes accurrite,Et devota mente quarite,
units.tr: Now from the end of the ages, Life as leader and light of conduct, you have provided Nicholas. Nicholas, true brother, truly good our Father, shines forth today, etc. Salvation, light and refuge, and at once the outstanding healer of all diseases. The blind see, the lame walk, evils are plunged into the depths through this celibate. The deaf hear, the mute speak, the dead rise and rejoice at this divine gift. All peoples, run together, and seek with a devout mind.

units.la: Ex hoc fonte remedium.Ite pii, simul quariteEt quarendo inardesciteNicolai laudibus.Ille noster est patronusPius pater, pastor bonus,Et pietatis formula.Ille noster est protector,Gloriosus & effector,Per cuncta pericula.Nicolae pastor bone,Dulcis pater, & patrone,In Christo viventium.Tu nos rege, nos guberna,Ducens tecum ad aeternaParadisi gaudia. Amen.
units.tr: A remedy from this fountain. Go, pious ones, seek together, and in seeking burn with the praises of Nicholas. He is our patron, pious father, good shepherd, and model of piety. He is our protector, glorious and deliverer through all dangers. Good shepherd Nicholas, sweet father and patron of those living in Christ, rule us, govern us, leading us with you to the joys of paradise. Amen.

units.la: ORATIO.
units.tr: PRAYER.

units.la: DEus, qui beatum Nicolaum confessorem tuum, sanctimonia sacræ religionis insignem, miraculis magnis clarificare non desinis; concede propitius, ut, qui ejus patrocinia devote poscimus, dono tuæ gratiæ consequamur.
units.tr: O God, who never cease to glorify your confessor, blessed Nicholas, distinguished for the holiness of sacred religion, with great miracles: graciously grant that we, who devoutly seek his patronage, may obtain it by the gift of your grace.

units.la: DE SS. DOCTORIBUS.
units.tr: ON THE HOLY DOCTORS.

units.la: DE S. ANTONIO.
units.tr: ON ST ANTHONY.

units.la: 17. Januarii.
units.tr: 17 January.

units.la: Deus, qui nobis obtentu beati Antonii Confessoris tui, morbidum ignem extingui, & membris ægris refrigeria præstari concedis, fac nos propitius ipsius meritis & precibus à gehennæ incendiis liberatos, integros mente & corpore tibi feliciter in gloriâ præsentari.
units.tr: O God, who grant us, through the intercession of blessed Anthony your Confessor, that the fire of disease is quenched and relief is given to sick limbs, mercifully grant that, by his merits and prayers, we may be freed from the fires of hell and presented to you in glory, whole in mind and body.

units.la: Graduale: Felix corpus & felix anima, felix virtus Sancti Antonii, cujus nomen collaudant omnia, & venerantur gentes & populi. Flammas ignis, Orci incendia mox suffocat victor Dæmonii. Tua prece, laude, & gloriâ nos copula sanctorum cœtui. Halleluja.
units.tr: Gradual: Happy the body and happy the soul, happy the virtue of Saint Anthony, whose name all things praise, and whom nations and peoples venerate. The victor over the demon soon quenches the flames of fire and the burnings of hell. By your prayer, praise and glory, join us to the company of the saints. Alleluia.

units.la: Prosa:
units.tr: Prose:

units.la: Antonius humilis, Sanctitate nobilis, Afflictorum gloria. Cum sanctorum cœtibus, Fulget in cœlestibus, Sublimi victoria. Charisui merito, More Christus solito, Consolatur omnia. Data sibi gratia Per secula spatia Facta est prænuncia. Ferens ejulatibus, Igne perennibus, Expectata gaudia. Felix ejus anima, Linquens orbis infima, Carne jam depositâ, Christum est intuita. &c. Hunc patrator deprecetur, Ut per illum condonetur Quod mens timet conscia. Laus & honor illi datur, Satis ex se commendatur, Operum per merita.
units.tr: Anthony, humble and noble in holiness, the glory of the afflicted. With the companies of the saints he shines in heaven, with a lofty victory. By the merit of his grace, as Christ does by custom, he comforts all things. Given grace for every span of ages, he was made a foretelling of it. Bearing up those who wail for the everlasting fires, he is the awaited joy. Happy is his soul, leaving the lowest parts of the world, now that the flesh is laid aside, and beholding Christ. &c. Let the one who performs this intercede, so that through him what the conscious mind fears may be forgiven. Praise and honour are given to him, and he is sufficiently commended by his own works and merits.

units.la: DeDamonia vincit iste, Et concedis illi Christe Semper esse subdita. Veneretur hic patronus, Qui coelestis habet thronus Qui dando beneficia, Mundum replet laetitia. Hic divinum dans odorem, Pestem pellit & languore, Velut rosa vel lilia Redolet Ecclesia. O Antoni Dei verna, Mundi jubar, & lucerna, Apud Christi gregei istum Clementer concilia. Ut fons summa pietatis, Nos mundatos a peccatis, Ad superna claritatis Perducat concilia. Amen dicant omnia.
units.tr: This man conquers the demon, and you, Christ, grant that he always be subject to him. Let this patron be venerated, who has a heavenly throne, who fills the world with joy by bestowing benefits. Giving a divine fragrance here, he drives out plague and sickness, and the Church gives off a scent like roses or lilies. O Anthony, spring-born of God, light and lamp of the world, graciously bring this one together with Christ's flock. May the highest fountain of piety, having cleansed us from sins, lead us to the councils of heavenly brightness. Let all say Amen.

units.la: Secreta: Sacrificium nostrum, quaesumus Domine, benignus intende, quod sicut beati Antonii precibus, cruciatus temporales sanare non desinis: ita erui misericorditer impetremus ab aeternis.
units.tr: Secret: Look kindly, we beseech you, Lord, upon our sacrifice, so that, just as by the prayers of blessed Anthony you never cease to heal temporal sufferings, so we may obtain to be mercifully delivered from eternal ones.

units.la: ALIVD:
units.tr: ANOTHER:

units.la: Antoni, compar inclyte Nostri quondam itineris Tu nobis adhuc miseris In patria jam praedite, Te glorioso comite Nos ora frui superis.
units.tr: Anthony, illustrious companion of our former journey, you who are still in the homeland and already endowed with it, pray that we wretched ones may enjoy the heights above, with you as our glorious companion.

units.la: GRADVALE:
units.tr: GRADUAL:

units.la: O Patriarcha pauperum, Antoni, tuis precibus Auge tuorum numerum In charitate Christi, Quos flagellatos corpore, Sanare consuevisti. Antoni, pastor inclyte, Qui cruciatus reficis, Morbos sanas & destruis, Ignis calorem extinguis, Pie pater, ad Dominum Ora pro nobis miserus.
units.tr: O Patriarch of the poor, Anthony, by your prayers increase the number of your people in the charity of Christ, whom you were accustomed to heal when they were scourged in body. Anthony, illustrious minister, who restores those in torment, heals and destroys diseases, quenches the heat of fire, holy father, pray to the Lord for us, who are wretched.

units.la: Post communionem: Prosit nobis, quaesumus Domine, ad salutem sacri muneris oblatio, per quam beati Antonii fulti suffragio, exemplo ipsius, omnia tela nequissimi ignea extinguentes, Sanctorum mereamur adjungi consortio.
units.tr: Post-communion: May the offering of this holy gift, we beseech you, Lord, be profitable to us for salvation, so that, supported by the intercession of blessed Anthony and following his example, quenching all the fiery darts of the most wicked one, we may deserve to be joined to the fellowship of the saints.

units.la: DE S. HIERONYMO.
units.tr: ON ST JEROME.

units.la: 30. Septembris.
units.tr: 30 September.

units.la: GRADVALE.
units.tr: GRADUAL.

units.la: O robur Ecclesia, Mundi lux Hieronyme Iubar sapientia, Salva nos juvamine, Forma sanctitatis, Doctor veritatis. Hallel.
units.tr: O strength of the Church, light of the world, Jerome, radiant wisdom, save us with your help, form of holiness, teacher of truth. Alleluia.

units.la: VERSUS:
units.tr: VERSES:

units.la: Tu lucerna viatorum Es Hieronyme beate, In candelabro doctorum Speculum & decus rite, Assis nobis alme pater Contra hostes, praesul vitae. Hallel.
units.tr: You, blessed Jerome, are the lamp of travellers, and in the candlestick of teachers the mirror and proper ornament. Kind father, stand by us against our enemies, bishop of life. Alleluia.

units.la: VERSUS.
units.tr: VERSES.

units.la: Aureo candelabro fulgens gloriosa lucerna, Doctrinae rutilans Hieronyme sede superna, Ad te clamantes, mundo lux, sal terrae, guberna.
units.tr: Shining lamp, glorious on the golden candlestick, Jerome gleaming with doctrine from your seat on high, light of the world, salt of the earth, guide us who cry out to you.

units.la: SEQUENTIA.
units.tr: SEQUENCE.

units.la: In profundo tenebrarum | Baptista cibis diris Mundo fulsit fidus clarum | Socius in gloria. &c. Magnus vir Hieronymus, | Deitas per egregia Parent hunc videntes, | Hieronymi suffragia Salvi sunt voventes, | Nos ducat ad caelestia. Surgunt morientes, | Tortiora dextra porrige, Fama claret vivis, | Hieronyme nos corrige, Apostolis summus viris | Et recto calle dirige. Aequant privilegia. | Amen.
units.tr: In the depths of darkness the Baptist, the faithful one, shone as a bright light for the world, a companion in glory, etc. Great man Jerome, divine through outstanding deeds, those who see him and the parents who vow to Jerome's help are saved; may he lead us to the heavenly things. The dying rise; stretch out your right hand more firmly. Fame shines on the living; Jerome, correct us, highest among apostles and men, and direct us along the straight path. They match the privileges. Amen.

units.la: Offertorium : O vir ineffabilis, virtutum vas admirabile, ô diadema honoris & gloriæ, angularis lapis firmissimus, exemplarinno- centiæ, columna aurea, & totius Ecclesiæ fundamentum, cum plus tanderis, minùs confunderis.
units.tr: Offertory: O man beyond words, admirable vessel of virtues, O diadem of honour and glory, most firm corner stone, pattern of innocence, golden column and foundation of the whole Church: the more you are exalted, the less you are put to shame.

units.la: Vale igitur, Hieronyme gloriose, nostram semper apud Deum faciens memoriam, ut tuâ valeamus piissimâ intercessione, & in præsenti ab omnibus protegi periculis, & in futuro, gaudia, quæ tu jam possides, adipisci.
units.tr: Farewell, then, glorious Jerome, always keeping our memory before God, so that by your most loving intercession we may be protected from all dangers in the present and obtain in the future the joys you already possess.

units.la: Complenda: Paternis intercessionibus almifici confessoris Hieronymi ac Doctoris magnifici, angelicis refectidelicis, supplicter, Domine, deprecamur, ut Ecclesia tua nunquam destituatur auxiliis, quam ejus- dem decorasti meritis & doctrinis.
units.tr: Closing prayer: By the paternal intercessions of the gentle confessor Jerome and the magnificent Doctor, refreshed with angelic delights, we humbly beseech you, O Lord, that your Church may never be left without help, she whom you have adorned with his merits and teachings.

units.la: Alibi. Subvenias tristi populo, Hieronyme, Christi doctor & amice, tu fons nitidissimæ linguæ.
units.tr: Elsewhere: Come to the aid of the sorrowing people, Jerome, teacher and friend of Christ, you fountain of most bright eloquence.

units.la: Præsta, quæsumus Domine, ut, cujus venerandam memoriam agimus, ejus semper & erudiamur, doctrinis, & meritis adjuvemur.
units.tr: Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that we, who celebrate his venerable memory, may always be instructed by his teachings and aided by his merits.

units.la: DE PONTIFICIBUS.
units.tr: ON THE PONTIFFS.

units.la: DE UNO PONTIFICE.
units.tr: ON ONE PONTIFF.

units.la: Pastor bone, miserere Ecclesiæ, tuisque precibus refice. Confer opem plebi tuæ, preces intende, & pio juvamine maculas dique. In via nos adjuva, colloca in patria, & redde quae speramus bona. Amen.
units.tr: Good shepherd, have mercy on the Church, and restore her by your prayers. Bring help to your people, give heed to their prayers, and by your holy assistance wipe away our stains. Help us on the way, place us in the fatherland, and grant the good things we hope for. Amen.

units.la: DE S. LIBERIO, CONTRA CALCULUM.
units.tr: Concerning Saint Liberius, against the stone

units.la: Deus, qui beatum Liberium, Pontificem tuum, innumeris gloriosum miraculis, speciali in medendis arenarum & calculi passionibus privilegio decoratsi, praesta quaesumus, ut ipsius meritis & intercessione, ab his aliisque malis eruti, gaudiis perfrui merearmur aeternis.
units.tr: O God, who adorned blessed Liberius, your Bishop, glorious with countless miracles and with a special privilege of healing the sufferings of gravel and the stone, grant, we beseech you, that by his merits and intercession, delivered from these and other evils, we may deserve to enjoy eternal joys.

units.la: DE ABBATIBUS.
units.tr: CONCERNING ABBOTS.

units.la: Intercessio nos, quaesumus Domine, beati N. Abbatis commendet, ut, quod nostris meritis non valemus, ejus patrocinio assequamur. Da supplicanti coetui, | Proinde te, piissime, Obtentu hujus optimi, | Precamur omnes supplices, Remissionem criminum, | Ut hujus almi gratia Rupendo nexu vinculi, &c. | Nobis remittas debita.
units.tr: May the intercession of blessed N., the Abbot, commend us, we beseech you, O Lord, so that what we cannot obtain by our own merits we may obtain by his patronage. Grant to this suppliant assembly: therefore, most merciful one, we all pray as suppliants, through the intercession of this most excellent man, for the remission of our sins; that by the grace of this kindly man, with the bond of chains broken, etc., you would forgive us our debts.

units.la: DE S. GOTHARDO, ABBATE Hirsfeldensi. 26. Martii.
units.tr: Concerning St Gotthard, Abbot of Hirsfeld. 26 March.

units.la: Opem nobis praesul bone | Et nos salva in agone Fer in nostris angustiis, | Ab aeternis supplicus.
units.tr: Good prelate, bring us help, and save us in our agony. Bring it into our distresses, we who suppliantly pray to be saved from the eternal (punishments).

units.la: DE S. BERNHARDO ABBATE CLAREVALLENSI, 20. Maji.
units.tr: Concerning St Bernard, Abbot of Clairvaux, 20 May.

units.la: O alme pater Bernharde, & ardentissime amator, cultor suavitatis, & mellifluæ dulcedinis Dei, qui es spes & solatium omnium ad te clamantium, corde toto tuæ sanctæ protectioni me commendo, propter excellentiam meritorum tuorum, ut ab omnibus, quæ contraria sunt animæ meæ, tueri me digneris.
units.tr: O kindly father Bernard, most ardent lover and cultivator of the sweetness and honey-flowing delight of God, who are the hope and comfort of all who cry out to you, I commend myself with my whole heart to your holy protection, on account of the excellence of your merits, that you would deign to shield me from all things that are contrary to my soul.

units.la: Intercessio nos, quæsumus Domine, beati Bernhardi Abbatis commendet, ut, quod meritis nostris non valemus, ejus patrocinio assequamur.
units.tr: Let the intercession of blessed Bernard, Abbot, commend us, we beseech you, O Lord, so that what we cannot obtain by our own merits we may obtain through his patronage.

units.la: DE MONACHIS.
units.tr: ON MONKS.

units.la: DE S. BENEDICTO. 7. Maji.
units.tr: ON ST BENEDICT. 7 May.

units.la: Precatio Monachorum Florinensium, ad sepulchrum Benedicti, cujus reliquias furanti erant:
units.tr: Prayer of the Monks of Florinus, at the tomb of Benedict, whose relics they were stealing:

units.la: O Benedicte, unica spes nostra post Deum, ne derelinquas nos orphanos, qui huc, non nostris meritis, sed pro multorum salute, venisti.
units.tr: O Benedict, our only hope after God, do not leave us orphans, you who came here not for our merits but for the salvation of many.

units.la: Preces ardentissimæ Monachorum Benedicti ordinis, ad Patronum, cum Abbas Monasterii Vinum liberet generosissimum, at Fratribus sitientibus proprium austerum & tenuem curaret. Abbas cum Priore | Fratres de pejore, Bibit de meliore, | O Benedicte respice.
units.tr: Most fervent prayers of the monks of the Benedictine order to their patron, when the abbot of the monastery was pouring out the most generous wine, but was keeping the thin, sour wine for the thirsty brothers. The abbot with the prior, the brothers get the worse; he drinks the better. O Benedict, look upon us.

units.la: DE S. ONOPHRIO. 10. Junii.
units.tr: ON ST ONOPHRIUS. 10 June.

units.la: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui beatissimo Confessori tuo Onophrio tantæ fidei constantiam donasti, ut pro tuo amore gloriam & vitam caducam despiceret, & famem ac sitim, etiam nuditatem indeserto patienter sustinuit, præsta, quæsumus, ejus nos precibus adjuvari, ut mundi hujus tentationibus illæsi, transire valeamus, & ad gloriam regni tui ipso intercedente pervenire mereamur.
units.tr: Almighty, eternal God, who gave your most blessed confessor Onophrius such constancy of faith that for love of you he despised glory and fleeting life, and patiently endured hunger, thirst and even nakedness in the wilderness, grant, we pray, that we may be aided by his prayers, so that, unharmed by the temptations of this world, we may pass through them and, by his intercession, deserve to attain the glory of your kingdom.

units.la: DE S. FRANCISCO. 4. Octobris.
units.tr: ON ST FRANCIS. 4 October.

units.la: O Francisce, lux solaris, | Prode Christo stigmata. Crucifixus singularis, | Ora pro tuis famulis, Jam cum Christo gloriaris | Ut rapti ex miseriis In choro coelestium. | Tecum laudemus dulciter Tu sis nobis vita via, | Trinitatem perennIter. Tu pro nobis semper pia
units.tr: O Francis, solar light, who for Christ bore the stigmata, singularly crucified, pray for your servants. Now you are glorified with Christ, that we, snatched from miseries, may be in the choir of the heavenly ones. Let us praise the Trinity sweetly with you forever. Be for us life and way; always devoted, pray for us.

units.la: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui Ecclesiam tuam variis sanctorum meritis semper illuminas, protegis & confervas, concede ut beati Francisci & Sanctorum sequentiu, cum intercessione, & hic ab omnibus mundemur offensis, & in futuro cœlesti gloria perfruamur.
units.tr: Almighty, eternal God, who always illuminate, protect and preserve your Church through the various merits of the saints, grant that through the intercession of blessed Francis and the saints who follow him, we may here be cleansed from all offences and in the future enjoy heavenly glory.

units.la: Alia oratio: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui frigescente mundo, ad inflammandum corda nostra, in carne beatissimi patris nostri Francisci, passionis tuæ sacra stigmata renovasti: concede propitius, ut ejus meritis & precibus dignos fructus pœnitentiæ faciamus. O patriarcha pauperum Francisce tuis precibus Auge tuorum numerum In charitate Christi. Quos cancellatis manibus Caecutiens, ut moriens Iacob benedixisti.
units.tr: Another prayer: Almighty, eternal God, who, when the world had grown cold, renewed in the flesh of our most blessed father Francis the sacred stigmata of your passion, in order to kindle our hearts, graciously grant that by his merits and prayers we may bring forth worthy fruits of repentance. O Francis, patriarch of the poor, by your prayers increase the number of your people in the charity of Christ, whom, blind, with crossed hands, you blessed as Jacob did when dying.

units.la: Hic Franciscus pauper & modicus, coelum dives ingreditur, hymnis caelestibus honoratur.
units.tr: This Francis, poor and humble, enters heaven rich, and is honoured with heavenly hymns.

units.la: Ex libro Conformitatum, Franciscanorum: Francisce Jesu Typice, Dux normaque Minorum, Sedes nobis perpetuè. Da regni coelotum.
units.tr: From the book of the Conformities of the Franciscans: O Francis, type of Jesus, leader and rule of the Minorites, be for us a seat forever; give us the kingdom of heaven.

units.la: DE S. BONAVENTURA, SERAPHICO, Ordinis Franciscanorum.
units.tr: ON SAINT BONAVENTURE, THE SERAPHIC, OF THE ORDER OF FRANCISCANS.

units.la: O praesul dignissime Bonaventura doctor inclyte, audi servulos tuos, ut possideat gaudia beatorum perenniter in patria. Tecu. Hall.
units.tr: O most worthy prelate Bonaventure, illustrious teacher, hear your little servants, that they may possess the joys of the blessed forever in the fatherland. Pray with us. Hallelujah.

units.la: DE EREMITIS.
units.tr: Concerning Hermits.

units.la: DE S. GALLO. 16. Octobris.
units.tr: Concerning St. Gall, 16 October.

units.la: Quaesumus mundi fator & redemptor, ut sacris ejus precibus tueri hanc velis plebem, tribuens, quod optat corde benigno.
units.tr: We beseech you, Maker and Redeemer of the world, that by his holy prayers you would be pleased to protect this people, granting what he desires with a kindly heart.

units.la: DE ELEEMOSYNARIIS.
units.tr: Concerning Almsgivers.

units.la: Collecta: Deus, cujus misericordiae non est numerus, suscipe propitius preces humilitatis nostrae, & animabus, quae nobis in oratione commendatae sunt, & quorum utimur eleemosynis vel usi sumus, quibus tui nominis dedisti confessionem, cunctorum remissionem tribue peccatorum.
units.tr: Collect: O God, whose mercy has no measure, graciously receive the prayers of our lowliness, and grant the forgiveness of all sins to the souls who have been commended to us in prayer, and whose alms we use or have used, and to whom you have given the confession of your name.

units.la: Secreta: Prosit, quæsumus Domine, hæc sancta præsentis sacrificii oblatio animabus, quæ nobis in orationem commendatæ sunt, & quarum utimur eleemosynis, vel usi sumus, ut per nomen sanctum tuum à perpetuis cruciatibus ereptæ, translatum in requiem habere mereantur æternam.
units.tr: Secret: We beseech you, Lord, that this holy offering of the present sacrifice may profit the souls who have been commended to us in prayer, and whose alms we use or have used, so that, delivered through your holy name from everlasting torments, they may be deemed worthy to possess rest eternal.

units.la: DE ALIIS SANCTIS.
units.tr: ON OTHER SAINTS.

units.la: Aurelium Armenium Nottingus Vercellensis Episcopus sic invocat:
units.tr: Nottingus, Bishop of Vercelli, invokes Aurelius Armenius thus:

units.la: Aureli, decus meum atque unicum post Deum animæ præsidium meæ, tibi expando desiderium famuli tui, quod Deo conjunctus proculdubio nescire non potes. Rogo te, per divinum amorem, qui te mihi venerabilem, Ecclesiæ celebrem, ægris medicum, unumque cum Deo Sanctum & immortalem effecit, ne me diutius in hoc ambiguo fluctuare permittas: sed exaudi me famulum tibi prostratum, & doce me, ut sciam, quid agere debeam secundum Dei tuamque voluntatem.
units.tr: Aurelius, my glory and, after God, the one and only protection of my soul, I lay open to you the longing of your servant, which you, being joined to God, cannot doubt you know. I beg you, by the divine love which made you venerable to me, renowned to the Church, a physician to the sick, and holy and immortal, one with God, not to let me waver any longer in this uncertainty; but hear me, your servant, prostrate before you, and teach me what I ought to do according to the will of God and of yourself.

units.la: DE OMNIBVS SANCTIS.
units.tr: ON ALL SAINTS.

units.la: Majestatem tuam, Domine, supplicites deprecamur, ut, sicut nos jugiter omnium sanctorum tuorum commemoratione lætificas: ita semper supplicatione defendas.
units.tr: We humbly beseech your majesty, O Lord, that as you constantly gladden us with the remembrance of all your saints, so you may always defend us with their intercession.

units.la: Omnes sancti tui, quæsumus Domine, nos ubiq; adjuvent, ut, dum eorum merita recolimus, patrocinia sentiamus, & pace tuam nostris concede temporibus.
units.tr: May all your saints, we pray, O Lord, help us everywhere, so that while we call their merits to mind, we may feel their patronage, and grant your peace to our times.

units.la: DE SANCTIS COMMENTITIIS.
units.tr: ON THE FABULOUS SAINTS.

units.la: DE S. GEORGIO.
units.tr: ON ST GEORGE.

units.la: 23. Aprillis.
units.tr: 23 April.

units.la: Ut Latii Martem, sic nos te dive Georgi Nunc colimus:
units.tr: As the Latins worshipped Mars, so now we worship you, divine George.

units.la: Et: Maxime bellorum rector, quem nostra juventus pro Mavorte colit.
units.tr: And: Greatest ruler of wars, whom our youth worships in place of Mars.

units.la: DE EODEM:
units.tr: ON THE SAME:

units.la: O victor insignis.
units.tr: O distinguished victor,

units.la: Athleta mirabilis,
units.tr: wondrous athlete,

units.la: Tormentis variis
units.tr: tormented in various ways

units.la: Versans septem annis,
units.tr: for seven years,

units.la: Ut elegit Sanctus
units.tr: as the holy one chose,

units.la: Jacet Georgius
units.tr: George lies

units.la: Ense trucidatus.
units.tr: slain by the sword.

units.la: Nunc humili prece, melodiis suavibus, cuncti flagitemus, ut nobis veniam erga Jesum Christum obtineat. Amen.
units.tr: Now let us all implore with humble prayer and sweet melodies that he may obtain pardon for us from Jesus Christ. Amen.

units.la: Hic nos salvet a peccatis,
units.tr: May he save us from sins,

units.la: Ut in coelorum beatis
units.tr: so that among the blessed of heaven

units.la: Possimus quiescere.
units.tr: we may rest.

units.la: DE S. CRIHSTOPHORO.
units.tr: ON ST CHRISTOPHER.

units.la: 25. Julii.
units.tr: 25 July.

units.la: Christophori sancti speciem quicunque tuetur,
units.tr: Whoever gazes upon the image of St Christopher

units.la: Illo nempe die nullo languore tenetur.
units.tr: is on that very day held by no sickness.

units.la: AD EUNDEM:
units.tr: TO THE SAME:

units.la: O gloriose martyr Christophore, sis mee-
units.tr: O glorious martyr Christopher, be my

units.la: R [illegible, ~1 letter] mor nostri ad Deum, omni hora, & tuere fine mora, corpus,sensum & honorem confer-va, qui cœli florem meruisti hic portare inter ulnas ultra mare, nos per tantam dignitatem fac vitare pravitatem, & amare corde toto Deum verum laude, voto, prae cunctis mundanis istis, ut post mundi hujus tristis blandimentis, te praesente pducamur ad cœli regnū.
units.tr: intercessor with God at every hour, and without delay guard body, senses and honour. You who deserved to carry the flower of heaven in your arms here across the sea, by such great dignity make us avoid wickedness, and make us love the true God with our whole heart, with praise and vow, above all these worldly things, so that after the sad allurements of this world, with you present, we may be led to the kingdom of heaven.

units.la: De eodem. Deus, qui beatum Chriftophorum martyrem tuum virtute constantiae in passione roboratsi, concede propitius, ut qui ejus commemorationem agimus, ipsius meritis & precibus ab omni languore corporis & animae praeservemur, atq; ad gaudia aeterna feliciter perducamur.
units.tr: Also: Holy Christopher, martyr of Jesus Christ, who suffered punishments for the name of Christ, bring help to the wretched, and you who merited the kingdoms of heavenly light from this sad world, etc.

units.la: Item: Sancte Christophore, Martyr Jesu Christi, Qui pro Christi nomine Poenas pertulisti, Opem confer miseris, Atque mundo tristi Qui coelestis luminis Regna meruisti. &c.
units.tr: Likewise: Holy Christopher, martyr of Jesus Christ, who suffered punishments for the name of Christ, bring help to the wretched, and you who deserved the kingdoms of heavenly light to a sorrowful world. etc.

units.la: ET: O martyr Christophore, pro salvatoris honore, Fac nos mente fore dignos Deitatis favore, Et promissione Christi, quia quod petis, obtinuisti. Da populo tristi bona, qua moriendo petisti, Confer solamen mentis, & tolle gravamen Judicis examen fac mite sit in omnibus.
units.tr: AND: O martyr Christopher, for the honour of the Saviour, make us worthy of the favour of the Deity, and by the promise of Christ, since you have obtained what you asked. Give the sorrowful people the good things you sought by dying, bring comfort of mind and take away the burden; make the Judge's examination gentle in all things.

units.la: Amen.
units.tr: Amen.

units.la: DE TRIBUS REGIBUS.
units.tr: ABOUT THE THREE KINGS.

units.la: 6. Januarii.
units.tr: 6 January.

units.la: Concede proiptius, ut per horum trium Magorum pias intercessiones & merita, nobis famulis tuis tribuas, ut itinere, quo iturí sumus, celeritate, lætitiâ, gratiâ & pace, negotioq; bene peracto, te ipso sole vero, vera stella, & verâ luminis luce, ad loca destinata, cum omni prosperitate, ad ipsorum cœlesti- umq; civium consortia, salvi ac sani redire va-leamus.
units.tr: Graciously grant that, through the pious intercessions and merits of these three Magi, you may give us your servants speed, joy, grace and peace on the journey we are about to undertake. Once our business is well completed, may we be able to return safe and sound, with all prosperity, to the places appointed for us and to the fellowship of their heavenly citizens, with you as the true sun, the true star, and the true light of light.

units.la: Ex veteri testamento.
units.tr: From the Old Testament.

units.la: DE S. IOB O.
units.tr: Concerning St Job.

units.la: SEQUENTIA: Sancti Job clara merita | Permissione Domini Mater promat Ecclesia, | Gravi percussº vulnere. Qui plenus sacri muneris | Vir innocens & justa Extat ab annis teneris. | Veniam tua prece Ablatis bonis seculi | Obtine, perpetuis Et liberis, à daemone, | Tecum da frui gaudiis.
units.tr: Sequence: Let the Church duly proclaim the illustrious merits of holy Job, who was struck with a grievous wound by the Lord's permission. He was a man innocent and just, who from his tender years was full of holy office. By your prayer, obtain pardon for us, who have been stripped of worldly goods, and grant that we may be freed from the devil for ever, and may with you enjoy the everlasting joys.

units.la: Secreta: Suscipe Domine, propitius hostius, quibus beati Job meritis te placari voluisti, & nobis salutem corporis & animæ potenti pietate restitui.
units.tr: Secret: Receive, O Lord, graciously these offerings, by whose merits you were pleased to be appeased through blessed Job, and by your mighty mercy restore to us health of body and soul.

units.la: DE XIIII. AUXILIATORIBUS,
units.tr: ON THE FOURTEEN HELPERS,

units.la: (Rothelffer) qui sint.
units.tr: (Rothelffer) who they are.

units.la: 1. Valentinus. 2. Otilia. 3. Apollonia. 4. Nicolaus & Christophorus. 5. Sebastianus & Rochus. 6. Florianus & Agatha.
units.tr: 1. Valentine. 2. Ottilia. 3. Apollonia. 4. Nicholas and Christopher. 5. Sebastian and Roch. 6. Florian and Agatha.

units.la: tha. 7. Urbanus. 8. Petronella. 9. Leonhar-dus. 10. Margareta. 11. Gallus. 12. Wendeli-nus. 13. Eulogius. 14. Pelagius. Inter sanctos Deo gratos, | Ad se Deus nos clamantes, Adjutores vos beatos | Per vos salvet fluctuantes, Praedicat Ecclesia, | In valle miseriae.
units.tr: 7. Urban. 8. Petronella. 9. Leonard. 10. Margaret. 11. Gall. 12. Wendelin. 13. Eulogius. 14. Pelagius. Among the saints who are pleasing to God, you blessed helpers, God saves us as we call upon him, and through you he saves us as we are tossed by the waves; the Church proclaims this in the valley of misery.

units.la: Conditor & redemtor generis humani, exaudi me indignum famulum tuum, ut per sanctorum merita & interventum, deleas omnes iniquitates meas, cunctaque bona cordi meo inferas, mores bonos & continentiam linguae, charitatem, atque humilitatem, caeterasque omnes virtutes.
units.tr: Creator and Redeemer of the human race, hear me, your unworthy servant, so that through the merits and intercession of the saints you may blot out all my iniquities and bring into my heart every good thing: good morals, restraint of the tongue, charity, humility, and all the other virtues.

units.la: ET:
units.tr: AND:

units.la: Da, ut omnis, qui in suis necessitatibus eorum implorat auxilium, secundum promissionis tuae gratiam, petitionis suae salutarem consequatur effectum.
units.tr: Grant that everyone who implores their help in his needs may obtain, according to the grace of your promise, the saving effect of his petition.

units.la: SANCTÆ MARTYRES. DE VIRGINE ET MARTYRE.
units.tr: Holy Martyrs. Concerning a Virgin and Martyr.

units.la: Indulgentiam nobis, quaesumus, Domine, beata N. virgo & martyr imploret.
units.tr: May the blessed virgin and martyr N. obtain for us, we beseech you, Lord, an indulgence.

units.la: DE S. AGNETE.
units.tr: Concerning St Agnes.

units.la: 21. Januarii. Ave Agnes gloriosa, | Charitate da perfectâ Me in fide serves rectâ | Deum, per quem es electa, Dulcis virgo & dilecta | Colere pie omnibus. Te exoro precibus.
units.tr: 21 January. Hail, glorious Agnes: grant me perfect charity, and keep me upright in the true faith, to worship God, through whom you were chosen, sweet and beloved virgin, to be devout toward all. I entreat you with prayers.

units.la: Deus, qui beatam Agnetem, virginem tu- am, castitatis amore decorafti, & flammis tra- ditam illæsam confervafti, da nobis, quæsu- mus, ejus meritis & precibus, ejusdem casti- tatis tenore fulciri, & ab omni vitiorum æstu liberari.
units.tr: O God, who adorned the blessed Agnes, your virgin, with the love of chastity, and preserved her unharmed when she was given over to the flames, grant us, we beseech you, by her merits and prayers, to be strengthened by the same firmness of chastity, and to be freed from every heat of vice.

units.la: Et: Apud quem nunc intercedat, ut cœli nobis concedat intrare palatium.
units.tr: And: May she now intercede with him, that he may grant us to enter the palace of heaven.

units.la: DE S. AGATHA.
units.tr: ON ST. AGATHA.

units.la: 5. Februarii.
units.tr: 5 February.

units.la: Jam retinens quasi sponsa polo Pro miseris supplicaDomino, Sic sua festa coli faciat, Celebrantibus ut faveat.
units.tr: Now, already held in heaven as a bride, she pleads for the wretched with the Lord, that he may make her feast be kept and may favour those who celebrate it.

units.la: DE S. DOROTHEA.
units.tr: Concerning St. Dorothea.

units.la: 6. Februarii.
units.tr: 6 February.

units.la: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, in cujus no- mine gloriosa virgo martyr Dorothea cuncta genera tormentorum superavit, supplicitér te exoramus, ut ejus interventu cuncta peri- cula vincamus, ipsamq; in omnibus necessi- tatibus celerem adjutricem nobis sentiamus.
units.tr: Almighty and everlasting God, in whose name the glorious virgin and martyr Dorothea overcame every kind of torment, we humbly beseech you that, through her intercession, we may overcome all dangers and find her a swift helper to us in all our necessities.

units.la: DE S. APOLLONIA.
units.tr: CONCERNING ST APOLLONIA.

units.la: 11. Februarii.
units.tr: 11 February.

units.la: Virgo Christi egregia | Ne pro reatu criminum, Pro nobis Apollonia. | Morbo vexemur dentium; Funde preces ad Do- | Sed sanitate capitis minum. | Gratulemur & corporis. Ut tollat omne | noxium. R3. Æter-
units.tr: Distinguished virgin of Christ, Apollonia, pray for us. Let us not be vexed by toothache, but let us also be well in head and body. Pour out prayers to the Lord that he may take away every harm. R3. Æter-

units.la: Æterne ac mitissime Deus, concede propitius, ut qui beatæ & gloriosæ virginis ac Martyris Apolloniæ, (quam in excussis pro tui nominis confessione dentibus, de morte acerbissima triumphare fecisti) memoriam recolimus, ut ejus meritis & precibus, à dolore dentium, & ab omni languore corporis, & animæ protegi & eripi mereamur.
units.tr: Eternal and most gentle God, graciously grant that we, who call to mind the memory of the blessed and glorious virgin and martyr Apollonia (whom, after her teeth were knocked out for confessing your name, you made triumph in a most bitter death), may through her merits and prayers be worthy to be protected and delivered from toothache, from every affliction of body, and from every ailment of soul.

units.la: DE S. MARGARETA.
units.tr: CONCERNING ST MARGARET.

units.la: 13. Julii. O miranda & laudanda Summi Regis filia Margarita exquisita. Margareta nobis nostrum. Cursum rege sursum Virgo delectabilis. Hallel.
units.tr: 13 July. O wonderful and praiseworthy Margaret, chosen daughter of the Highest King, our Margaret, direct our course upward with the King. Delightful virgin. Hallel.

units.la: ITEM: Ad mucronem cervix tensa Orat voce cum immensa Pro se venerantibus. Mox sponsa pondit regnū cœli. Promisso pacto fideli. Cunctis te laudantibus.
units.tr: ALSO: With her neck stretched out to the sword, she cried out with a mighty voice for those who venerate her. Soon the bride obtained the kingdom of heaven by the promised faithful covenant, while all praise you.

units.la: DE S. CHRISTINA.
units.tr: CONCERNING ST CHRISTINA.

units.la: 24. Julii. Christina virgo felix Te deprecantes respice, Ne cum impiis damnemur. Nos tua sancta salva prece.
units.tr: 24 July. Happy virgin Christina, look upon us who entreat you, lest we be condemned together with the impious. Save us by your holy prayer.

units.la: DE S. AFRA.
units.tr: CONCERNING ST AFRA.

units.la: 7. Augusti. O Narcisse, cum Felice Vos pro nobis omni vice. Et pro nostra civitate, Et pro cunctis supplicate. Afra simul & consortes, Stent pro nobis prece fortes, Et ut nobis expiatis Sit portio cum beatis.
units.tr: 7 August. O Narcissus, together with Felix, pray for us on every occasion, and for our city, and intercede for all. Afra, and your companions, stand strong in prayer for us, so that, with us cleansed, we may have a share with the blessed.

units.la: DE S. URSULA: Et undecim mille virginibus.
units.tr: ON ST URSULA: And the Eleven Thousand Virgins.

units.la: 21. Octobris.
units.tr: 21 October.

units.la: O praeclara vos puella | Subvenite sine mora, Nunc implete meum | In tam gravi tempestate velle, (hora, | Me peccante defensate Et du morbis venerut | A daemonum instantia.
units.tr: O illustrious maidens, help without delay. Now fulfil my desire in this so grave storm-hour. Defend me, a sinner, and from diseases... from the assault of the demons.

units.la: Collecta. Deus, gloria virginum, & amator earum, qui beatae Ursulae in palma martyrii contulisti undecim millium virginum comitatum, concede nobis, earum multiplici interventu, petitionum efficaciam, fidei constantiam & operis puritatem.
units.tr: Collect. O God, the glory of virgins and their lover, who in the palm of martyrdom gave blessed Ursula a company of eleven thousand virgins, grant us, through their manifold intercession, the efficacy of our petitions, constancy in faith, and purity in works.

units.la: SEQUENTIA.
units.tr: SEQUENCE.

units.la: Ut flores, decidivâ ex hac virgineâ sorte, claruit Ursula sancta. Cujus hodie celebramus solennia. Fulgens inter alias, ut Lucifer inter alias stellas.
units.tr: As a flower from this virginal lot, holy Ursula shone forth, whose solemnities we celebrate today. Shining among the others, as Lucifer among the stars.

units.la: Virgo beata, fortiter ferens omnia, nec mortí recusans, cum tuis pro nobis Deum ora.
units.tr: Blessed virgin, bearing all things bravely and not refusing death, pray to God for us with your companions.

units.la: Offertorium.
units.tr: Offertory.

units.la: Virgines egregiae, Vigiles prudentes, Summi Regis gloria, In dextra consistentes, In valle miseriae, Nos audite flentes. Ad vestrae thronos gloriae, Preces offerentes.
units.tr: Noble virgins, prudent watchers, glory of the highest King, standing at his right hand, hear us weeping in this vale of misery, as we offer our prayers before the thrones of your glory.

units.la: COMMUNIO.
units.tr: COMMUNION.

units.la: Splendor lucis aeternalis, Iesu Doctor gloriae Prece chori virginalis Congaudens hodie, Nos defendat infernalis A fletu moestitia.
units.tr: Splendour of eternal light, Jesus, Teacher of glory, rejoicing today with the prayer of the virgin choir, may the infernal sorrow of tears not hold us in its grief.

units.la: PRECATIO ALIA:
units.tr: OTHER PRAYER:

units.la: Concede, Domine, propitius, ut earum virginum precibus & meritis, cum ipsis in æ-terna beatitudine collocari mereamur.
units.tr: Grant, O Lord, graciously, that through the prayers and merits of these virgins we may be found worthy to be placed with them in eternal blessedness.

units.la: ALIA:
units.tr: ANOTHER:

units.la: Quarum orationibusFelices cum felicibus,Pace fruamur sedulâ,Per sæculorum sæcula.
units.tr: By whose prayers, may we, happy with the happy, enjoy peace unceasing, through the ages of ages.

units.la: DE S. CATHARINA.
units.tr: On S. Catharine.

units.la: 25. Novembris.
units.tr: 25 November.

units.la: Deus, qui dedisti legem Mosi in summi-tate montis Sinai, & in eodem loco per Angelos tuos corpus beatæ Catharinæ virginis martyris tuæ mirabiliter collocasti, tribue quæsumus, ut ejus meritis & intercessione ad montem, qui Christus est, valeamus per-venire.
units.tr: O God, who gave the law to Moses on the summit of Mount Sinai, and who in that same place didst marvellously lay the body of thy blessed virgin and martyr Catharine by the hands of thine angels, grant, we beseech thee, that by her merits and intercession we may come to the mountain, which is Christ.

units.la: Catharina flos rosarumConsolatrix animarumTuæ precis interventuAngelorum nos concentuFac gaudere jugiter.
units.tr: Catharine, flower of roses, comforter of souls, by the intervention of your prayer and the harmony of the angels, make us rejoice without ceasing.

units.la: Ave virginum gemma Catharina,
units.tr: Hail, Catharine, gem of virgins,

units.la: Ave sponsa Regis regum gloriosa.
units.tr: Hail, glorious bride of the King of kings.

units.la: Ave viva Christi hostia,Tua venerantibus patrocinia,Impetrata non deneges suffragia.
units.tr: Hail, living victim of Christ; to those who venerate you, grant the protection they seek, and do not deny the help that is asked of you.

units.la: ETIAM.
units.tr: Also.

units.la: Ave virgo Dei digna, Christo preces me consigna, Preces audi, presta votum, Cor in bono fac immotum. Confer mihi cor contritum, Rege visum & auditum, Rege gustum & olfactum, Virgo sancta rege tactum. Ut in cunctis te regente, Vivam Deo pure mente, O beata Catharina, Babylonis de sententia, Tutum mihi fer ducatum, Plasmatorem fac placatu. Esto mihi consolatrix, Pro me fis interpellatrix. Christum pro me interpella, Salus mortis de procella,
units.tr: Hail, virgin worthy of God, commend my prayers to Christ; hear the prayers, grant the vow, and make my heart firm in good. Bestow on me a contrite heart, rule my sight and hearing, rule my taste and smell; holy virgin, rule my touch. That with you ruling in all things I may live to God with a pure mind. O blessed Catharine, by the sentence of Babylon, bring me a safe guidance, and make the Creator placable toward me. Be my consoler, be my intercessor before him. Plead Christ for me, the salvation from the storm of death.

units.la: ET: Sponsa sponso gratos Fac nos & acceptos.
units.tr: ET: Bride, make us pleasing and acceptable to the Bridegroom.

units.la: Superare fac me mundu, Ne demergar in profundu. Ne me sinas naufragari, In peccatis, in hoc mari, Visitatu me in firmum, Et in bonis fac me firmum. Agonista Dei fortis, Esto praesens hora mortis, Decumbentem fove, leva, Et de morte solve sava. Ut resurgam novus homo, Civis in caelesti domo, Duplex mors ne me infestet, Jesus Christus illud praestet, Tua prece exoratus. Idem Pater, idem Natus, Idem utriusq; flamen, Quin vivit & regat. Ame.
units.tr: Make me overcome the world, lest I be plunged into its depths. Do not let me be shipwrecked in sins, in this sea. Visit me when I am weak, and make me firm in good things. Strong champion of God, be present at the hour of death; cherish me as I lie down, lift me up, and free me from cruel death. That I may rise a new man, a citizen in the heavenly home, let not the twofold death harm me; Jesus Christ grant this, entreated by your prayer. The same Father, the same Son, the same Spirit of both, who lives and reigns. Amen.

units.la: Item: Monstrate vita viam, Ut philosophiam Mundi transeamus, Veram inquiramus.
units.tr: Likewise: Show life the way, so that we may pass beyond the philosophy of the world and seek the true one.

units.la: ET:
units.tr: ET:

units.la: Ora & inclina nobis verum Sina, ut intremus chorum tecum Angelorum.
units.tr: Pray for us and bend toward us the true Sinai, that we may enter the choir of angels with you.

units.la: COMPLETORIUM.
units.tr: Compline.

units.la: Catharina collaudemus, Virtutum insignia, Ut spe certa respiremus Per ejus suffraga.
units.tr: Let us praise Catharine, the badge of virtues, so that we may breathe again with sure hope through her supports.

units.la: SEQUENTIA.
units.tr: Sequence.

units.la: Sanctissimæ virginis votiva festa recolamus. Venerantes hunc diem præclarum omnes concinamus, &c.
units.tr: Let us celebrate the votive feasts of the most holy virgin. Honouring this glorious day, let us all sing together, etc.

units.la: Fit pœnalis machina,Pereunt tot millia,Dum rotantur agminaPaganorum.Mox truncatur capite,Adsunt turba calica,Sepelitur debitèMonte Sina.
units.tr: The machine of punishment is made; so many thousands perish as the troops of the pagans are whirled around. Soon she is beheaded, a throng is present, and she is duly buried on Mount Sinai.

units.la: Ora pro populo,Precare pro clero,Martyr ChristiCatharina.Astantem populum,Precantem te clerũ,Fove, rege per secula,Catharina. Amen.
units.tr: Pray for the people, intercede for the clergy, Catharine, martyr of Christ. Cherish and rule through the ages the people standing by and the clergy praying to you, Catharine. Amen.

units.la: DE S. BARBARA.
units.tr: On S. Barbara.

units.la: 4. Decembris.
units.tr: 4 December.

units.la: Intercessio nos, Domine, quæsumus, beatæ Barbaræ Virginis & Martyris tuæ semper adjuvet, ut non subitò moriamur.
units.tr: May the intercession of your blessed virgin and martyr Barbara always help us, Lord, we beseech you, so that we do not die suddenly.

units.la: Alia precatio.
units.tr: Another prayer.

units.la: Intercessio, quæsumus, Domine Deus noster, beatæ Barbaræ Virginis & Martyris tuæ gloriosæ, ab omni adversitate protegat, ut per ejus interventum, gloriosissimi corporis & sanguinis Domini nostri Jesu Christi Sacramentum ante vitæ nostræ exitum, cum verâ fide & purâ confessione percipere mereamur.
units.tr: May the intercession, we beseech you, Lord our God, of your blessed virgin and glorious martyr Barbara protect us from every adversity, so that through her intervention we may deserve to receive, before the end of our life, the sacrament of the most glorious body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, with true faith and pure confession.

units.la: DE ALIIS SANCTIS VIRGINIBUS & viduis.
units.tr: On other holy virgins and widows.

units.la: De omnibus virginibus & viduis, (exclusis conjugatis.)
units.tr: Of all virgins and widows (excluding the married).

units.la: Deus, qui nos in tantis periculis constitutos, tutos, pro humilitate, scis, fragilitate non posse subsistere, da nobis per merita omnium sanctarum virginum, viduarum & continentium tuarum, salutem mentis & corporis, ut ea, quae pro peccatis nostris juste patimur, te adjuvante vincamus.
units.tr: O God, who knowest that we, placed in such great dangers, cannot stand by our own frailty though we are kept safe by our humility, grant us, through the merits of all your holy virgins, widows and continent ones, health of mind and body, so that with your help we may overcome those things which we justly suffer for our sins.

units.la: DE SANCTIS VIRGINIBUS.
units.tr: ON THE HOLY VIRGINS.

units.la: Exultent filiæ Sion, in Rege suo, nescientes thorum delicti crimine sordidatum.
units.tr: Let the daughters of Zion rejoice in their King, not knowing a bed soiled by the crime of sin.

units.la: Quarum Christe sponsus, virginum virginis es filius.
units.tr: Christ, bridegroom of virgins, you are the Son of the Virgin of virgins.

units.la: Cujus gratia mira opera in sanctis tuis sunt edita.
units.tr: By your grace wonderful works have been wrought in your saints.

units.la: Ut das cernere in hac virgine, cujus haec festa sunt hodie.
units.tr: As you grant us to see in this virgin, whose feast it is today.

units.la: Quae fragili sexu foemineo, viriliter carnis jura domito,
units.tr: She, a frail woman, manfully subdued the laws of the flesh.

units.la: Angelicam hic vitam duxerat, in carne dum praeter carnem vixerat.
units.tr: Here she had led an angelic life, living beyond the flesh while in the flesh.

units.la: Hoc miratur serpens antiquus, calcaneum ejus observabat callidus.
units.tr: The ancient serpent marvels at this; the crafty one watched her heel.

units.la: Quod noceret, dum machinatur, sub pedibus foeminae caput ejus teritur.
units.tr: Plotting to harm her, he has his head crushed beneath the foot of the woman.

units.la: Insidias hostis hanc, Christe docuisti virginem vincere in prima congressione.
units.tr: Christ, you taught this virgin to conquer the enemy's snares in the first encounter.

units.la: Dum non consentiret, sed illi resisteret, vincere qui solet, tentatus si non repugnet.
units.tr: Since she did not consent but resisted him, he conquers, as he usually does, if the one tempted does not resist.

units.la: Quae haec virgo, resistens, fecit a te fugere.
units.tr: This virgin, by resisting, made him flee from you.

units.la: Quo fugato, appropinquabat tibi Domino. Nunc inter virgines adducta, post eam, quæ mater est intacta, virginis virginum Mariæ digna est pedisequa.
units.tr: With him put to flight, she drew near to you, the Lord. Now received among the virgins, she is worthy to be the handmaid of Mary, who is the untouched mother and the virgin of virgins.

units.la: Te agnum sine macula jam sequitur stolâ candidâ,
units.tr: Now she follows you, the Lamb without spot, clothed in a white robe,

units.la: Filium virginis, quocunque virginum flos Cujus intercessione tu nos tuere. (ierit.
units.tr: Son of the virgin, wherever the flower of virgins has gone. By her intercession, protect us.

units.la: De una virgine.
units.tr: On one virgin.

units.la: Salve sancta N. virgo Dei inclyta, tuis precibus nos Christo commenda. Ad te clamamus in angustiis constituti. Ad te suspiramus, auxilium quaerentes. Eja virgo Dei electa, tuum laetum oculorum aspectum ad nos inclina, & Jesum crucifixum, qui tollit mundi reatum, redde nobis placatum, o clemens, o pia, o dulcis virgo.
units.tr: Hail, holy N., famous virgin of God; by your prayers commend us to Christ. To you we cry out, placed in distress. To you we sigh, seeking help. Come, chosen virgin of God, turn your joyful gaze upon us, and render us Jesus crucified, who takes away the guilt of the world, made gracious to us, O merciful, O pious, O sweet virgin.

units.la: ET:
units.tr: AND:

units.la: Tute jam dulcibus plena deliciis, Christo miserias nostras suggerito, nobis consolationem precando.
units.tr: Now you, full of sweet delights, present our miseries to Christ, pleading consolation for us.

units.la: DE S. BRIGITTA. 1. Februarii.
units.tr: On Saint Bridget. 1 February.

units.la: O Brigitta, mater bona, Dulcis ductrix, et matrona Nobis fer suffragia. Naufragantes in hoc mari, Tuo ductu salutari Duc ad vitæ bravia.
units.tr: O Bridget, good mother, sweet guide and matron, bring us your aid. We who are shipwrecked on this sea, lead us by your saving guidance to the prizes of life.

units.la: DE S. GERTHRUDE, 17. Martii.
units.tr: Of St Gertrude, 17 March.

units.la: Deus, q beatam Gerthrudem, piam virgi- nem, ex stirpe Regiâ progenitam, speciali ho- spitaspitalitatis gratiâ sublimasti, tribue, quæsumus, ut ejus precibus & meritis intervenientibus, tam præsens, quàm futurum hospitium, nostræ infirmitati congruum, & tuæ majestati inveniamus acceptum.
units.tr: O God, who exalted the blessed Gertrude, a pious virgin born of royal stock, with the special grace of hospitality, grant, we beseech thee, that through her prayers and intercessions we may find both present and future hospitality, fitting for our weakness and acceptable to thy majesty.

units.la: DE S. MARIA MAGDALENA.
units.tr: Of St Mary Magdalene.

units.la: 22. Julii. Hæc est illa fœmina Cujus cuncta crimina Ad Christi vestigia, Ejus lavit gratia. Quæ dum plorat, & mens orat, Facto clamat, quòd cor aJesum super omnia. (mat. Non ignorat, quem adorat, Quid precetur: jam delet, Quod mens tenet conscia. O Maria, stella maris, Pia mater appellaris, Operum per merita, Matri Christi coæquatâ, Dum sui sic vocata, Sed honore subdita. Illa enim fuit porta, Per quem mundo lux est orta: Hæc resurgentis pranuntia, Mundum replet lætitiâ. Illa mundi imperatrix: Ista beata peccatrix, Lætitia primordia Fuerunt in Ecclesiâ. O Maria Magdalena, Audi vota laude plena, Apud Christum, chorum ipsum Clementer concilia. Ut fons suprema pietatis, Qui te lavit à peccatis, Servos suos atque tuos Mundet, data venia. Amen.
units.tr: 22 July. This is that woman whose every sin was washed away by grace at the feet of Christ. While she weeps and her mind prays, by her deed she proclaims that she loves Jesus above all things. She does not fail to know whom she adores or what she should ask; now she blots out what her conscious mind holds. O Mary, star of the sea, you are called the loving mother, by the merits of your works, made equal to the Mother of Christ, though subject to her in honour. For she was the gate through which the light rose upon the world; you, the herald of the Risen One, fill the world with joy. She was the empress of the world; you, the blessed sinner. The beginnings of joy were in the Church. O Mary Magdalene, hear our prayers full of praise, and plead for us graciously with Christ himself, the highest fount of piety, who washed you from your sins, that he may cleanse his servants and yours by granting pardon. Amen.

units.la: Adeandem: Te quæsumus, gratissimam nobis deposce veniam.
units.tr: To the same: We beseech you, ask for us the most gracious pardon.

units.la: DE S. ANNA, B. MARIÆ VIRGINIS MATRE.
units.tr: Of St Anne, mother of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

units.la: 16. Julii.
units.tr: 16 July.

units.la: Nardi Nardus spirat in odorem, Et spumetum profert florem, Sed flos fructus dat honore Regis in accubitu. Salus redit de Iudaea, Qua sanatur Idumaea Ex Ægypto fert trophaa In exitu. Holofernem Iudith straviţ, Anna quando generavit, Quae se Deo praeparavit Habitaculum. Coeli cohors Annam laudet, Nam in coelis Anna gaudet, Et rogare natam audet, Et Iesum nepotulum. Non avertit aurem nata, Sed et matris ad precata Iesus dona profert grata, Ut de nobis cogitet. Ego Annam nunc accede, Roga natam, nec recede, Donec nepos nos a sede Sua sancta visitet. Amen.
units.tr: Spikenard breathes out its fragrance, and the flower-bud bears a flower; but the flower gives fruit, to the honour of the King's couch. Salvation returns from Judaea, by which Idumaea is healed; from Egypt it brings its trophies on the going out. Judith struck down Holofernes, when Anna bore a child, who prepared herself as a dwelling for God. Let the host of heaven praise Anna, for Anna rejoices in heaven, and dares to ask of her daughter, and of Jesus her little grandson. The daughter does not turn away her ear, and Jesus brings his gracious gifts at his mother's prayers, that he may think of us. I now approach Anna: ask your daughter, and do not withdraw, until the grandson visits us from his holy seat. Amen.

units.la: Deus, qui beatam Annam, matrem tuae genitricis fieri voluisti: praesta quaesumus, ut meritis utriusque, matris & filiae, regna coelestia consequamur.
units.tr: O God, who wast pleased to make the blessed Anna the mother of thy mother, grant, we beseech thee, that by the merits of both, mother and daughter, we may attain the heavenly kingdom.

units.la: Deus, qui beatam Annam dilectae genitricis tuae matre egregiam ad coelestis vitae gaudia sublevasti: fac nos, quaesumus, ejus meritis gloriosis ad aeternam pertingere beatitudinem, ex cujus puerperio, pro salute mundi humanam dignatus es assumere carnem.
units.tr: O God, who didst raise up the blessed Anna, excellent in being the mother of thy beloved mother, to the joys of heavenly life: grant, we beseech thee, that by her glorious merits we may attain to eternal blessedness, from whose childbearing thou didst deign to take on human flesh for the salvation of the world.

units.la: DE S. MARTHA.
units.tr: ON ST MARTHA.

units.la: 27. Julii.
units.tr: 27 July.

units.la: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, cujus filius summa carne pro nobis, in aede beatae Marthae hospitari dignatus est, concede propitius, ut precibus & meritis illius, quae illum placide suscepit in terris, ab illo misericorditer suscipi mereamur in coelis.
units.tr: Almighty and everlasting God, whose Son, in his human flesh, deigned to be entertained for our sake in the house of blessed Martha, graciously grant that by her prayers and merits, who received him gladly on earth, we may be mercifully received by him in heaven.

units.la: DE S. CLARA. 11. Augusti.
units.tr: ON ST CLARE. 11 August.

units.la: O virgo clarens vespere, Præclaris clara meritis, Liga perfecto sedēre Nos in amore Christi. Da membra fore capitis, Et sensibus & motibus, Iesu, quem dilexisti, Halleluja.
units.tr: O virgin, shining in the evening, bright in your distinguished merits, you bound yourself in perfect love of Christ. Grant that we may be members of the Head, in our senses and our movements, Jesus, whom you loved. Hallelujah.

units.la: DE S. VERONICA. 17. Augusti.
units.tr: ON ST VERONICA. 17 August.

units.la: Ave facies præclara, Qua nobis in crucis ara Facta es sic pallida. In anxietate denigrata, Sudore sanguinis rigata, Te texit linteolus. In quo mansit tua forma, Qua passionis tua norma, Cunctis est pralucida. Hac cordi meo fit impressa, Per te Christe, nec cessa Hoc cremare indefessa Amoris tui facula. Ut post hanc vitam cum beatis Possim vultum Deitatis Et videre voluptatis, In perenni gloria. Amen.
units.tr: Hail, glorious face, which on the altar of the cross became so pale. Blackened in anguish, bedewed with sweat and blood, a little linen cloth covered you. On it your form remained, which is the clear pattern of your passion for all. Let it be impressed on my heart, through you, Christ, and let it never cease, tirelessly, to kindle the torch of your love. So that after this life, among the blessed, I may see the face of the Godhead and enjoy it in everlasting glory. Amen.

units.la: Hanc orationem recitans tres annos & quadraginta dies indulgentiarum concessas habet, ex munificentia & liberalitate Innocentii IV. circa annum Christi 1250.
units.tr: Whoever recites this prayer has three years and forty days of indulgences granted, by the generosity and liberality of Innocent IV, around the year of Christ 1250.

units.la: DE S. ELISABETHA.
units.tr: ON ST ELIZABETH.

units.la: 19. Novembris. Eja mater nos agnosce, Libro vitæ nos deposce Cum electis inseri, Ut consortes tuæ sortis Et à pœnes & à portis Eruamur inferi.
units.tr: 19 November. Come, mother, acknowledge us, and ask for us to be written in the book of life, to be numbered with the chosen, so that, as companions of your lot, we may be snatched from the punishments and the gates of hell.

units.la: DE S. OTILIA.
units.tr: ON ST OTILIA.

units.la: Collecta: Deus, qui beatissimā Otiliam virginem tuam coœam natam ad Baptismi gratiam corpocorporaliter illuminasti, & omnem cœcitatem corporis & animæ ab eâ misericorditer repulisti, tuam pietatem devotissimè exoramus, ut familiam tuam, per ejus suffragia, tuæ benedictionis dona postulantem, clementer exaudias, & ad fontem sempiternum misericordiæ tuæ pervenire concedas.
units.tr: Collect: O God, who enlightened your most blessed virgin Otilia, born blind, in body to the grace of Baptism, and mercifully drove out from her all blindness of body and soul, we most devoutly beseech your loving-kindness that, through her intercessions, you would graciously hear your household, which asks for the gifts of your blessing, and grant that it may come to the everlasting fountain of your mercy.

units.la: Complenda: Adjutor noster & refugium, omnipotens & misericors Deus, qui gloriossimam virginem tuam Otiliam, pro resuscitatione patris sui defuncti lachrymantem, & tuam misericordiam deprecantem exaudisti, atq; ab omnibus concupiscentiis & vanitatibus hujus seculi eam liberasti: concede nobis, fidelibus tuis, per ejus exempla, de virtute in virtutem proficere, ac in amore tuo semper fervere.
units.tr: Postcommunion: Our helper and refuge, almighty and merciful God, who heard your most glorious virgin Otilia, weeping for the restoration of her dead father and imploring your mercy, and who freed her from all the lusts and vanities of this age: grant us, your faithful people, through her examples, to advance from virtue to virtue and always to burn with love for you.

units.la: DE S. MONICÆ, AVGVSTI-NI MATRIS, TRANSLATIONE.
units.tr: On the Translation of St Monica, Mother of Augustine.

units.la: INTROITUS.
units.tr: INTROIT.

units.la: Quæ ad portum Tyberinum Cœli scandis solium, Patrem nostrum Augustinum Tu assume filium. Ora nobis vespertinum Ut donetur bravium, Christus fidus matutinum Videre per seculum. Halleluja.
units.tr: You who ascend the throne of heaven at the Tiber harbour, take up our father Augustine as your son. Pray for us at evening, that the prize may be granted, and that Christ, faithful, we may see the morning through all the ages. Alleluia.

units.la: Felix mater Monica, comple tuorum vota filiorum, & tui ardoris in eis lumen ostende. Halleluja.
units.tr: Happy mother Monica, fulfil the prayers of your sons, and show in them the light of your burning zeal. Alleluia.

units.la: SEQUENTIA:
units.tr: SEQUENCE:

units.la: Ave mater gloriosa, Augustini cordis mœsti
units.tr: Hail, glorious mother, of the sorrowful heart of Augustine,

units.la: Morte Christi lachrymosa, Prolem, cernis tecum sisti,
units.tr: Weeping at the death of Christ, you see your offspring standing with you,
