units.la: Præsta nobis, quæsumus Domine, per huius aspersionem aquæ, integritatem mentis, sanitatem corporis, tutelam salutis, securitatem spei, corroborationem fidei, hic & in æterna sæcula sæculorum. ℣.
units.tr: Grant us, we beseech you, Lord, through the sprinkling of this water, integrity of mind, health of body, protection of salvation, security of hope, strengthening of faith, here and for ever and ever. ℣.

units.la: De Campanarum baptismo & consecratione.
units.tr: On the baptism and consecration of bells.

units.la: Dum Campana aquâ, vino, cinere & sale mixta, abluitur, oleo sancto ungitur, exorcizatur, multa cruces illi imprimuntur, plusquam viginti benedictiones adhibentur, patrini etiam complures invitantur, denique nomen illi imponitur: ista igitur dum fiunt, precationes plures & multi psalmi sacri recitantur.
units.tr: While the bell is washed in water mixed with wine, ash and salt, anointed with holy oil, exorcised, marked with many crosses, subjected to more than twenty blessings, and several godparents are invited, and finally given a name, many prayers and many sacred psalms are recited while these things are done.

units.la: Dum sal in aquam crucis in modum mittitur: Haec commixtio salis & aquae efficiatur salutare sacramentum, in nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus Sancti.
units.tr: While salt is put into the water in the form of a cross: This mixing of salt and water is made into a saving sacrament, in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Precatio: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui ante arcam sederis per clangorem tubarum, muros lapideos, quibus cingebatur adversantium exercitus, cadere fecisti: in hoc tintinnabulum caelesti benedictione perfundere, purificare, sanctificare, & consecrare digneris, ut ante sonitum ejus effugiant ignita jacula inimici, percussio fulminum, impetus lapidum, laesio tempestatum, ut ad interrogationem propheticam: Quid est tibi mare, quod fugisti? Quis motibus cum Jordanico retroactis fluento, respondeant: A facie Domini mota est terra, a facie Dei Jacob, qui convertit petram solidam in stagnum aquae, & rupem in fontes aquarum. Non ergo nobis, domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam, secundum misericordiam tuam, ut cum praesens hoc vasculum, sicut reliqua altaris vasa, sacro Chrismate tangitur, & oleo sacrosancto ungitur, tua benedictione sanctificetur, & quod arte aut metalli specie non poterit fieri dignum, fiat tua benedictione perfusum, ut quicunq; ad sonitum ejus convenerint, ab omnibus inimici tentationibus liberentur in corpore, & a pravis cogitationibus mundentur in mente, semperque fidei Catholicae documenta sectentur, atque tuae consolationis gratiam percipere mereantur. Salvator mundi, cui flectitur omne genu caelestium, terrestrium, & infetorum, qui cum patre & spritu sancto vivis & regnas Deus in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
units.tr: Prayer: Almighty, everlasting God, who by the sound of trumpets caused the stone walls that surrounded the army of the adversaries to fall before the ark, deign to bathe, purify, sanctify and consecrate this bell with heavenly blessing, so that at the sound of it the fiery darts of the enemy, the striking of lightning, the assault of stones and the harm of storms may flee away. Thus, to the prophetic question, "What ailed you, O sea, that you fled?" and "Who turned back the Jordan's flowing stream?", let the answer be: "The earth trembled at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the God of Jacob, who turned the hard rock into a pool of water and the flint into a fountain of waters." Therefore, Lord, not to us, not to us, but to your name give the glory, according to your mercy. So that, just as this little vessel is touched with holy chrism and anointed with sacred oil like the other vessels of the altar, it may be sanctified by your blessing; and what cannot be made worthy by art or by the kind of metal may be made worthy by being bathed in your blessing. So that whoever gather at its sound may be freed in body from all the temptations of the enemy, be cleansed in mind from evil thoughts, always follow the teachings of the Catholic faith, and deserve to receive the grace of your consolation. Saviour of the world, to whom every knee of those in heaven, on earth and under the earth is bowed, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit live and reign, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: De consecratione Campanarum, canon in Synodo Coloniensi sic habet.
units.tr: On the consecration of bells; a canon of the Synod of Cologne states as follows.

units.la: Benedicuntur Campanae, ut sint tubae Ecclesiae militantis, quibus vocetur populus ad templa, ad audiendum verbum Dei: clerus vero ad annunciandum mane misericordiam Dei, & veritatem ejus per noctem, ut per illarum sonitum fideles invitentur ad preces, & ut crescat in his devotio fidei: quamvis etiam patres alio respexerint, scilicet, ut daemones tinnitu campanarum Christianos ad preces concitanti-um terreantur, quin potius precibus ipsis ter-riti titi, abscedant, illisque submotis, fruges, mé-tes, & corpora fidelium serventur, ut procul pellantur hostiles exercitus & omnes insidiæ inimici, fragor grandinum, procellæ turbi-num, impetus tempestatum & fulgurum té-perentur, infesta tonitrua & ventorum fulmi-na suspendantur, spiritus procellarum, & aë-ræ potestatis prosternantur. Breviter: Ut audientes confugiant ad Sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ gremium.
units.tr: Bells are blessed so that they may be the trumpets of the militant Church, by which the people are called to the churches to hear the Word of God, and the clergy are called to proclaim the mercy of God in the morning and his truth in the night; so that by their sound the faithful may be invited to prayer and devotion of faith may grow in them. Although the Fathers also had another purpose in view, namely that by the ringing of bells the demons, who stir Christians to prayer, may be terrified, or rather, terrified by the prayers themselves, may depart; and that, with them driven away, the fruits, harvests and bodies of the faithful may be preserved; that hostile armies and all the snares of the enemy may be driven far off; that the crash of hailstones, the squalls of whirlwinds, the force of storms and lightning may be restrained; that dreadful thunders and the thunderbolts of the winds may be held back; and that the spirits of the tempests and of the aerial power may be overthrown. In short: that those who hear it may flee to the bosom of holy Mother Church.

units.la: Inscriptio campanæ Stakbori oppiduli ad lo-cum renetum: Colo verum Deum: plebem voco, & congrego clerum: Divos adoro: festa decoro: defunctos ploro: pestem dæmonesque fugo.
units.tr: Inscription on the bell of the little town of Stakbor at the place called Renetum: I worship the true God; I call the people and gather the clergy; I honour the saints; I adorn the festivals; I mourn the dead; I drive away plague and demons.

units.la: Gravissima querela contra inanem & im-modicam campanarum consecrationem & baptizationem extat inter gravamina Germaniæ, imperante Carolo V. anno 1552. Legato Pontificis in comitiis Noribergensibus exhibita, gravamine 51, his verbis: Suffraganei excogitaverunt, ut solum ipsi, & nullus alius sacerdos laicis campanas baptizent. Credunt deinde simpliciores, ita affirmantibus suffraganeis, tales campanas baptizatas, dæmones & tempestates pellere. Quapropter innumeri adhibentur compatres, præcipue vero, qui fortuna pollent, exorantur, qui baptizationis tempore funem, quâ campana religata est, tangunt, & suffraganeo praecinente (quē- admodum in parvulorum baptizatione fi- eri solet) omnes pariter respondent; ac Cam- panæ nomen ingeminant, vestequē nova (quemadmodum & Christianis fieri solet) campana induitur. Inde ad sumptuosa pro- peratur convivia, quibus praecipuē compa- tres, ut eo largius munera offerant, exhibe- tur: nec non suffraganei, & eorum capellani, cum multis aliis ministris regaliter pascuntur. Nec hoc satis est, sed & suffraganeo mercē- dem persolvere necesse est, quam illi munu- sculum vocare solent. Inde evenit, ut aliquā- do etiam in parvis villis centum floreni in ta- li absumantur & expendantur baptizatione. Quæ res non solum superstitiosa, sed etiā Christiana religioni contraria ac simpliciorum seduc- tio, & mera est exactio. Veruntamen Episco- pi, ut suffraganeos vel vilissima obærare pos- sint mercede, talia, & adhuc absurdiora tole- rant. Res igitur tam nephanda & illicita meri- to aboleri debent.
units.tr: A most serious complaint against the empty and immoderate consecration and baptism of bells is found among the grievances of Germany, under the emperor Charles V, in the year 1552. Presented by the Papal legate at the Diet of Nuremberg, it is grievance 51, in these words: The suffragans have devised that only they, and no other priest, may baptise bells for laymen. The simpler folk then believe, as the suffragans assert, that bells so baptised drive away demons and storms. For this reason countless godparents are admitted, especially those who are rich, and they are entreated; at the time of the baptism they touch the rope by which the bell is hung, and, when the suffragan sings the words first (as is usually done in the baptism of infants), they all respond together and repeat the bell's name over and over; and the bell is dressed in new clothing, as is done for Christians. Then they hurry to lavish feasts, at which the godparents in particular are served, so that they may offer gifts more freely; and the suffragans and their chaplains, with many other ministers, are feasted like kings. Nor is this enough, but they must also pay the suffragan a fee, which they are accustomed to call a little gift. Hence it happens that sometimes even in small villages a hundred florins are spent and expended on such a baptism. This practice is not only superstitious, but also contrary to the Christian religion, a deception of the simpler folk, and sheer extortion. Yet the bishops tolerate such things, and even more absurd ones, so that the suffragans may be enriched by even the cheapest fees. Therefore such wicked and unlawful things ought rightly to be abolished.

units.la: Subjicitur ibidem: Cæterum si conducere videtur, ut campanæ consecrentur, (ita enim suffraganei baptizationem appellant, quot es à prudentioribus hac de re inter- pellantur) conveniens erit, ut talis conse- cratio per unumquenque fiat sacerdotum, quemadmodum cum aquâ benedictâ, sale, herbis, & similibus fieri solet: idque absque pretio & expensis laicorum, ut populus simplex ita seducatur, & damno afficiatur, nec non avaritiæ detestandæ præsumtio evitetur.
units.tr: It is added in the same place: Moreover, if it seems advisable that bells be consecrated (for so the suffragans call the baptism, as many wise men are asked about this matter), it will be fitting that such consecration be performed by each of the priests, as is usually done with holy water, salt, herbs and the like; and this should be done without payment or expense to the laity, so that the simple people are not deceived and harmed, and the presumption of detestable greed is avoided.

units.la: AURI, THURIS, MYRRHÆ, die Epiphaniæ.
units.tr: Gold, Frankincense and Myrrh, on the Feast of the Epiphany.

units.la: Per hos sacros sermones Evangelii (postquam historicum textus de Magis prælectus fuerit) & per merita sanctorum trium Regum dignare, omnipotens Deus, benedicere has creaturas thuris & myrrhæ, & thymiamatis & auri sive argenti, dextera tua, & præsta, ut omnes in te credentes, & odorem illorum gustantes, ab omni ægritudine absolvantur.
units.tr: Through these holy sermons of the Gospel (after the historical text about the Magi has been read aloud), and through the merits of the holy three Kings, deign, almighty God, to bless these creatures of frankincense and myrrh, and of the incense, and of gold or silver, by your right hand; and grant that all who believe in you and taste their fragrance may be freed from every sickness.

units.la: Quæsumus, per filium, in virtute Spiritus sancti, hoc aurum & argetum, quod benedicimus, benedicas, quod in tuo nomine sanctificamus, & consecramus, cœlesti ac perpetuâ sanctificatione sanctifices, ut insidiis diabolicæ fraudis obsistat, sanitatem animæ & corporis, tuâ opitulatione, operans, contraria valetudinis incommoda depellat.
units.tr: We beseech you, through the Son, in the power of the Holy Spirit: bless this gold and silver, which we bless; sanctify it, which we hallow and consecrate in your name, with a heavenly and perpetual sanctification; so that it may withstand the snares of diabolical deceit, and, by your aid working the health of soul and body, drive away the troubles of ill health.

units.la: Quod ipse præstare dignetur, qui &c.
units.tr: Which may he deign to grant, who &c.

units.la: CHRISMATIS, OLEI SANCTI, & olei Catechumenorum, die Cœnæ Dominicæ.
units.tr: Of the chrism, the holy oil, and the oil of the catechumens, on Maundy Thursday (the day of the Lord's Supper).

units.la: Christi-
units.tr: Christi-

units.la: CHRISMATIS, SEU OLEI infirmorum.
units.tr: CHRISM, OR OIL OF THE SICK.

units.la: Exorcizo te, immundissime spiritus, omnisque incursio Satanæ, & omne phantasma, in nomine Patris, & Filii, & spiritus S. ut recedas ab hoc oleo, ut possit effici unctio spiritualis, ad corroborandum templum Dei vivi, ut in eo possit Spiritus sanctus habitare, per nomen Dei patris omnipotentis, & per nomen Christi. Emitte, quæsumus Domine, Spiritum sanctum paracletum, de cœlis, in hanc pinguedinem olivæ, quam de viridi ligno producere dignatus es, ad refectionem mentis & corporis, ut tua sancta benedictione, sit omni hoc cœlestis medicinæ unguento peruncto, tutamen mentis & corporis, ad evacuandos omnes dolores, omnes infirmitates, omnemque ægritudinem mentis & corporis, unde unxisti Sacerdotes, Reges, Prophetas, & Martyres tuos. Sit Chrisma tuum perfectum nobis Domine, à te benedictum, permanens in visciérbus nostris, in nomine Domini nostri Iesu Christi.
units.tr: I exorcise you, most unclean spirit, and every incursion and every phantasm of Satan, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, that you depart from this oil, so that a spiritual anointing may be made, for strengthening the temple of the living God, that the Holy Spirit may dwell in it, through the name of God the almighty Father, and through the name of Christ. We beseech you, Lord, send down the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, from heaven upon this fatness of the olive, which you have deigned to produce from the green tree, for the refreshment of mind and body, so that, anointed with every part of this heavenly medicinal ointment under your holy blessing, it may be a protection of mind and body, for driving out all pains, all infirmities, and every sickness of mind and body, wherewith you anointed your priests, kings, prophets and martyrs. May your chrism be perfect for us, Lord, blessed by you, abiding in our inmost parts, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: BALSAMI.
units.tr: OF BALSAM.

units.la: Suppliciter deposcimus, ut huic unguento, quod radix produxit stirpea, spiritualem gratiam largiendo, plenitudinem sanctificationis infundas. Sit nobis, Domine, fidei hilaritate conditum. Sit sacerdotalis unguti chrisma perpetuum: fit ad cœleste vexillum, impressione dignifimũ, ut quicunq; bapti-smate sacro renati, isto fuerint liquore perun-ēti, corporum atq; animarum benedictione plenissimam confequanter, & illi beatæ fidei collato munere perenniter amplientur.
units.tr: We humbly beg that you pour the fullness of sanctification into this ointment, which the stem of the tree has produced, bestowing spiritual grace. Lord, let it be seasoned with the cheerfulness of faith. Let it be the perpetual chrism of the priestly anointing: it is made as a heavenly banner, most worthy of the impression, so that all who have been reborn by the holy baptism and anointed with this liquid may obtain the fullest blessing of body and soul, and may be enriched forever with the gift of that blessed faith.

units.la: Balsamo cum modulo olei mixto: Oremus Dominum, quatenus hos ex diversis creaturarum speciebus liquores creatos, sanctæ Trinitatis perfectione benedicat, & benedicendo sanctificet, concedatq; ut simul permixti unum fiant, ut quicunq; inde exterius perundtus fuerit, ita interius liniatur, quòd omnibus corporalis materiæ carens, fe partícipem regni cœlestis effici mereatur.
units.tr: Over the balsam mixed with a small measure of oil: Let us pray the Lord that he bless these liquids, created from different kinds of creatures, with the perfection of the holy Trinity, and by blessing sanctify them, and grant that, being mixed together, they become one, so that whoever is anointed outwardly with it may be anointed inwardly as well, and, lacking nothing of corporeal matter, may deserve to be made a partaker of the heavenly kingdom.

units.la: Ad unctionem oculorum ægroti: Ungo oculos tuos oleo sanctificato, in nomine Patris &c. Periftam unctionem & suam piisimam misericordiam indulgat tibi Dominus, quicquid deliquisti per visum.
units.tr: For anointing the eyes of the sick: I anoint your eyes with sanctified oil, in the name of the Father, etc. May the Lord grant you the perfect anointing and his most merciful pardon, for whatever you have sinned through sight.

units.la: Sic etiam fi nares, labia, aures, pectus, manus, & pedes unguntur: Ungo &c.
units.tr: So also when the nostrils, lips, ears, breast, hands and feet are anointed: I anoint, etc.

units.la: Chrismatis, ad Baptismum infantis.
units.tr: Of the chrism for the baptism of an infant.

units.la: Exorcizo te, creatura, per Deum, ut omnis virtus adversarii, omnis exercitus diaboli, omnisq; incursio & omne phantasma Satanæ eradicetur & effugetur à te, ut fias omnibus, qui ex te ungendi sunt, in adoptionem filiorum, per Spiritum sanctum, in nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus Sancti.
units.tr: I exorcise you, creature, through God, that every power of the adversary, every army of the devil, and every incursion and every phantasm of Satan be uprooted and driven out of you, so that you may become, for all who are to be anointed with you, adoption as sons, through the Holy Spirit, in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Exprafatione, qua est commendatio oleorum: Ut hujus creaturæ pinguedinem sanctificare tuâ benedictione dignetis, & sancti Spiritus eiadmiscere virtutem, cooperante Filii tui potentiâ, à cujus nomine sancto chrisma nomen accepit, ut sit iis, qui renati fuerint ex aqua & Spiritu sancto, chrisma salutis, eosque æternæ vitæ participes, & cœlestis regni faciat consortes.
units.tr: In the preface, which is the commendation of the oils: That you deign to sanctify the fatness of this creature by your blessing, and to mingle in the power of the Holy Spirit, with the power of your Son cooperating, from whose holy name the chrism has taken its name, so that it may be a chrism of salvation to those who have been reborn of water and the Holy Spirit, and make them partakers of eternal life and companions of the heavenly kingdom.

units.la: Et, balsamo cum modico olei commixto: Hæc commixtio liquorum fiat omnibus ex eâ perunctis propitiatio & custodia salutaris in seculâ seculorum, Amen.
units.tr: And, with balsam mixed with a little oil: May this mixing of liquids become for all anointed with it a propitiation and saving protection for ever and ever, Amen.

units.la: Olei catechumenorum in confirmatione.
units.tr: Oil of the catechumens in confirmation.

units.la: Exorcizo te, creatura olei, in nomine Patris, Filii, & Sp. ✝ S. ut in hac invocatione Trinitatis atque unius virtute deitatis, omnis nequissima virtus adversarii, omnis inveterata malitia diaboli, omnis violenta incursio, omne confusum & cæcum phantasma, eradicetur & effugetur, & discedat à te, ut res divini sacramenti purificata fias, in adoptionem carnis & spiritus, iis, qui exteungendi sunt, in remissionem omnium peccatorum, ut efficiantur eorum corpora ad omnem gratiam spiritualem suscipiendam sanctificata.
units.tr: I exorcise you, creature of oil, in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy ✝ Spirit, that in this invocation of the Trinity and by the power of the one deity, every most wicked power of the adversary, every inveterate malice of the devil, every violent incursion, and every confused and blind phantasm, be uprooted and driven out and depart from you, so that you may be made purified as the matter of the divine sacrament, for the adoption of flesh and spirit, for those who are to be anointed with you, for the remission of all sins, so that their bodies may be sanctified to receive every spiritual grace.

units.la: Emittere digneris tuam benedictionem super hoc oleum, & tinctis beatæ regenerationis lavacro tribuas per unctionem hujus creaturæ purgationem mentis & corporis, per Dominum nostrum. Ut si quæ illis advenientium spirituum inhærere reliquiæ vel maculæ, ad tactum olei hujus sanctificati abscedant, nullus spiritualibus nequitiis locus, nulla refugii sit facultas, nulla infidiantib' malis latendi lacetia relinquatur: sed venientibus ad fidem servis tuis, & Sancti spiritus tui operatione mundandis, fit unctionis hujus præparatio utilis ad salutem, &c.
units.tr: Deign to send down your blessing upon this oil, and grant, through the anointing of this creature, to those bathed in the laver of blessed regeneration, the cleansing of mind and body, through our Lord. So that if any remnants or stains of the spirits that have come upon them cling to them, they may depart at the touch of this sanctified oil; let no place remain for spiritual wickedness, no opportunity of escape, and no hiding-place be left for the evil ones who lie in wait; but for your servants coming to faith, and to be cleansed by the working of your Holy Spirit, may the preparation of this anointing be useful for salvation, etc.

units.la: Ad oleum:
units.tr: To the oil:

units.la: Ave sanctum oleum, Ave sanctum oleum. Ave sanctum oleum.
units.tr: Hail, holy oil. Hail, holy oil. Hail, holy oil.

units.la: Ad balsamum:
units.tr: To the balsam:

units.la: Ave sanctum balsamum. Ave sanctum balsamum. Ave sanctum balsamum.
units.tr: Hail, holy balsam. Hail, holy balsam. Hail, holy balsam.

units.la: Et ad chrisma:
units.tr: And to the chrism:

units.la: Ave sanctum chrisma. Ave sanctum chrisma. Ave sanctum chrisma.
units.tr: Hail, holy chrism. Hail, holy chrism. Hail, holy chrism.

units.la: CANDELARUM, IN DIE purificationis.
units.tr: CANDLES, ON THE DAY OF THE PURIFICATION.

units.la: Domine Jesu Christe, fili Dei vivi, benedic candelas istas supplicationibus nostris, infunde eis Domine per virtutem sanctæ crucruncis, benedictionem cœlestem, qui eas ad repellendas tenebras humano generi tribuisti, talemque benedictionem signaculo sanctæ crucis accipiant, ut quibuscunque locis accensæ sive positæ fuerint, discedant principes tenebrarum, & contremiscant, & fugiant pavidi, cum omnibus ministris suis, de habitationibus illis, nec præsumant amplius inquietare aut molestare servientes tibi omnipotenti Deo.
units.tr: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, bless these candles at our supplication. Pour upon them, Lord, through the power of the holy cross, heavenly blessing, you who granted them to the human race to drive away darkness. May they receive such a blessing by the sign of the holy cross that, wherever they are lit or placed, the princes of darkness may depart and tremble and flee in fear, with all their ministers, from those dwellings, and may no longer presume to disturb or molest those who serve you, almighty God.

units.la: Cineris, in die Cinerum.
units.tr: Of the Ashes, on Ash Wednesday.

units.la: Omnipotens Deus, parce metuentibus, propitiare supplicantibus, & mittere dignerit sanctum Angelum tuum de cœlis, qui benedicat & sanctificet hos cineres, ut sint remedium salubre omnibus nomen tuum implorantibus, ac semetipsos pro conscientia delictorum suorum accusantibus, ante conspectum divinæ clementiæ tuæ facinora sua deplorantibus, vel serenissimam majestatem tuam supplicitër obnixeque flagitantibus, & præsta, per invocationem sanctissimi nominis tui, ut quicunque eos super se asperserint, pro redemtione peccatorum suorum corporis sanitatem & animæ tutelam percipiant.
units.tr: Almighty God, spare those who fear you, be merciful to those who entreat you, and deign to send your holy Angel from heaven to bless and sanctify these ashes, that they may be a healthful remedy for all who call upon your name, and for those who accuse themselves on account of the awareness of their sins, who lament their misdeeds before the sight of your divine mercy, or who humbly and earnestly beseech your most serene majesty. And grant, through the invocation of your most holy name, that whoever sprinkles them upon themselves may receive, for the redemption of their sins, health of body and protection of soul.

units.la: Et: Hos cineres, quos causâ proferendæ humilitatis atque promerendæ veniæ, capitibus nostris imponi decrevimus, benedicere pro tuâ pietate dignare, ut, qui nos cinerem esse, & ob pravitatis nostrae meritum in pul-verem reversuros cognoscimus, peccatorum omnium veniam & praemia poenitentibˣs re-promissa mifericorditer cofequi mereamur.
units.tr: And: Deign, in your goodness, to bless these ashes, which we have decided to place upon our heads for the sake of showing humility and earning pardon, so that we, who know that we are ash and that, on account of the merit of our wickedness, we shall return to dust, may mercifully deserve to obtain forgiveness of all our sins and the rewards promised to the penitent.

units.la: Et: Deus, qui humiliatione flecteris & sa-tisfactione placaris, aurem tuae pietatis inclina precibus nostris, & capitibus fervorum tuorum horum cineru aspersione attactis, effunde propitius gratiam tuae benedictionis, &c.
units.tr: And: O God, who are moved by humiliation and appeased by satisfaction, incline the ear of your goodness to our prayers, and, with the heads of your servants touched by the sprinkling of these ashes, graciously pour forth the grace of your blessing, etc.

units.la: ROSAE CONSECRATIO.
units.tr: THE CONSECRATION OF THE ROSE.

units.la: Dominica Laetare,
units.tr: On the Sunday Laetare,

units.la: Deus, cujus verbo & potentia facta sunt omnia, & cujus nutu universa diriguntur, qui es laetitia & gaudium omnium fidelium, magnitatem tuam supplices exoramus, ut hanc rosam odore vivuq; gratissimam, quam hodierna die in signum spiritualis laetitiae in manibus gestamus, benedicere & sanctificare tua pietate digneris, ut plebs tibi dicata ex jugo Babylonicae captivitatis educta, peruniti filii tui gratiam, qui est gloria & exultatio plebis Israel illius Hierusalem, quae sum est mater nostra, sinceris cordibus gaudium repraesentet, & quia ad honorem nominis tui Ecclesia tua hoc signo hodie exultat & gaudet, tu ei, Domine, verum & perfectum gaudium largiaris, & devotionem ejus acciens, peccata dimittas, fide repleas indulgentia foveas, misericordia protegas, adversitatibus tuas, prospera cuncta concedas, quaeque nus per fructum boni operis in odorem unguentorum illius floris transeat, qui de radice Jesse productus, flos campi & lilium convallium mystice praedicatur, cum quo in superna gloria cum sanctis omnibus sine fine laetetur.
units.tr: O God, by whose word and power all things were made, and by whose nod all things are directed, who art the joy and gladness of all the faithful, we humbly beseech thy majesty that thou wouldst deign, in thy goodness, to bless and sanctify this rose, most pleasing for its scent and its life, which on this day we carry in our hands as a sign of spiritual joy; so that thy people, dedicated to thee and led out from the yoke of the Babylonian captivity, may with sincere hearts represent the joy of the grace of thy well-beloved Son, who is the glory and exultation of the people of Israel and of that Jerusalem which is our mother. And since thy Church rejoices and exults today by this sign, to the honour of thy name, grant her, O Lord, true and perfect joy; and, receiving her devotion, forgive her sins, fill her with faith, cherish her with indulgence, protect her with mercy, turn away adversities and grant all prosperous things; and may what we are, through the fruit of good works, pass into the fragrance of the ointments of that flower which, sprung from the root of Jesse, is mystically proclaimed the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys, and with whom in heavenly glory we may rejoice with all the saints without end.

units.la: ROSÆ PRÆSENTATIO, AD magnum aliquem Principem.
units.tr: THE PRESENTATION OF THE ROSE, to some great Prince.

units.la: Accipe (inquit Pontifex) Rosam, de manibus nostris, qui, licet immeriti, locum Dei in terris tenemus, per quam designatur gaudium utriusque Hierusalem, triumphantis (scilicet & militantis Ecclesiae, per quam omnibus Christi fidelibus manifestatur flos ipse speciosissimus, qui est gaudium & corona Sanctorum omnium, suscipe hanc tu dilectissime fili, qui secundum seculum nobilis, potens, ac multa virtute praeditus es, ut amplius omni virtute in Christo, Domino nobiliteris, tanquam rosa plantata super rivos aquarum multarum, quam gratiam ex sua ubertate clementia tibi concedere dignetur, qui est trinus & unus in secula seculorum, Amen. In nomine Patris, & Filii, & Sp. S. Amen.
units.tr: The Pontiff says: "Receive this Rose from our hands. We, though unworthy, hold the place of God on earth. By it is signified the joy of both Jerusalems, the triumphant and the militant Church, through which the most beautiful flower itself, who is the joy and crown of all the saints, is made manifest to all the faithful of Christ. Receive it, most beloved son, you who are noble according to the world, powerful, and endowed with great virtue, so that you may be ennobled further in Christ our Lord in every virtue, like a rose planted beside streams of many waters. May he who is three and one, for ever and ever, deign to grant you this grace out of his abundant mercy. Amen. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen."

units.la: PALMARUM.
units.tr: OF THE PALMS.

units.la: Auge fidem in te sperantium, Deus, & supplicum preces clementer exaudi, & veniat super nos multiplex misericordia tua. Benedicantur & hi palmites olivarum, & sicut in figura Ecclesiae multiplicasti Noë egredientem de arca, & Moysen exeunrem de Ægypto, cum filiis Israël: ita nos portantes palmas & ramos olivarum, bonis actibus occurramus Christo, & per ipsum in gaudium introeamus æternum.
units.tr: "Increase the faith of those who hope in you, O God, and mercifully hear the prayers of your suppliants, and let your manifold mercy come upon us. Bless also these branches of olive, and, as you multiplied Noah coming out of the ark, and Moses coming out of Egypt with the sons of Israel, as a figure of the Church, so let us, carrying palms and olive branches, go out to meet Christ with good works, and through him enter into eternal joy."

units.la: Et: Petimus, ut hanc creaturam olivæ, quam ex ligni materiâ prodire jussisti, quamque columba rediens ad arcam proprio protulit ore, benedicere & sanctificare digneris, ut quicunque ex ea acceperint, accipiant sibi ad protectionem animæ & corporis, fiatque, domine, nostræ salutis remedium, tuæque gratiæ Sacramentum.
units.tr: And: "We ask that you deign to bless and sanctify this creature of the olive, which you commanded to spring from the wood, and which the dove, returning to the ark, carried in its own mouth, so that whoever receives from it may receive it for the protection of soul and body. May it be, O Lord, a remedy for our salvation and a sacrament of your grace."

units.la: Iterum: Qui populis obviam Jesu ramos portantibus benedixisti, benedic etiam hos ramos palmæ & olivæ, quos tui famuli ad honorem nominis tui fideliter suscipiunt, ut, in quemcunque locum introducti fuerint, tuam benedictionem habitatores loci illius consequantur, omni adversa valetudine fugatâ, dextera tua protegat, quos redemit Jesus Christus filius tuus dominus noster.
units.tr: Again: "You who blessed the peoples bearing branches to meet Jesus, bless also these branches of palm and olive, which your servants faithfully receive to the honour of your name, so that, into whatever place they are carried, the inhabitants of that place may obtain your blessing, every adverse sickness being put to flight, and that your right hand may protect those whom Jesus Christ your Son, our Lord, has redeemed."

units.la: Et: Deus, qui miro ordine dispositionis ex rebus etiam insensibilibus dispensatione nostræ salutis ostendere voluisti, &c. Et, qui per olivæ ramum pacem terris columbam nunciare jussisti, præsta quæsumus, ut hos olivæ cæterarumque arborum ramos cœlesti benedictione sanctifices, ut cuncto populo tuo proficiant ad salutem.
units.tr: And: "O God, who by a wonderful order of arrangement willed to show, through insensible things also, the dispensing of our salvation, etc. And you who commanded that peace be announced to the earth by the olive branch and the dove, grant, we beseech you, that you sanctify these branches of the olive and of other trees with heavenly blessing, so that they may profit your whole people unto salvation."

units.la: Item: Benedic, quæsumus domine, hos palmas palmarum seu olivarum ramos, & praesta, ut, quod populus tuus tua veneratione, hodiernâ die, corporaliter agit, hoc spiritualiter summâ devotione perficiat, de hoste victoriam reportando, & opus misericordiae summopere diligendo.
units.tr: Likewise: "Bless, we beseech you, Lord, these palms or branches of olive, and grant that what your people do bodily today in your veneration, they may carry out spiritually with the greatest devotion, winning victory over the enemy and cherishing the work of mercy above all."

units.la: Et: Benedicere dignare hos ramos palmarum caeterarumque frondium, ut omnes, qui eos laturi sunt, ita benedictionis tuae dono repleantur, quatenus & in hoc seculo hostis antiqui tentamenta superare, & in futuro cum palmâ victoriae & fructu bonorum operum valeant apparere.
units.tr: And: "Deign to bless these branches of palm and of other foliage, so that all who are to carry them may be filled with the gift of your blessing, that they may both in this world overcome the temptations of the ancient enemy, and in the future appear with the palm of victory and the fruit of good works."

units.la: IGNIS.
units.tr: OF FIRE.

units.la: In Sabbatho sancto.
units.tr: On Holy Saturday.

units.la: Adesto invocationibus nostris, & calorem hujus ignis, omnesque ejus alimonias gratiâ tuae benedictionis ita perfunde, ut omnia, quae hoc igne fuerint conflata sive calefacta, sint benedicta, omniq; humanae saluti proficua, omnesq; eo rationabiliter utentes, ardore Spiritus sancti, ad laudem tui nominis, corda eorum sentiant accendi.
units.tr: "Be present at our invocations, and so suffuse the heat of this fire and all its nourishments with the grace of your blessing, that all things which are fused or warmed by this fire may be blessed and profitable to all human salvation, and that all who use it reasonably may feel their hearts kindled by the ardour of the Holy Spirit, to the praise of your name."

units.la: Item: In quocunque loco, ex hujus aliquid sanctificationis mysterio fuerit deportatum, expulsâ diabolicæ fraudis nequitiâ, virtus tuae majestatis adiuvat.
units.tr: Likewise: "Wherever anything from this fire has been carried away by the mystery of its sanctification, the power of your majesty helps, the wickedness of diabolical fraud being driven out."

units.la: IGNIS,
units.tr: OF FIRE,

units.la: Quandocunque volueris,
units.tr: Whenever you wish,

units.la: Domine, Deus noster, Pater omnipotens, lumen indeficiens, conditor omnium luminum, exaudi nos famulos tuos, & benedic hunc ignem, qui tua sanctificatione atque benedictione consecretur, tu, qui illuminas omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum, illumina tenebras cordis nostri, & conscientias nostras igne tuae charitatis, ut tuo lumine igniti, tuo lumine illuminati, expulsis a cordibus nostris peccatorum tenebris, ad vitam te illustrante pervenire mereamur aeternam.
units.tr: "Lord our God, almighty Father, unfailing light, creator of all lights, hear us your servants and bless this fire, which is consecrated by your sanctification and blessing. You who illuminate every man coming into this world, illuminate the darkness of our heart, and our consciences with the fire of your love, so that, kindled by your light and enlightened by your light, the shadows of sins being cast out of our hearts, we may be deemed, under your guidance, to attain eternal life."

units.la: DE AGNVS DEI CONFECTIONE & benedictione.
units.tr: On the Making and Blessing of the Agnus Dei

units.la: Ad aquam: Domine Deus pater omnipotens, fabricator elementorum omnium, & conservator humani generis, datorque gratiae spiritualis, & largitor salutis aeternae, qui aquas ex Paradiso fonte manantes totam terram irrigare iussisti, super quas unigenitus tuus vestigiis pedibus ambulavit, & in sis baptizari dignatus est, quae una cum suo sanguine de latere sacratissimo profluxerunt, & baptizari in eis praecepit discipulis omnes gentes, adesto benignus & clemens, & nobis tua haec magnalia recolentibus adveniat, ut ea, quae in hoc aquarum vasculo ad gloriam tui nominis praeparato infundere decrevimus & immergere, benedicas, & benedicta sanctifica čtifices, quatenus ipsorum veneratione & honore nobis famulis tuis crimina diluantur, abstergantur maculæ peccatorum, impetrentur veniæ, gratiæ conferantur, ut tandem una cum sanctis & electis tuis vitam percipere mereamur æternam.
units.tr: At the water: Lord God, Father almighty, maker of all the elements and preserver of the human race, giver of spiritual grace and bestower of eternal salvation, who commanded the waters flowing from the fountain of Paradise to water the whole earth, over which your only-begotten Son walked with his feet, and in which he deigned to be baptized, waters that flowed out with his blood from his most sacred side, and who commanded the disciples to baptize all nations in them: be present with us graciously and mercifully, and come to us as we call to mind these your great works. Bless the things we have decided to pour into and immerse in this little vessel of water, prepared for the glory of your name, and, having blessed them, sanctify them, so that through the veneration and honor paid to them, our sins may be washed away and the stains of our wrongdoing wiped out for us your servants, pardon may be obtained, and grace bestowed, so that at last, together with your saints and elect, we may be worthy to receive eternal life.

units.la: Postquam balsamum in aquam in modum crucis infusum fuerit: Consecrare & sanctificare digneris, Domine, aquas istas per istam unctionem balsami, & nostram benedictionem, in nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus ✝ sancti. Amen.
units.tr: After the balsam has been poured into the water in the form of a cross: Lord, deign to consecrate and sanctify these waters by this anointing with balsam and by our blessing, in the name of the Father, the Son, and the ✝ Holy Spirit. Amen.

units.la: Et infuso chrismate, in modum crucis: Consecrare, & sanctificare digneris, Domine, aquas istas, per istam unctionem sancti Chrismatis, & nostram benedictionem, in nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus ✝ sancti. Amen.
units.tr: And with the chrism poured in, in the form of a cross: Lord, deign to consecrate and sanctify these waters by this anointing with holy chrism and by our blessing, in the name of the Father, the Son, and the ✝ Holy Spirit. Amen.

units.la: Et ad capsas, ubi sunt Agnus Dei: Deus omnium sanctificationum dominator, Dominus, cujus pietas sine fine permanet, qui Abraham patrem fidei nostræ præcepto tuo filium Isaac immolare disponentem in figuram redemptionis nostræ per arietem vepribus inhærentem ejus sacrificium consummare voluisti, quique Mosi famulo tuo legifero juge holocaustum præcepisti in agnis immaculatis offerri, te supplicitér deprecamur, ut nostræ vocis exoratus officio, has cereas formas innocentissimi agni imagine figuras benedicere, & per invocationem tui sancti nominis sanctificare digneris, ut per ejus tactum & visum fideles invitentur ad laudes, fragor grandinum, procella turbinum, impetus tempestatum, ventorum rabies, infesta tonitrua temperetur: fugiant atque tremiscant maligni spiritus ante sanctae crucis vexillum, quod in illis exsculptum est, cui flectitur omne genu &c. qui tanquam ovis ad occisionem ductus est, &c.
units.tr: And at the boxes where the Agnus Dei are: God, lord of all sanctification, Lord, whose mercy endures without end, who willed that Abraham, the father of our faith, who by your command was preparing to sacrifice his son Isaac, should complete his sacrifice as a figure of our redemption through the ram caught in the thicket; and who commanded your servant Moses, the lawgiver, that a continual burnt offering be offered in unblemished lambs: we humbly beseech you, that, being moved by the prayer of our voice, you would deign to bless these wax forms, figures of the most innocent Lamb, and sanctify them by the invocation of your holy name, so that through their touch and sight the faithful may be invited to praise you; and that the crash of hailstones, the storm of whirlwinds, the force of tempests, the rage of winds and the hostile thunderbolts may be tempered; and that the evil spirits may flee and tremble before the banner of the holy cross, which is engraved upon them, before which every knee bows, etc., who was led like a sheep to the slaughter, etc.

units.la: Er: Deus, qui legalium hostiarum & ceremoniarum es institutor &c. & plasmationem tuam his hostiis & sacrificiis obcediendo placari voluisti, sicut in sacrificio agni primitiarum instituisti Abel, & in oblatione Melchisedech sacerdotis tui, atque immolatione hostiarum, agnorum, arietum, & taurorum pinguium, Abrahae, Mosi & Aaron famulis tuis.&c. Et sicut ille Agnus, de cujus sanguine postes & super limina domus linebantur, immolatus, populum tuum a persecutione Aegyptiaca media nocte liberavit, & quemadmodum ille agnus innocens tua voluntate immolatus in ara crucis Jesus Christus filius, protoplasto nostrum de diabolica potestate eripuit: sic isti agni immaculati virtutem illam accipiant, quos consecrandos offerim inconspectu divinae majestatis tuae. Tu eos benedicere, sanctificare, & consecrare digneris, ut tuâ largâ benedictione sanctificati eandem virtute accipiant, contra omnes diabolicas versutias, & fraudes maligni spiritus, ut illos devotè super se ferentibus nulla tempestas eisdem prævaleat, nulla adversitas dominetur, nulla aura pestilens, neq; aeris corruptio, nullusq; morbus caducus, nulla maris procella, & tempestas, nullum incendiū neq; iniquitas dominetur eis, neq; prævaleat homo partus cum matre incolumis conservetur.
units.tr: And: God, who are the founder of the legal sacrifices and ceremonies, etc., and who willed to be appeased by the obedience of your creature to these victims and sacrifices, as you appointed in the sacrifice of the firstlings Abel, and in the offering of Melchizedek, your priest, and in the slaughter of victims, lambs, rams and fat bullocks, for Abraham, Moses and Aaron, your servants, etc. And just as that Lamb, whose blood was smeared on the doorposts and lintels of the house, when it was slain, freed your people from Egyptian persecution at midnight, and just as that innocent Lamb, Jesus Christ, your Son, sacrificed by your will on the altar of the cross, snatched our first parent from the power of the devil: so may these unblemished lambs, which we offer to be consecrated in the sight of your divine majesty, receive that same power. Deign to bless, sanctify and consecrate them, so that, sanctified by your abundant blessing, they may receive the same virtue against all the devil's cunning and the frauds of the evil spirit; so that for those who devoutly carry them, no storm may prevail, no adversity may rule, no pestilent air, no corruption of the atmosphere, no falling sickness, no storm or tempest at sea, no fire, and no wickedness may have power over them; and that a woman in labor may be kept safe with her child, so that no man may prevail.

units.la: Iterum: Sic istos Agnos benedicere, sanctificare, & consecrare digneris, quatenus eos de vote deferetes, ob reverentiam & honorem nominis tui, liberetur ab omni inundatione aquarum, & ab omni fluctuatione diabolicæ potestatis, & à morte subitaneâ, per virtutem passionis Jesu Christi.
units.tr: Again: Deign to bless, sanctify and consecrate these Lambs, so that those who carry them from their vows, out of reverence and honor for your name, may be freed from every flood of waters, from every surge of the devil's power, and from sudden death, through the power of the passion of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Mox ad Agnus Dei baptizatos: Quæsumus Domine, hi Agni sacrâ & perenni undâ balsamoq; sacri chrismatis perfusi, tu illos benedicere, sanctificare, & consecrare digneris, quatenus à te benedicti virtutem accipiant contra omnia diabolica tentamenta, & omnes portantes tuti esse possint inter adversa & prospera, & tuâ consolatione acceptâ nullum periculum timeant, nullamq; formidet umbram, nulla saevitia diabolica aut versutia humana eis nocebit: sed fortitudine tuæ virtutis roborati, tuâ consolatione glorientur.
units.tr: Immediately, to the Agnus Dei that have been baptized: We beseech you, Lord, that you deign to bless, sanctify and consecrate these Lambs, which have been sprinkled with holy and everlasting water and with the balsam of holy chrism; so that, blessed by you, they may receive power against all diabolical temptations, and that all who carry them may be safe in adversity and in prosperity; and that, having received your consolation, they may fear no danger and dread no shadow; that no diabolical cruelty or human cunning may harm them, but being strengthened by the fortitude of your power, they may glory in your comfort.

units.la: Domine Jesu Christe, qui vere es agnus innocens. nocens, sacerdos & hostia, Tu vere es agnus immolatus &c. Rogamus ergo clementiam tuam, ut hos agnos immaculatos benedicere, sanctificare, & confectrare digneris, quos de cera virginea in tuum honorem formavimus, per opera crucis, & sacra unda, balsamoq; & sacro chrismate liquoris confecti in sanctificationem tuae conceptionis, quam absq; contagione ac propagine humana, sola divina virtute suscepisti, sic eos defendentes tueris, protegas & defendas ab omni periculo incendii, fulguris, procellae, & tempestatis, & ab omni adversitate custodi, per mysterium passionis tuae, & sic eos liberare digneris ab omnibus periculis, & in puerperio laborantes, sicut matrem tuam ab omni periculo liberasti, & Susannam de falso crimine, & B. Theclam virginem & martyrem tuam ab incediis, & Petrum a vinculis absoluto illesum abire fecisti: ita nos ab hoc seculo illaesos abire facias, ut tecum sine fine vivere valeamus.
units.tr: Lord Jesus Christ, who truly are the innocent Lamb, both priest and victim, you truly are the Lamb slain, etc. We therefore beseech your mercy that you deign to bless, sanctify and consecrate these unblemished lambs, which we have formed in your honor from virgin wax, through the work of the cross, the holy water, the balsam and the holy chrism of a prepared liquid, for the sanctification of your conception, which you received without contagion or human seed, by divine power alone. So, defending them, keep them, protect and defend them from every danger of fire, lightning, storm and tempest, and guard them from every adversity through the mystery of your passion. Deign thus to free them from all dangers, and those who labor in childbirth, just as you freed your mother from every danger, and as you kept Susanna from the false accusation, your blessed virgin and martyr Thecla from the fires, and made Peter, when loosed from his chains, depart unharmed: so make us depart unharmed from this world, that we may be able to live with you without end.

units.la: Urbanus V. ad Imperatorem gracum tres Agnus Dei misit, cum his versiculis:
units.tr: Pope Urban V sent three Agnus Dei to the Greek emperor, with these verses:

units.la: Balsamum, & munda cera, cum chrismatis unda, Conficiunt Agnum, quod munus do tibi magnum, Fonte velut natum per mysticam sanctificatum, Fulgura desursum depellit, omne malignum Peccatum frangit, ut Christi sanguis, & angit, Pragnans seu satur, simul & partus liberatur, Dona defert dignis, virtutem destruit ignis, Portatus munde de fluctibus eripit unda.
units.tr: Balsam, and pure wax, with the water of chrism, they make a Lamb, which I give you as a great gift. Born, as it were, from the fountain, and sanctified by mystical rite, it drives off lightning from above and breaks every evil sin, as Christ's blood does, and... The pregnant or the full, and at once the woman in labor is delivered. It bestows gifts on the worthy and destroys the power of fire. Carried, it snatches the clean from the waves of the flood.

units.la: III. DE IIS, QVAE EXtra templum. Cœmeterii consecratio.
units.tr: III. Concerning those things outside the church. The consecration of a cemetery.

units.la: In medio Letania: Ut hoc cœmeterium purgare & benedicere digneris, te rogamus, audi nos.
units.tr: In the middle of the Litany: That it may please you to cleanse and bless this cemetery, we beseech you, hear us.

units.la: Ut ad introitum nostrum purgetur, benedicatur, consecretur, & sanctificetur hoc cœmeterium, ut humana corpora, hic post vitæ cursum quiescentia, post hujus vitæ volumina, mercantur adipisci perennis gaudia vitæ.
units.tr: That this cemetery may be cleansed, blessed, consecrated and sanctified at our entrance, so that human bodies resting here after the course of this life may, after the turns of this life, obtain the joys of everlasting life.

units.la: Et in collecta: Ut ibi sepeliendi veniam accipiant peccatorum, & in resurrectione sine peccato invetiantur.
units.tr: And in the Collect: That those to be buried there may receive forgiveness of their sins, and be found without sin at the resurrection.

units.la: II. IN STATU OECONOMICO. DOMUS NOVÆ, VEL A Dæmone vexata.
units.tr: II. CONCERNING THE ECONOMIC STATE. OF A NEW HOUSE, OR ONE VEXED BY A DEMON.

units.la: Deus, qui sacerdotibus tuis præcæteris tantam gratiam contulisti, ut, quicquid in tuo nomine digne perfecteq; ab iis agitur, à te fieri credatur, quæsumus tuam clementiam immensam, ut, quod modo visitaturi sumus, visites, & quicquid benedicturi, benedicas, & ad ea, quæ acturi sumus, dexteram tuæ potentiæ extendas, sintq; ad nostræ humilitatis ingressu & introitu, sanctorum tuorum meritis, fuga dæmonum, & Angeli pacis ingressus.
units.tr: God, who has given your priests such great grace above others that whatever is done worthily and perfectly in your name by them is believed to be done by you, we beseech your immense mercy: that you would visit what we are about to visit, bless what we are about to bless, and stretch out the right hand of your power to the things we are about to do; and may there be, at the entry and coming in of our lowliness, through the merits of your saints, the flight of demons and the entrance of the angel of peace.

units.la: Domum tuam, Domine, clementer ingredere, & præsta, ut in hac domo nulla mali ignoscat. -lignorum spirituum dominetur nequitia, Deus, qui in omni loco dominationis tuae totus assistis, totus operaris, adesto supplicationibus nostris, ut hujus domus ædificatae sis protector, & nulla hic nequitia contrariae potestatis obsistar, sed virtute spiritus sancti & operatione, fiat tibi hic primum servitium & devota libertas existat.
units.tr: Enter your house, Lord, mercifully, and grant that in this house no wickedness of evil spirits may hold sway. O God, who stand wholly present and wholly at work in every place of your dominion, be present to our prayers, that you may be the protector of this house now built, and that no wickedness of the opposing power may resist here; but by the virtue and working of the Holy Spirit, may this place first become a service to you, and a devoted liberty may exist here.

units.la: Deus, qui in omni loco dominationis tuae dedicator assistis, exaudi nos, quaesumus, ut inviolabilis hujus domus permaneat benedictio, & beneficia tui muneris universitas, quae supplicat, mereatur.
units.tr: O God, who stand present as the dedicator in every place of your dominion, hear us, we beseech you, that the inviolable blessing of this house may remain, and that the whole of the benefits of your gift, for which we supplicate, may be deserved.

units.la: Incensi benedictio: Per intercessionem beati Michaelis Archangeli, stantis à dextris altaris incensi & omnium sanctorum Angelorum, incensum istud digneris Domine benedicere, & in odorem suavitatis accipere.
units.tr: Blessing of the incense: Through the intercession of blessed Michael the Archangel, who stands at the right of the altar of incense, and of all holy angels, deign, Lord, to bless this incense and to receive it as an odour of sweetness.

units.la: Incenso in ignem posito: Incensum à te benedictum, ascendat ad te Domine, & descendat super nos misericordia tua.
units.tr: When the incense is placed on the fire: Let the incense blessed by you ascend to you, Lord, and let your mercy descend upon us.

units.la: Facta cruce † super domum, et in eâ habitantes: In nomine Patris † & Filii † & Spiritus sancti. Amen.
units.tr: When the cross is made † over the house and over those dwelling in it: In the name of the Father † and of the Son † and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

units.la: Deniq; benedictio ad omnes: Benedictio Dei omnipotentis Patris, & Filii, & Spiritus sancti, descendat super vos & domum istam, & maneat semper.
units.tr: Finally, the blessing for all: May the blessing of almighty God, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, descend upon you and upon this house, and remain forever.

units.la: Loci, vel Domus.
units.tr: Of a place, or a house.

units.la: Benedic Domine Deus omnipotens locum istum (domum istam) ut sit in eo (in eâ)sanitas, castitas, victoria, virtus, humilitas, bonitas, & mansuetudo, plenitudo legis, & gratiarum actio Deo Patri, & Filio, & Spiritui sancto, & hæc benedictio maneat super hunc locum (super hanc domum) & super habitantes in eo (in eâ) per &c.
units.tr: Bless, Lord God almighty, this place (this house), that there may be in it (in her) health, chastity, victory, virtue, humility, goodness and gentleness, fullness of the law, and thanksgiving to God the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit; and may this blessing remain upon this place (this house) and upon those dwelling in it (in her), through, etc.

units.la: Thalami: Benedic Domine thalamum hunc, & omnes habitantes in eo, ut in tua pace consistant, & in tua voluntate permaneant & senescant, & multiplicentur in longitudinem dierum.
units.tr: Of a bedchamber: Bless, Lord, this bedchamber and all who dwell in it, that they may stand in your peace, remain in your will, grow old, and be multiplied to length of days.

units.la: Putei novi.
units.tr: Of a new well.

units.la: Deus, qui in hujus putei altitudinem, percrepidinem sistularum, copiam aquarum manare jussisti, præsta, ut te jubente atq; benedicente, per nostræ officium functionis, repulsis hinc plantasmaticis calliditatibus atque insidiis diabolicis, purificatus atque emundatus semper hic puteus perseveret.
units.tr: O God, who commanded that in the depth of this well, through the abundance of its pipes, a copious supply of water should flow, grant that, at your bidding and blessing, through the office of our ministry, the illusory wiles and diabolical snares being driven away, this well may always persevere purified and cleansed.

units.la: Baculi, ad iter.
units.tr: Of a staff, for a journey.

units.la: Accipe hunc baculum ad sustentationem itineris piæ peregrinationis tuæ, ut vincere valeas omnes inimicos, & securus perveni-re possis ad limina tuta, ut peracto obœdi-entiæ cursu, ad nos revertaris cum gaudio.
units.tr: Receive this staff for the support of your pious pilgrimage, that you may be able to overcome all enemies and may come safely to secure thresholds, so that, the course of obedience being completed, you may return to us with joy.

units.la: Peregrinorum.
units.tr: Of pilgrims.

units.la: In nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi, accipe hanc sportam, habitum peregrinationis tuæ. ut bene castigatus & fanatus atq; emundatus pervenire merearis ad sanctorum limina, quo pergere cupis, ut, perasto itinere, ad nos incolumis & alacer reverti mererâris.
units.tr: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, receive this bag, the garb of your pilgrimage, so that, well chastened, healed and cleansed, you may deserve to arrive at the thresholds of the saints to which you wish to go, and that, the journey being completed, you may deserve to return to us safe and cheerful.

units.la: Novorum fructuum.
units.tr: Of new fruits.

units.la: Benedic, Domine, hunc fructum novum arborum, ut hi, qui utuntur eo, sint mente & corpore sanitati restituti.
units.tr: Bless, Lord, this new fruit of the trees, that those who use it may be restored to health in mind and body.

units.la: Ficuum, vel uvæ.
units.tr: Of figs, or grapes.

units.la: Benedic, Domine, hos fructus novos uvæ sive ficuum, quæ tu Domine per rorem cœli & inundantiam pluviarum & tempora serena atq; tranquilla, ad maturitatem perducere dignatus es, ad percipiendum nobis cum gratiarum actione.
units.tr: Bless, Lord, these new fruits of the grape or the fig, which you, Lord, have deigned to bring to ripeness by the dew of heaven, the abundance of rains, and serene and tranquil weather, that we may receive them with thanksgiving.

units.la: Vinagii.
units.tr: Of wine.

units.la: Benedic, Domine, istam creaturam vini vel N. ut sit remedium salutare humano generi, & præsta, ut per tui sanctissimi nominis invocationem, & per interceßionem beatæ Mariæ semper virginis, vel B. N. ac sanctorum omnium, ut quicunque ex eo vel ex ea gustaverint vel sumserint, corporis sanitatem & animæ tutelam accipiant.
units.tr: Bless, Lord, this creature of wine (or of N.), that it may be a saving remedy for the human race; and grant that, through the invocation of your most holy name, and through the intercession of blessed Mary, ever virgin, or of blessed N., and of all saints, whoever taste or partake of it may receive health of body and protection of soul.

units.la: Vini, pro amore Johannis Evangelistæ.
units.tr: Of wine, for the love of John the Evangelist.

units.la: Benedicere & sanctificare dignetis hanc creaturam vini, ut quicunque ex ea gustaverint, per intercessionem Mariæ & Johannis Apostoli vitam consequantur æternam, extinguatur ab omnibus digne sumentibus, si quid venenosum sumserint.
units.tr: Deign to bless and sanctify this creature of wine, that whoever taste of it may obtain eternal life through the intercession of Mary and of the Apostle John; and may it extinguish any poison in all who partake of it worthily, if they have taken anything venomous.

units.la: Item: Benedicere digneris hanc creaturam vini, ut omnes ex eo sumentes, expulso omni nocivo gustu, infuso tuae benedictionis mysterio, mereantur in corpore & anima misericorditer exhilarari.
units.tr: Likewise: Deign to bless this creature of wine, that all who partake of it, every harmful taste being expelled and the mystery of your blessing infused, may deserve to be mercifully gladdened in body and soul.

units.la: Item: Benedic hujus substantiam vini, ut qui de eo quacumque gustaverint vel sumserint, vitam consequatur sempiternam.
units.tr: Likewise: Bless the substance of this wine, that whoever taste or partake of it in any way may obtain everlasting life.

units.la: Benedic hanc creaturam vini, tua sancta benedictione coelesti, ut omnibus, cum fide, reverentia & gratiarum actione ex eo sumentibus, sit salus mentis & corporis, atque contra omnes morbos, & venenata & immunda, atque universas inimicorum insidias, tutamentum.
units.tr: Bless this creature of wine with your holy heavenly blessing, that to all who partake of it with faith, reverence and thanksgiving there may be health of mind and body, and protection against all diseases, poisonings and uncleanness, and against all the snares of enemies.

units.la: Item: Sicut Johannes de calice bibens non est laesus: ita & isti in amore tuo, & beati Johannis, de calice isto bibentes, meritis ipsius ab omni aegritudine absolvantur.
units.tr: Likewise: As John, drinking from the cup, was not harmed, so may those who drink from this cup in your love and in that of blessed John be absolved by his merits from every sickness.

units.la: Item: Ab hostium visibilium insidiis, & ab omni cibo & potu mortifero & pestifero corporis & animae mereantur illaesi tua misericordia mediante conservari.
units.tr: Likewise: From the snares of visible enemies, and from every deadly and pestilential food and drink, may they deserve to be preserved unharmed in body and soul through your mercy.

units.la: Item: Ut ubicunque ipsa creatura vini aspersa vel propinata fuerit, divinae benedictionis opulentia repleatur: & omnibus accipientibus ex ea cum gratiarum actione, in viscer ibus eorum sanctificetur.
units.tr: Likewise: Wherever this creature of wine is sprinkled or poured out, may it be filled with the abundance of divine blessing; and may it be sanctified in the bowels of all who receive it with thanksgiving.

units.la: Benedictus Trinitatis descendat super hanc creaturarum vini, ut fit omnibus ex eâ fumentibus remedium contra periculum corporis & animæ,& præguftatio ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: May the blessing of the Trinity descend upon this creature of wine, so that it may be a remedy for all who partake of it against danger to body and soul, and a foretaste of eternal life.

units.la: Item: Benedictio Dei Patris,& Filii,& Spiritus sancti descendat & maneat super hanc creaturam vini, ut fit omnibus fumentibus remedium contra periculum corporis & animæ, & ad vitam æternam certa & libera deductio.
units.tr: Likewise: May the blessing of God the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, descend and remain upon this creature of wine, so that it may be a remedy for all who partake of it against danger to body and soul, and a sure and free guide to eternal life.

units.la: Herbarum & frondium & florum, in die affumtionis Mariæ.
units.tr: Of herbs, and fronds, and flowers, on the day of Mary's Assumption.

units.la: Exorcifo te creatura frondium & florum, in nomine Patris omnipotentis, & in nomine †Filii ejus, & in virtute Spiritus †sancti. Proinde omnis virtus adversarii, omnibus exercitus diaboli, omnis potestas inimici, omnis incursio dæmonum eradicare & explantare ab hac creatura frondium vel rum, ut ad Dei gratiam festinantium vestigia non sequaris.
units.tr: I exorcise you, creature of fronds and flowers, in the name of God the Father almighty, and in the name of his Son †, and in the power of the Holy †Spirit. Therefore, let every power of the adversary, every army of the devil, every dominion of the enemy, and every assault of demons be uprooted and plucked out from this creature of fronds and flowers, so that you may not follow the footsteps of those who hasten toward the grace of God.

units.la: Item: Conferant tam corporis quàm animæ sanitatem. Et ab hominibus pecoribusque, gustantibus, omnem putredinem & omne phantasma diaboli, & omnem morbum & omnem dolum expellere digneris.
units.tr: Likewise: May they bring health both of body and of soul. And deign to drive out from men and beasts who taste of them all putrefaction, every phantasm of the devil, every sickness and every deceit.

units.la: Item: Ut quisquis languore depressus, ex eis aliquid degustaverit, Ecclesiæ tuæ reprae-sentatus, optatæ munus salutis percipiat, te donante.
units.tr: Likewise: So that whoever, weighed down by sickness, has tasted any of them, presented to your Church, may receive, by your gift, the reward of the salvation he longed for.

units.la: AQVA.
units.tr: WATER.

units.la: Exorcifo te, creatura aquæ, ut omnis virtus adversarii, ab hac creatura aquæ eradicetur & effugetur.
units.tr: I exorcise you, creature of water, that every power of the adversary may be rooted out and driven away from this creature of water.

units.la: PANIS.
units.tr: BREAD.

units.la: Domine S. Pater, omnipotens æterne Deus, benedicere dignéris hunc panem tua sancta spirituali benedictione, ut sit omnibus sumentibus salus mentis & corporis, atq; contra omnes morbos, & universas inimicorum insidias auxilium & tutamen, per dominum nostrum Jesum Christum filium tuum, panem, qui de cælo descendit, & dat vitam & salutem mundo, & tecum vivit. &c.
units.tr: Lord, holy Father, almighty eternal God, deign to bless this bread with your holy spiritual blessing, so that it may be a health of mind and body for all who eat it, and a help and protection against all diseases and all the snares of enemies, through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, the bread which came down from heaven and gives life and salvation to the world, and who lives with you, etc.

units.la: PANIS ET LAGANORUM.
units.tr: BREAD AND FLATCAKES.

units.la: Benedic, Domine, creaturam istam panis, sicut benedixisti quinque panes in deserto, ut omnes gustantes ex ea, accipiant tam corporis quam animæ sanitatem.
units.tr: Bless, Lord, this creature of bread, as you blessed the five loaves in the wilderness, so that all who taste of it may receive health of body and of soul.

units.la: PLACENTARUM.
units.tr: OF CAKES.

units.la: Sint in anima alimentum, gustantesq; ex eis tam corporis, quam anima accipiant sanitatem.
units.tr: Let them be nourishment for the soul, and let those who taste of them receive health of body and of soul.

units.la: CARNIUM, OVIUM, & AVIUM.
units.tr: OF MEATS, EGGS, AND BIRDS.

units.la: Dignare, Domine Deus omnipotens, benedicere & sanctificare has ovium sive avium carnes, ut quicunque ex populis tuis fidelibus de eis comederint, omni benedictione cœlesti & gratiæ tuæ saturitate repleantur in bonis.
units.tr: Deign, Lord God almighty, to bless and sanctify these flesh meats of sheep or birds, so that whoever of your faithful people eat of them may be filled with every heavenly blessing and with the abundance of your grace, and be made rich in good things.

units.la: LARDI.
units.tr: OF LARD.

units.la: Benedic Domine creaturam istam lardi, ut sit re...
units.tr: Bless, Lord, this creature of lard, that it may be...

units.la: X J. fit re&c. sit remedium salutare generi humano, & pro-sta per invocationem nominis tui, ut quicunqueex eo sumserint, corporis sanitatem & animae tu-telam percipiant.
units.tr: ...etc. that it may be a healthful remedy for the human race, and grant, through the invocation of your name, that whoever has taken of it may receive health of body and protection of soul.

units.la: CASEI.
units.tr: OF CHEESE.

units.la: Dignare benedicere & sanctificare hanc creaturam caseï, ut quicunq; fideliũ tuorũ de eâ comederint, omni benedictione coelesti & gratiæ tuæ sanctitate repleantur.
units.tr: Deign to bless and sanctify this creature of cheese, so that whoever of your faithful people eat of it may be filled with every heavenly blessing and the holiness of your grace.

units.la: CASEI & OVORUM.
units.tr: OF CHEESE AND EGGS.

units.la: Deus creator & conservator generis humani, dator gratiæ spiritualis, largitor aeternæ salutis, Domine, effunde benedictionem tuam super hanc creaturam casei & ovorum, ut armata coelesti defensione, quicunque ex eis gustaverit, sibi proficiat ad aeternam salutem.
units.tr: God, creator and preserver of the human race, giver of spiritual grace, bestower of eternal salvation, Lord, pour out your blessing upon this creature of cheese and eggs, so that, armed with heavenly defence, whoever tastes of them may profit to eternal salvation.

units.la: OVORUM.
units.tr: OF EGGS.

units.la: Subveniat quæsumus Domine tuæ benedictionis gratia huic ovorum creaturæ, de quâ pullos gallinarum procreare dignatus es, ut cibus salubris fiat fidelibus tuis, in tuarum gratiarum actione fumentibus.
units.tr: We beseech you, Lord, let the grace of your blessing come to the aid of this creature of eggs, from which you have deigned to bring forth the chicks of hens, so that it may become wholesome food for your faithful, who partake of it with thanksgiving for your graces.

units.la: AGNI IN PASCHATE.
units.tr: OF THE PASCHAL LAMB.

units.la: Deus, qui per famulum tuum Moysen, in liberatione populi tui de Aegypto, agnum occidi jussisti, in similitudinem domini nostri Iesu Christi, & utrosq; postes domorum de sanguine hujus agni perungi praecepisti, ita benedicere & sanctificare dignerus hanc creaturam carnis, quam nos famuli tui, ad laudem tuam fume-
units.tr: God, who through your servant Moses, in the liberation of your people from Egypt, commanded a lamb to be slain, as a likeness of our Lord Jesus Christ, and commanded that both door-posts of the houses be anointed with the blood of this lamb, deign so to bless and sanctify this creature of flesh, which we your servants wish to receive to your praise

units.la: rı redefideramus, per resurrectionem domini nostri Jesu Christi.
units.tr: through the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: GENERALIS.
units.tr: GENERAL.

units.la: Benedic, domine, creaturam istam, ut sit remedium salutare generi humano, & praesta per invocationem sancti nominis tui, ut quicunque ex ea sumserit vel gustaverit, corporis sanitatem & animae tutelam percipiat.
units.tr: Bless, Lord, this creature, so that it may be a healthful remedy for the human race, and grant, through the invocation of your holy name, that whoever eats or tastes of it may receive health of body and protection of soul.

units.la: Item: Tu, Domine, mitte Spiritum tuum Sanctum in hanc creaturam, ut qui ex ea gustaverint, proficiat illis ad aeternam salutem.
units.tr: Likewise: You, Lord, send your Holy Spirit upon this creature, so that it may profit those who taste of it to eternal salvation.

units.la: VESTIUM.
units.tr: OF GARMENTS.

units.la: Domine Deus bonarum virtutum dator, & omnium benedictionum largus infusor, te supplices deprecamur, ut hanc vestem benedicere & sanctificare digneris, ut hac indutus famulus tuus N. salutem animae, & corporis requiem acquirere possit.
units.tr: Lord God, giver of good virtues and generous pourer-out of all blessings, we humbly beseech you to deign to bless and sanctify this garment, so that your servant N., clothed in it, may obtain salvation of soul and rest of body.

units.la: EXEMPLUM, QUAM REM AGANT sacrificuli sterio, dum consecrationem seu benedictionem conficiunt.
units.tr: An example of what the little priests do when they perform consecration or blessing.

units.la: Anno Christi 1595. die Veneris, ipso Quadragesimae tempore, Sacrificulus quidam Wormatiensis, in vicinia Pfeddershemii, ab uno, ex convivis pluribus, cui is notus erat, in hospitium non invitus introducebatur. Cumque caro assata de vitulo ab hospite apportaretur, & omnium oculi in sacrificulum conjecti essent, qualem is sele gerere vellet: Faxo, inquit ille, ut de hoc fer-culo, die atque tempore isto, conscientia illasa mihi vesci liceat. Proinde exurgens, & oratione ad ferculum propositum conversa; Præcipio, inquit, tibi, caro vitulina, ut fias piscis, in nomine Patris, & Filii, & Spiritus sancti. Amen.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 1595, on a Friday in Lent itself, a certain little priest of Worms was taken, not unwillingly, into the lodging of a host near Pfeddersheim. He had been introduced there by one of the many guests, a man who knew him. When roast veal was brought in by the host and everyone's eyes were fixed on the little priest, to see how he would conduct himself, he said: "I will make it so that I may eat of this dish, on this day and at this time, with a conscience unharmed." Then, rising and turning his words to the dish before him, he said: "I command you, veal, to become fish, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen."

units.la: Mox confidens, hospites affatur subridens: Jam mihi quoque de hoc asso pisce, qui prius caro vituli erat, vesci impune licet. Animadvertens autem, rem istam præsentibus convivis atque ipsi hospiti videri ridiculam, mox facti rationem reddere paratus, Si, inquit, ex panis frustulo ipsum mihi corpus Christi conficere, vi consecrationis, in Missa administratione, licet: quidni ex vitulina carne piscem, vi Benedictionis divina mihi conficere per transsubstantiationem liceat? Qui enim me creavit sine me, is jam non creatur sine me. Protinus igitur ferculo propositio, in portiones minutiores concisio, optimam de renibus partem sibi reservavit, reliquis inter cæteros liberaliter distributis; quos monuit simul, ut de pisce isto hilariter vescentur.
units.tr: Immediately, growing confident, he addressed the guests with a smile: "Now I too may eat freely of this roasted fish, which was veal a moment ago." But noticing that the guests and the host himself found the matter laughable, he was ready at once to give an account of what he had done. "If," he said, "by the power of consecration, I may at the administration of the Mass make the very body of Christ out of a crumb of bread, why may I not, by the power of the divine blessing, make a fish for myself out of veal, through transubstantiation? For he who created me without me is now not created without me." Straightaway he set the dish before himself, cut it into smaller portions, kept the best part from the kidneys for himself, and generously distributed the rest among the others, at the same time urging them to eat of that fish cheerfully.

units.la: II. Libri pars: QUOS EX SANCTIS, QUIBUS, PONTIFICII PATRONOS AC DEOS TUTELARES assignarint.
units.tr: II. Part of the book: WHOM THE PAPISTS HAVE ASSIGNED FROM AMONG THE SAINTS AS PATRONS AND TUTELARY GODS.

units.la: HActenus, Lector Christiane, de horrenda Idololatria Pontificia, quæ in sanctorum Invocatione committitur, etiam de salutatione Angelica, quam Monachi imprudentes in formam precum commutare non dubitarunt, egimus plus satis. Eaque refutatio ut evidentior tibi redderetur, placuit exempla nō pauca, & illa quidem maximè perspicua subjicere, ad quorum commemorationem vel cordatus pectore toto cohorrescat. Denique formulas nonnullas magicæ & in Deum blasphemæ consecrationis addere libuit.
units.tr: Hitherto, Christian reader, we have discussed the horrid Papist idolatry committed in the invocation of saints, and also the Angelic salutation, which the unwary monks did not hesitate to turn into a form of prayer, more than enough. To make this refutation more evident to you, we decided to add not a few examples, and indeed the most conspicuous ones, at the mere recollection of which any discerning person should shudder to the depths of his heart. Finally, we were pleased to add some formulas of magical consecration that blaspheme God.

units.la: Reliquum est, ut, cùm opusculum hoc, præter opinionem, longiùs excrescat, breviter de secunda & tertia libelli parte, & earum quidem illa de Sanctorum patrocinio, de eorundem Reliquiis hac postrema deinceps agatur.
units.tr: It remains, since this little work, contrary to expectation, has grown rather long, that we briefly treat of the second and third parts of the booklet: the first of these concerns the patronage of the saints, and the last their relics.

units.la: M. Ritus Sacrificiorum. APUD ETHNICOS.
units.tr: M. Rites of sacrifice. AMONG THE HEATHENS.

units.la: Aqua vino admiscebatur. Manus lavabantur. Huc & illuc se vertit Sacerdos, circa aram, vel si respondum dandum, agitatus afflatu Spiritus divini. Ad Orientem sacrificium fiebat. Cerei circa imagines accendebantur. Imagines gestabantur. Thus incensum offerebatur. Hostia vendebantur.
units.tr: Water was mixed with wine. Hands were washed. The priest turned this way and that around the altar or, when an answer had to be given, was moved by the breath of the divine Spirit. The sacrifice was made facing east. Wax candles were lit around the images. Images were carried about. Incense was offered. Victims were sold.

units.la: Sacra vestes induebantur. Ad altare sacrificabatur.
units.tr: Sacred vestments were put on. The sacrifice was offered at the altar.

units.la: Sacrificia varia perac̈ta, etiam matutina, & nocturna.
units.tr: Various sacrifices were performed, also morning and night sacrifices.

units.la: APUD PAPISTAS.
units.tr: AMONG THE PAPISTS.

units.la: Aqua vino miscetur. Lotiones. Sacrificuli vertigines multivariae, & motus ridiculi, ad altare in Missa. Altaria ad Orientem extructa. Cerei ad imagines in altari accenduntur. Idola & hostia circumferuntur. Thus incenditur. (tur. Hostia venduntur, quoties emitor occurrat. Vestimenta Missatica adhibentur. Ad altare sacrificium offertur. Missa varia, pro vivis: peregrinantibus: aegrotis: mortuis.
units.tr: Water is mixed with wine. Washings. The little priest's manifold twistings and ridiculous motions at the altar in the Mass. Altars built facing east. Wax candles are lit before the images on the altar. Idols and victims are carried around. Incense is burned. Victims are sold, whenever a buyer turns up. Mass vestments are used. Sacrifice is offered at the altar. Masses are said for the living, for travellers, for the sick, for the dead.

units.la: Item pro pace: lachrymis: pluvia: serenitate: sapientia: stabili loco: incarcerato: contra sterilitatem: pestem: tribulationes: & pro agonizante.
units.tr: Likewise for peace, for tears, for rain, for fair weather, for wisdom, for a settled place, for a prisoner, against barrenness, against plague, against tribulations, and for the dying.

units.la: Sic horae canonicae, mane, vesperi, & aliis statis temporibus observantur.
units.tr: So too the canonical hours are observed in the morning, in the evening, and at other set times.

Superficiei, contra ulcera & tumores, Cosmas, & Damianus. & rabidi canis morsum, Hubertus. ab Eryfipelate, qui ignis sacer, Antonius. Obligationi vulnerum, Æsculapius. PATRO-
units.tr: For prevention from all diseases; of parts, dry things; the twelve signs of the Zodiac are seen in the table. Cure in general, by a single remedy; of species, diseases defined by natural differences, by medicines; indefinite, by bloodletting. Of the whole body, of the parts: of the generated and the ungenerated; the surface of the limbs; the rest of the body; of the extremities. Of the chest, of the abdomen, of the head, of all the parts. {Among the heathen.} {Among the Papists.} For prevention from all diseases, Hygieia: Servatius. For preserving the viscera, Carna: Mary, the angels, the saints. For curing diseases, Aesculapius: Raphael the Archangel. From non-poisonous diseases, of the whole body, namely fever, Febris, lest it harm: Petronella. From quartan fever, Sigismund. Of the parts: of the whole head, from epilepsy, Hercules: John and Valentine. Of the parts of the head, from diseases of the eyes, Otilia. and redness, Clara. Of the teeth: for extraction of teeth, sons of Aesculapius; for their pain, of the chest, from quinsy, cough, Apollonia. from asthma, Angerona: Blaise. from ulceration of the breasts, Agatha. Of the abdomen, from stone, Liberius and Benedict. from diseases of the genitals, Apollinaris. from disorders of the womb, Stephen. of the menses, Mena. Of the limbs, from arthritis, Wolfgang. Of the surface, against ulcers and tumours, Cosmas and Damian. and the bite of a mad dog, Hubert. from erysipelas, which is holy fire, Anthony. for binding of wounds, Aesculapius. PATRO-
