units.la: SIc, de Idololatricâ Sanctorum Invocatione, & Salutione Angelicâ, unâ cum Appendice superstitiosæ & magicę creaturarum consecrationis : sic etiam de Sanctis, quos Pontificii, & his hoc tempore succenturiati Jesuitæ, Ethnicos, ut in aliis plerisq;, ita in parte quoque istâ imitati, Patronos & Deos tutelares, rebus penè universis atque singulis assignant.
units.tr: Thus, concerning the idolatrous invocation of the saints and the angelic salutation, together with the appendix on the superstitious and magical consecration of creatures; and thus also concerning the saints, whom the Papists, and the Jesuits who have been brought in as reserves in this age, have imitated the heathen, as in many other respects, so also in this part, assigning to almost every single thing its patrons and guardian gods.

units.la: Restat, ut de tertiâ etiam libri parte agamus, quæ Reliquias Sanctorū, quas vocant, complectitur. De quâ non dubitârim tritum, istud pronuntiare:
units.tr: It remains that we deal also with the third part of the book, which embraces the so-called relics of the saints. Concerning it I would not hesitate to pronounce that well-worn saying:

units.la: Risum teneatis, amici.
units.tr: Hold your laughter, friends.

units.la: Ecce enim, introducimus mirificos Sanctos, quos monstra potiùs hominum, quàm homines veros dixeris. Ecquem nanq;, obsecro te, eum hominem pronuntiâris, cui corpora duo, imò non duo, sed tria, quin non tria, sed quatuor; cui pro capite uno tria, sic tria vel etiam quatuor brachia pro duobus, attribuantur?
units.tr: For behold, we are introducing wondrous saints, whom you would call monsters rather than true men. For what man, I beg you, would you pronounce a man, to whom two bodies are attributed, or rather not two but three, nay not three but four; to whom, for one head, three or even four arms are assigned in place of two?

units.la: Cerbero tria capita assignari, ægrè feri-mus, idq; ab ipsis etiam Poëtis, quibus fingere, ut & pictoribus quoidvis licet, item-dem is tamen. Et sanctis Dei hominibus, corcorpora affingi, eosque à Monachis, genere omnium, quotquot in universo terrarum orbe vivunt, impudentissimo, in monstra horrenda ingentia transmutari, patienter feramus? Non admittit hoc Christiana pietas, quæ de Sanctis ipsis piè & honorificè sentire jubet, utpote fidelibus Dei servis, & fortissimis Jesu Christi athletis, qui vitam, cum morte crudeli, charissimam commutando, pro nomine Servatoris unici occumbere nō dubitarunt, ac proinde gloriosi victores, in Ecclesia triumphante, coronam vitæ, at quàm dulce brabeum! aureolum illud præmium consecuti sunt.
units.tr: We bear it with difficulty that Cerberus is given three heads, and this even by the poets themselves, to whom it is permitted to feign whatever they like, as it is to painters; yet it is the same thing. Shall we patiently bear that bodies are attached to the holy men of God, and that they are transformed into horrible, huge monsters by the monks, of all kinds the most shameless of everyone who lives in the whole world? Christian piety does not admit this, which bids us think and speak piously and honourably of the saints themselves, as faithful servants of God and most valiant athletes of Jesus Christ, who did not hesitate to die for the name of the one Saviour, exchanging a most dear life for a cruel death; and therefore, as glorious victors in the triumphant Church, they obtained the crown of life, and what a sweet prize, that golden little reward!

units.la: At illis ea affingere, quæ cum ipsorum ignominiâ & infamiâ conjuncta sunt, & male feriatis Sanctos deridendos propinant, id verò iniusmodi est, ut nullâ apud hypocritas iustos venia dignum sit, ut nullam apud improbos illos hierophantas mereatur excusationem.
units.tr: But to attribute to them things that are bound up with their disgrace and infamy, and to offer the saints, ill-treated, to be mocked, is of such a kind that it deserves no pardon from upright hypocrites, and merits no excuse from those wicked hierophants.

units.la: Repeto hoc: Veneramur Sanctos; sed facere aliter non possumus, certè non debemus, quin commenta Monachorum putidissima, quibus Jesuitæ, longè iis ipsis impudentiores, hac luce, quæ haud scio an clarior esse queat, turpiter patrocinari, causæ pessimæ pessimi advocati, non erubescunt, toto pectore execremur, & quod corde sentimus, ore etiam profiteamur, ac scriptis publicis testatum faciamus.
units.tr: I repeat this: we venerate the saints; but we cannot do otherwise, and certainly ought not, than with our whole heart execrate the most putrid fictions of the monks, which the Jesuits, far more shameless than those very monks, do not blush to defend shamefully in this light, which I scarcely know could be any clearer, a worst cause with a worst advocate. What we feel in our heart we should also profess with our mouth, and make attested in public writings.

units.la: Itaqui
units.tr: Therefore.

units.la: Itaque, si placet, audiamus recitari ex infinitis aliis nonnulla. Nam universa atque singula qui commemorare velit, scilicet is laborem suscepcrit immensum, scilicet is in hujuscemodi narratione cum opera oleum perdiderit. Prius tamen hoc repeto:
units.tr: Therefore, if you please, let us hear some of the countless others recited. For whoever wished to recount them all, one by one, would undertake an immense labour, and in such a narrative would surely waste his oil along with his effort. Yet first I repeat this:

units.la: Risum teneatis, amici.
units.tr: Hold your laughter, friends.

units.la: Vestigia pedis ad mare a Petro oblati, frustum.
units.tr: Footprint at the sea, offered by Peter, a fragment.

units.la: 2. Sanguis, qui ex hostiis fluxit, Lutetiae, ad Johannis Arenarii: & ad Johannis Angelici: & Divioni: & alibi.
units.tr: 2. Blood which flowed from the hosts, at Paris, at John Arenarius's, and at John Angelicus's, and at Dijon, and elsewhere.

units.la: 3. Cultellus, quo hostia transfixa a Judaeo, Lutetiae ad Johannis Arenarii.
units.tr: 3. Knife with which a host was pierced by a Jew, at Paris, at John Arenarius's.

units.la: 4. Pedum Christi vestigia, quae solo impressit, post Ascensionem nonnullis apparens. Sic Romae, ad Laurentii, ubi Petro obvius factus: & Pictavii ad Radegondae: & apud Suessiones: & Arelate.
units.tr: 4. Footprints of Christ, which he left on the ground, appearing to some after the Ascension. So at Rome, at St Lawrence's, where he met Peter; and at Poitiers, at Radegund's; and at Soissons; and at Arles.

units.la: 5. Natium Christi forma, quas lapidi impressit, factus latomus, ut atrium templi aedificaret, Rhemis, in lapide, post majus altare.
units.tr: 5. Imprint of Christ's knees, which he left on a stone while working as a stonecutter to build the temple court, at Reims, in the stone, behind the high altar.

units.la: 6. Imagines, quae per miraculum factae.
units.tr: 6. Images, which were made by a miracle.

units.la: Z f r, Corpo-
units.tr: Z f r, Body-

units.la: 1. Corporis Christi, Romæ, ad Mariæ, quæ vocatur in porticu: & ad Johannis Lateranensis.
units.tr: 1. Body of Christ, at Rome, at St Mary's which is called "in portico," and at St John Lateran's.

units.la: Ejusdem, cum esset 12. annorum, ibidem.
units.tr: Of the same, when he was twelve years old, in the same place.

units.la: Alia, apud Lucenses, ab angelis efficta.
units.tr: Another, among the people of Lucca, made by angels.

units.la: 2. Crucis Christi, Brixiæ: & apud Curtonenses.
units.tr: 2. Of the Cross of Christ, at Brescia, and among the people of Cortona.

units.la: 3. Quæ miracula ediderunt.
units.tr: 3. Which have performed miracles.

units.la: Crucifixorum.
units.tr: Of the crucifixes.

units.la: 1. Quibus barba crevit, Burgis in Hispania: & ad Salvatoris: & Aurengiæ.
units.tr: 1. Which grew a beard, at Burgos in Spain, at the church of the Saviour, and at Orange.

units.la: 2. quæ locutæ sunt, ad D. Dionysii, in Francia.
units.tr: 2. Which spoke, at St Denis in France.

units.la: 3. quæ lachrymatæ. Ex his una lachryma, Vindonici: alia Treviris: alia, apud D. Maximinum: alia Aureliæ, ad Petri puellaris.
units.tr: 3. Which wept. Of these, one tear is at Vendôme, another at Trier, another at St Maximin, and another at Orléans, at the church of St Peter "Puellaris".

units.la: II. MARIÆ.
units.tr: II. OF MARY.

units.la: 1. Partes. Capilli, Romæ, ad Mariæ supra Minervam: & in Hispania ad Salvatoris: & Mantisconc: & Cluniaci & Nuceriæ ad Sanctoridi: & Saniacquerii: & Luteciæ ad Stephani.
units.tr: 1. Parts. Hair, at Rome, at Santa Maria sopra Minerva; and in Spain at the Saviour's church; and at Mantes-Conc, at Cluny, at Nocera, at Sanctoridus, at Saint-Jacques, and at Paris, at St Stephen's.

units.la: Lac. Ubiq; ostenditur, in pixide vitreâ, aut crystallinâ.
units.tr: Milk. Shown everywhere, in a glass or crystal pyx.

units.la: 2. Vestes & supellex.
units.tr: 2. Garments and furnishings.

units.la: Interula seu camisia, Carnutis, & Aquis.
units.tr: Undergarment or shift, at Chartres and at Aachen.

units.la: Peplum, Treviris, ad D. Maximini: & Lisii in Italia: & Caffini.
units.tr: Cloak, at Trier, at St Maximinus's; at Lisio in Italy; and at Cassino.

units.la: Pittacium, ex Maria interula vel peplo, Bononiæ,
units.tr: Patch, from Mary's undergarment or cloak, at Bologna.

units.la: Cingulum, Prati: & ad Mariæ Montisferra-ti: & Halæ.
units.tr: Girdle, at Prato; at Our Lady of Montferrat; and at Halle.

units.la: Crepida, apud Saniacquerium.
units.tr: Sandal, at Saint-Jacques.

units.la: Calceus, apud Sanfloridum.
units.tr: Shoe, at Saint-Flour.

units.la: Pallen, Romæ, ad Martini & Vefontii, ad Johannis.
units.tr: Veil, at Rome, at the churches of Martin and of Besançon, at John's.

units.la: Acus, fila, & quasillum, Halæ.
units.tr: Needle, threads, and distaff, at Halle.

units.la: Annulus sponsaliorum, Perusii.
units.tr: Betrothal ring, at Perugia.

units.la: Vestes, Romæ, ad Johannis Lateranensis: & ad Barbaræ: & ad Mariæ supra Minervam: & ad Blasii: & in Hispaniâ ad Salvatoris: & Cassini, in altari Gregorii.
units.tr: Garments, at Rome, at St John Lateran's, at Barbara's, at Santa Maria sopra Minerva, at Blaise's; in Spain at the Saviour's church; and at Cassino, on the altar of Gregory.

units.la: 3. Imagines, depictæ à Luca. 1. Romæ, ad Mariæ inviolatæ. 2. ad Mariæ novæ. 3. ad Mariæ, Aræ cæli. 4. & ad Augustini. 5. & Cameraci.
units.tr: 3. Images, painted by Luke. 1. At Rome, at Our Lady Inviolate. 2. At Our Lady of the New (church). 3. At Our Lady of the Altar of Heaven. 4. And at Augustine's. 5. And at Cambrai.

units.la: III. JOSEPHI.
units.tr: III. OF JOSEPH.

units.la: Annulus Mariæ datus in desponsatione, Romæ, ad Mariæ inviolatæ.
units.tr: Ring of Mary, given at the betrothal, at Rome, at Our Lady Inviolate.

units.la: Caliga & subligaculum, Aquis, unâ cum intertextâ Mariæ.
units.tr: Boot and loincloth, at Aachen, together with a piece of Mary's woven cloth.

units.la: Crepida, Treviris, in Cœnobio Simeonis.
units.tr: Sandal, at Trier, in the monastery of Simeon.

units.la: Offa illius.
units.tr: His bone.

units.la: IV. MICHAELIS Angeli.
units.tr: IV. OF THE ANGEL MICHAEL.

units.la: Reliquia, apud Carcassonenses: & Turonenses, Ad Juliani.
units.tr: Relic, at Carcassonne; and at Tours, at Julian's.

units.la: Sica, ad Magni Michaëlis.
units.tr: Dagger, at the church of Great Michael.

units.la: Clypeus, ibidem.
units.tr: Shield, in the same place.

units.la: V. IOHANNIS Baptistæ. I. Partes.
units.tr: V. Of John the Baptist. I. Parts.

units.la: 1. Capitis partes.
units.tr: 1. Parts of the head.

units.la: Facies, tum vulnere ab Herodiade infliEto, Ambiis, ad Johannis Angelici.
units.tr: Face, with the wound inflicted by Herodias, at Amiens, at St John of Angély.

units.la: Posterior pars, in Rhodo: nunc in Melitâ. Occiput, Nemorosi.
units.tr: Back part, at Rhodes; now at Malta. Occiput, at Nemours.

units.la: Cerebrum, Novii Rantroviensis.
units.tr: Brain, of Novius of Rantrovium.

units.la: Pars capitis alia, ad Johannis, Morienni: Et Cassini, in turri argentea, in arcu majore.
units.tr: Another part of the head, at St John's in Maurienne; and at Cassino, in the silver tower, in the great arch.

units.la: Mandibula, Vesentione, ad Johannis Majoris: & Lutetiæ ad Johan. Lateranensis.
units.tr: Jawbone, at Besançon, at St John Major; and at Paris, at St John Lateran.

units.la: Auricula extremum, ad Sanfloridi, in Artois, in Hispaniâ, ad Salvatoris. Capilli, (menia.
units.tr: Tip of the ear, at Sanflori, in Artois; in Spain, at the Saviour's. Hair, (walls.

units.la: , Dens, apud Tronchinianos Monachos, prope Gandavum.
units.tr: Tooth, among the Tronchinian monks, near Ghent.

units.la: Frustum, Noviodúni.
units.tr: Fragment, at Noyon.

units.la: Pars alia, Lucæ.
units.tr: Another part, of Luke.

units.la: (2.) Caput integrum, Romæ in Sylvestri cœnobio & Gandavi; & in Aquitaniâ allatū.
units.tr: (2.) Whole head, at Rome in the monastery of Sylvester and at Ghent; and brought to Aquitaine.

units.la: 2. Corporis partes.
units.tr: 2. Parts of the body.

units.la: Brachium, Senis.
units.tr: Arm, at Siena.

units.la: Digitus, quo Agnum Dei, Christum, monstra-vit, 1. Vesentione, ad Johannis Magni. 2. Tholosæ. 3. Lugduni. 4. Biturigibus. 5. Florentiæ. 6. ad Johannis Fortuiti, prope Matisconem. Digiti, pro uno, numero sex.
units.tr: Finger with which he pointed out the Lamb of God, Christ: 1. at Besançon, at St John the Great; 2. at Toulouse; 3. at Lyon; 4. at Bourges; 5. at Florence; 6. at St John Fortuit, near Mâcon. Fingers, counted as one, make six in number.

units.la: Cineres, Genuæ: & Romæ, ad Johannis Lateranensis.
units.tr: Ashes, at Genoa; and at Rome, at St John Lateran.

units.la: II. Vestimenta.
units.tr: II. Vestments.

units.la: Calceus, Lutetiæ, apud Carthusianos.
units.tr: A shoe, at Paris, among the Carthusians.

units.la: Cilicium, Romæ ad Johannis Lateranensis.
units.tr: A hair shirt, at Rome, at the Lateran of John.

units.la: Ara, super quam precabatur in deserto, Romæ ad S. Johannis Lateranensis.
units.tr: The altar, upon which he prayed in the desert, at Rome, at the Lateran of St. John.

units.la: Gladius, quo decollatus est, Avinione.
units.tr: The sword with which he was beheaded, at Avignon.

units.la: Linteum, decollando substratum, Aquis.
units.tr: A linen cloth, laid under him when he was beheaded, at Aix.

units.la: Miracula. S. Johannis caput in patina sanguinem sudavit, Brettā.
units.tr: Miracles. The head of St. John sweated blood in a dish, at Brescia.

units.la: VI. SS. APOSTOLORVM.
units.tr: VI. THE HOLY APOSTLES.

units.la: I. Petri & Pauli, conjunctim.
units.tr: I. Of Peter and Paul, together.

units.la: Corpora. Dimidia pars, ad Petri, Romæ: altera pars, ad Pauli, Romæ, & quidem à Sylvestro parte utraque probè & æquè librata.
units.tr: Bodies. Half, at Peter's, at Rome; the other half, at Paul's, at Rome; and indeed divided between the two parts by Sylvester, very properly and evenly balanced.

units.la: Caput utriusq;, Romæ, ad Johannis Lateranensis.
units.tr: Head of each, at Rome, at John's of the Lateran.

units.la: Ossa, Treveris: & passim alibi.
units.tr: Bones, at Trier; and scattered elsewhere.

units.la: Vestes, Cassini, in altari Gregorii.
units.tr: Vestments, at Cassino, on the altar of Gregory.

units.la: II. Petri seorsim.
units.tr: II. Of Peter alone.

units.la: Cerebellum, Genevæ, ad majus altare. nb. Impostores pumicem miserae plebeculae mõ-straverant.
units.tr: Little brain, at Geneva, at the high altar. Note: the impostors had displayed a pumice stone to the wretched common folk.

units.la: Capitis pars, Romæ ad Praxedis.
units.tr: Part of the head, at Rome, at Praxedes'.

units.la: Capilli, in cœnobio Hirsaugiensi.
units.tr: Hair, in the monastery of Hirsau.

units.la: Mandibula cum barbâ, Pictavii.
units.tr: Jawbone with beard, at Poitiers.

units.la: Dentes, alibi plures, alibi singuli; Romæ ad Vincentii: & Anastasii: & Crucis: & Salvatoris: & Lateranensis: & Laurentii extra muros: & Sebastiani; & Praxedis;
units.tr: Teeth, in some places several, in others single; at Rome, at Vincent's, and Anastasius', and the Cross, and the Saviour's, and the Lateran, and Lawrence's outside the walls, and Sebastian's, and Praxedes'.

units.la: Lacerti pars, Romæ, ad Crucis.
units.tr: Part of an arm, at Rome, at the Cross.

units.la: Pollex, Argentinæ.
units.tr: Thumb, at Strasbourg.

units.la: Articuli digiti gigantei, in Anglia ad Parathalassiæ.
units.tr: Joints of a giant's finger, in England, at Parathalassia.

units.la: Coste pars, Romæ, ad Sebastiani.
units.tr: Part of a rib, at Rome, at Sebastian's.

units.la: Pedis digitus, Romæ ad Praxedis.
units.tr: Toe, at Rome, at Praxedes'.

units.la: Crepida, in Hispania ad Salvatoris: & alia Pictavii, ex serico raso & auro segmentata.
units.tr: Sandal, in Spain, at the Saviour's; and another at Poitiers, decorated with smooth silk and gold segments.

units.la: Cathedra Episcopalis, cum veste Sacerdotali, vel Missatica, Romæ.
units.tr: Episcopal chair, with the priestly or mass vestment, at Rome.

units.la: Altare, Romæ: & Pisis, in suburbio, quod ad mare vergit.
units.tr: Altar, at Rome; and at Pisa, in the suburb that faces the sea.

units.la: Gladius, quo Malcho abscidit auriculam,
units.tr: Sword, with which he cut off the ear of Malchus.

units.la: Pedum, Lutetiæ ad Stephani. (ibidem.
units.tr: Crozier, at Paris, at Stephen's. (In the same place.)

units.la: Scipio, Coloniæ: & Treviris.
units.tr: Shoulder-blade, at Cologne; and at Trier.

units.la: Catena, qua ligatus, Romæ, ad Petri.
units.tr: Chain, with which he was bound, at Rome, at Peter's.

units.la: Columna, super qua capite truncatus est, ad Anastasii.
units.tr: Column, against which he was beheaded, at Anastasius'.

units.la: III. PAULI seorsim.
units.tr: III. Of Paul alone.

units.la: Humerus, Argentinæ Biturigum.
units.tr: Shoulder, at Strasbourg, at Bourges.

units.la: CÆTERORUM X. APOSTOLORUM.
units.tr: The Remaining Ten Apostles.

units.la: I. corpora integra. Sex. Jacobi majoris. Jacobi minoris. Andreæ. Philippi. Simonis, & Judæ.
units.tr: I. Whole bodies: six, of James the Greater, James the Less, Andrew, Philip, Simon and Jude.

units.la: Unum: Matthiæ, Pictavii.
units.tr: One: Matthias, at Poitiers.

units.la: Matthæi, Salerni. Thomæ, Ortonnæ.
units.tr: Matthew, at Salerno. Thomas, at Ortona.

units.la: Bartholomæi, Neapoli.
units.tr: Bartholomew, at Naples.

units.la: Duo: Andreæ, etiam Melphis, præter id, quod apud Tholosates extat. Philippi, & Jacobi minoris } etiam Romæ, ad Sanctos Apostolos: præter prius, quod Tholosates habent. Simon, & Judas } etiâ Romæ, ad Petri: præter id, quod apud Tholosates extat.
units.tr: Two: Andrew, also at Melfi, besides the one that exists at Toulouse. Philip and James the Less, also at Rome, at the Holy Apostles, besides the earlier one that the Toulousians have. Simon and Jude, also at Rome, at St Peter's, besides the one that exists at Toulouse.

units.la: Bartholomæus, etiam Romæ, ad Bartholomei: præter id, quod Neapoli monstratur.
units.tr: Bartholomew, also at Rome, at St Bartholomew's, besides the one shown at Naples.

units.la: Hujus etiam pellis, Pisis.
units.tr: His skin also at Pisa.

units.la: Tria: Matthiæ, Pictavii: & Romæ, ad Mariæ majoris: & Treviris.
units.tr: Three: Matthias, at Poitiers, and at Rome, at Santa Maria Maggiore, and at Trier.

units.la: 1. Frusta, de corporibus Apostolorum.
units.tr: 1. Fragments, concerning the bodies of the Apostles.

units.la: Reliquiæ XII. Apostolorum, Petri, Pauli, Andreæ, Johannis, Jacobi utriusq;, Thomæ, Bartholomæi, Matthiæ, Simonis, Judæ, & Matthiæ, Cassini. Matthiæ caput, Romæ ad Petri, humerus, ad Chrisogoni. costa, ad Eustachii. brachium, ad Spiritus. alterum brachium, Lutetiæ, ad Stephani, pes, Aquis Sextiis. pars alia, ad Blasii. vestis, Cassini in turri argentea, quæ est in arcu majore. Bartholomæi pellis, Pisis, manus, ibidem. aliud membrum, Treveris, digitus, Romæ, ad Barbaræ. Philippi pes, Romæ, ad sanctos Apostolos. brachium, in templo Ilunensi. aliud membrum, Romæ ad Barbaræ: & Treveris. Jacobi, caput, Romæ ad Petri, brachium unum, ad Chrisogoni. brachium alterum, ad S. Apostolos. brachium tertium, Mathildis Francorum Regina, ad Patrem suum in Angliam revertens, eo detulit, anno 1125. Matthaei ossa, Treveris. brachium unum, Caffini. brachium alterum, Romæ, ad Marcelli, caput, ad Nicolai.
units.tr: Relics of the twelve Apostles: Peter, Paul, Andrew, John, both James, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthias, Simon, Jude, and Matthias (again), at Cassino. Head of Matthias, at Rome, at St Peter's; shoulder, at St Chrysogonus; rib, at St Eustace; arm, at the Holy Spirit; the other arm, at Paris, at St Stephen's; foot, at Aix-en-Provence; another part, at St Blaise; garment, at Cassino, in the silver tower which is in the major citadel. Skin of Bartholomew, at Pisa; hand, there. Another limb, at Trier; finger, at Rome, at St Barbara's. Foot of Philip, at Rome, at the Holy Apostles; arm, in the church at Ilun; another limb, at Rome at St Barbara's, and at Trier. Head of James, at Rome, at St Peter's; one arm at St Chrysogonus; a second arm at the Holy Apostles; a third arm, which Matilda, Queen of the Franks, carried to England when she returned to her father, in the year 1125. Bones of Matthew, at Trier. One arm at Cassino; a second arm at Rome, at St Marcellus; head, at St Nicholas.

units.la: Thomæ, nil nisi corpus extat amplius.
units.tr: Of Thomas, nothing but the body survives any more.

units.la: Johannis Apostoli & Evangelistæ, Calix, e quo venenum bibit, Bononiæ: & Romæ, ad Johannis Lateranensis.
units.tr: The cup of John the Apostle and Evangelist, from which he drank poison, at Bologna; and at Rome, at St John Lateran.

units.la: Tunica, & aliæ vestes, Caffini, in turri argentea, quæ est in arce majore.
units.tr: Tunic and other garments, at Cassino, in the silver tower which is in the major citadel.

units.la: Catena, quâ vinctus ducebatur ab Ephesō, Oratorium, ubi vinctus precabatur.
units.tr: The chain with which he was led bound from Ephesus; the oratory where, while bound, he prayed.

units.la: Monile XII. pectinum Apostolicorum, Lugduni, ad Mariæ Infulinæ.
units.tr: A necklace of the twelve combs of the Apostles, at Lyon, at (the church of) Mary of Infulina.

units.la: Marci Evangelistæ, corpus unum, in Reichenau, alterum, Venetiis.
units.tr: Of Mark the Evangelist, one body at Reichenau, another at Venice.

units.la: VII. SANCTORUM, tempore Christi.
units.tr: VII. OF THE SAINTS, from the time of Christ.

units.la: 1. Anna, matris Mariae virginis.
units.tr: 1. Anne, mother of the Virgin Mary.

units.la: Corpus unum, Aptae, oppido Provinciae: alterum, Lugduni, ad Mariae Insulanae.
units.tr: One body at Apt, a town in Provence; another at Lyons, at Mariae Insulanae.

units.la: Caput unum, Treveris: alterum, Tureni, apud Juliacenses. tertiu, oppido Thuringiae, Annabergae.
units.tr: One head at Trier; another at Turin, among the people of Jülich. A third in the town of Annaberg in Thuringia.

units.la: Fragmenta, Urficampi, coenobio agri Noviodunensis: & plus quam centum in locis.
units.tr: Fragments at Ourscamp, in the abbey of the Noyon country, and in more than a hundred places.

units.la: Brachium, Romae, ad Pauli.
units.tr: An arm at Rome, at St Paul's.

units.la: 2. Simeonis, brachium, Aquis.
units.tr: 2. Simeon: an arm at Aachen.

units.la: 3. Lazari, corpus unum, Massiliae: alterum, Augustoduni: tertium, Avalonae.
units.tr: 3. Lazarus: one body at Marseilles, another at Autun, and a third at Avallon.

units.la: 4. Magdalena, sororis ejus,
units.tr: 4. Mary Magdalene, the sister of Lazarus.

units.la: Corpus unum, Veseli, prope Altissiodorum: alterum, apud Sanmaximinum, oppidum Provinciae.
units.tr: One body at Vézelay, near Auxerre; another at Saint-Maximin, a town in Provence.

units.la: Caput, &c
units.tr: Head, etc.

units.la: vota Christi, quam ei iratus impressit, quod ipsum vellet attingere, sic fatus: Noli me tangere. Ibidem.
units.tr: ...the touch which Christ, in anger, impressed on her when she wished to touch him, saying: "Noli me tangere." Ibid.

units.la: Ossa, &c
units.tr: Bones, etc.

units.la: capilli, per universum orbem.
units.tr: Hair, throughout the whole world.

units.la: 5. Longini, latus Christi lancea aperientis,
units.tr: 5. Longinus, the soldier who opened Christ's side with his lance.

units.la: Corpus, unum, Mantuae.
units.tr: One body at Mantua.

units.la: alterum, Lugduni, ad Mariae Insulanae.
units.tr: Another at Lyons, at Mariae Insulanae.

units.la: 6. Magorum, trium scilicet Regum, Melchioris, Caspar is, & Balthasaris,
units.tr: 6. The Magi, namely the three Kings, Melchior, Caspar and Balthasar.

units.la: Corpora, altera Coloniæ;
units.tr: Bodies: one at Cologne;

units.la: altera, Mediolani, ad Euftorgii.
units.tr: another at Milan, at St Eustorgius.

units.la: VIII. MARTYRUM.
units.tr: VIII. OF MARTYRS.

units.la: 1. Dionysii, habiti pro discipulo, Apostolorū, corpus unum, Ratisbonæ:
units.tr: 1. One body of Dionysius, held to be a disciple of the Apostles, at Regensburg;

units.la: alterum, Sandionysii, in agro Parisiano, regni Franciæ.
units.tr: another, of Saint-Denis, in the countryside near Paris, in the kingdom of France.

units.la: caput, Lutetiæ, ad Stephani.
units.tr: The head, at Paris, in the church of St Stephen.

units.la: 2. Stephani, corpus, Romæ, ad Stephani caput, Arelate.
units.tr: 2. The body of Stephen, at Rome, in the church of St Stephen; the head at Arles.

units.la: Offa, plus quam ducentis locis.
units.tr: Bones, in more than two hundred places.

units.la: Lapides, Florentiæ: & Arelate, apud Augustinenses & Viganii in Aquitaniâ: & Pictavii: & Friburgi Brisgoiæ, apud Johannitas.
units.tr: Stones, at Florence; and at Arles, in the Augustinians' church; at Vigan in Aquitaine; at Poitiers; and at Freiburg im Breisgau, in the Johannites' church.

units.la: 3. Innocentium puerorum corpora, in Galliâ, Germaniâ, Italiâ, & ubique terrarum.
units.tr: 3. Bodies of the Innocents, in France, Germany, Italy, and everywhere in the world.

units.la: 4. Viti, testiculi, Friburgi Brisgoiæ.
units.tr: 4. The testicles of Vitus, at Freiburg im Breisgau.

units.la: 5. Laurentii corpus, Romæ, ad Laurentii vas plenum ascæ carnis, ibidem:
units.tr: 5. The body of Lawrence, at Rome, in the church of St Lawrence in Palisperna, with a vessel full of his burnt flesh in the same place;

units.la: ampulla duæ, una sanguinis, altera adipis ejus plena.
units.tr: two flasks, one full of his blood, the other of his fat.

units.la: brachium, &
units.tr: An arm, and

units.la: offa, in æde Palispernæ.
units.tr: a bone, in the church of Palisperna.

units.la: brachium alterum, in Hispaniâ.
units.tr: Another arm, in Spain.

units.la: Reliquiæ aliæ, ad Sylvestri: & passim in Galliâ.
units.tr: Other relics, at St Sylvester's, and scattered throughout France.

units.la: craticula, super quâ assus fuit, tota:
units.tr: The gridiron on which he was roasted, whole;

units.la: craticulæ fragmentum, in æde Palispernę. carbones, ad Eustachii.
units.tr: a fragment of the gridiron, in the church of Palisperna. Coals, at St Eustace's.

units.la: mappa, quâ Angelus ei corpus abstersit.
units.tr: The cloth with which the angel wiped his body.

units.la: dalmatica, (Levitenrock) Romæ ad Barbaræ.
units.tr: The dalmatic (the Levite's coat), at Rome, at St Barbara's.

units.la: 6. Gervasii, &
units.tr: 6. Gervasius and

units.la: Protasii corpora & sepulchra, Mediolani: & Brisaci in Germania: & Vesentione ad Petri.
units.tr: Protasius: bodies and tombs, at Milan; and at Breisach in Germany; and at Besançon, at St Peter's.

units.la: frusta infinita.
units.tr: Countless fragments.

units.la: 7. Sebastiani corpora quatuor.
units.tr: 7. Four bodies of Sebastian.

units.la: unum, Romæ, ad Laurentii: alterum, Suessione, ad Medardi. tertium, Piligni, apud Armoricos: quartum, prope Narbonam, in solo eius natali.
units.tr: One at Rome, at St Lawrence's; another at Soissons, at St Medard's; a third at Pilgni, among the Armoricans; a fourth near Narbonne, in his native soil.

units.la: Capita tria. Unum, Romæ, ad Petri. alterū, Tholosæ, apud Dominicanos; tertium, Magdeburgi.
units.tr: Three heads. One at Rome, at St Peter's; another at Toulouse, among the Dominicans; a third at Magdeburg.

units.la: Cerebrum, Andegavi, apud Franciscanos. Brachium, unum, Andegavi, apud Dominicanos; alterum, Tholosæ, ad Saturnini. tertium, Caledei, in Auernia.
units.tr: The brain, at Angers, among the Franciscans. One arm at Angers, among the Dominicans; another at Toulouse, at St Saturninus'; a third at Chaldette, in Auvergne.

units.la: quartum, Monsbrisonnæ Foreftanorum.
units.tr: A fourth at Montbrison, in Forez.

units.la: Frusta minuta, passim.
units.tr: Small fragments, scattered about.

units.la: Sagitta, quibus transfixus, Lambesci, in Provincia: & Pictavii, apud Augustinienses: & passim.
units.tr: The arrows with which he was pierced, at Lambesc in Provence; and at Poitiers, among the Augustinians; and elsewhere.

units.la: Aij 8. Antonii
units.tr: Aij 8. Antonius

units.la: 8. Antonii, corpora duo. unum, Arelate: alterum, Viennæ, apud Antinianos; brachium, Genevæ. (Impostores monstrarunt caudam cervinam.) genu, apud Augustinienses in Helvetiâ. varia membra, Burgi: & Mantifcone: & Divione: Catalauni: & Ouronii: & Vesontione, &c.
units.tr: 8. Two bodies of Antony. One at Arles; the other at Vienne, among the Antonines; an arm at Geneva. (Impostors showed a deer's tail.) A knee, among the Augustinians in Switzerland. Various limbs at Bourg, at Mâcon, at Dijon, at Châlons, at Ouroux, at Besançon, etc.

units.la: 9. Petronella, filia Petri, corpora duo. Vnum, Romæ, ad Petri: alterum, Coenomani, apud Dominicanos, reliquiæ aliæ, ad Barbaræ.
units.tr: 9. Petronilla, daughter of Peter, two bodies. One at Rome, at St Peter's; the other at Le Mans, among the Dominicans; other relics at St Barbara's.

units.la: 10. Sufannæ, corpora duo. unum Romæ, ad Sufannæ: alterum Tholosæ. Vestes Caffini in turri argentea, quæ est in arcu majore.
units.tr: 10. Two bodies of Susanna. One at Rome, at St Susanna's; the other at Toulouse. The garments of Cassinus in the silver tower, which is on the great arch.

units.la: 11. Helena corpus, Venetiis. caput alterum, Coloniæ, ad Gereonis.
units.tr: 11. The body of Helena, at Venice. Another head, at Cologne, at St Gereon's.

units.la: 12. Vrsulæ corpus, ad Johannis Angelici. caput, Coloniæ; pars quaedam, Coenomani, apud Dominicanos: & apud Turonenses Dominicanos: & Bergerati.
units.tr: 12. The body of Ursula, at the church of John Angelicus. A head at Cologne; some part at Le Mans, among the Dominicans; and among the Dominicans at Tours; and at Bergerac.

units.la: 13. Undecim mille virginum offa passim habentur, quæ centum quadrigis onerandis non sufficerent.
units.tr: 13. Bones of the eleven thousand virgins are found everywhere, enough to fill more than a hundred wagons.

units.la: 14. De Margaretha reliquiis Dominicani & Carmelitæ rixantur.
units.tr: 14. Over the relics of Margaret the Dominicans and the Carmelites are quarrelling.

units.la: IX. VULGARIUM
units.tr: IX. OF THE COMMON RELICS

units.la: Sanctorum.
units.tr: Of the saints.

units.la: 1. Hilarii, corpora duo. unum, Pictavii, apud Canonicos, ad Hilarii: alterū, Sellç in Epiro, apud Monachos.
units.tr: 1. Two bodies of Hilary. One at Poitiers, with the canons, at St Hilary's church; the other at Sellæ in Epirus, with the monks.

units.la: 2. Honorati corpora duo, unum Arelate: alterum, Insulæ Lyrinorum, prope Antipolin.
units.tr: 2. Two bodies of Honoratus. One at Arles; the other on the island of Lérins, near Antibes.

units.la: 3. Ægidii, corpora duo. unum, Tholosæ. alterum, Aquitaniæ oppido ab Ægidio cognominato.
units.tr: 3. Two bodies of Giles. One at Toulouse; the other in a town of Aquitaine named after Giles.

units.la: 4. Guilielmi duo corpora. unum, in Cœnobio Aquitaniæ, cui nomen D. Guilielmi à deserto. alterum, in Holsatiâ, Ecrichenî. duo capita, ibidem in Holsatiâ unum: & in suburbio Tureni Juliacensium, apud Guilelmitanos, alterum.
units.tr: 4. Two bodies of William. One in the monastery in Aquitaine called St William of the Desert; the other in Holstein, at Ecrichen. Two heads: one in Holstein, in the same place; and the other in the suburb of Düren in the territory of Jülich, with the Guillemites.

units.la: 5. Symphoriani corpus, & ossa, passim.
units.tr: 5. The body and bones of Symphorian, scattered in many places.

units.la: 6. Lupi, Altisfiodori: & Senis: & Lugduni: & Genevæ.
units.tr: 6. Of Lupus: at Auxerre, at Siena, at Lyon, and at Geneva.

units.la: 7. Ferreoli corpus integrum, Uticæ in Aquitania unum: alterum, Briodæ Arvernorum.
units.tr: 7. The whole body of Ferreolus: one at Utica in Aquitaine; the other at Brioude in Auvergne.

units.la: 8. Lamberti caput apud Canonicos Trevirenses, unum: alterum, Leodii:
units.tr: 8. The head of Lambert: one with the canons of Trier; the other at Liège.

units.la: 9. Arbogasti, pars tibia, Argentinæ.
units.tr: 9. A shinbone of Arbogast, at Strasbourg.

units.la: 10. Leutgardis caput, in Maismünster.
units.tr: 10. The head of Leutgardis, at Maismünster.

units.la: X. EX VETERI TESTAMENTO:
units.tr: X. FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT:

units.la: 1. Abraha, Isaaci, Jacobi, {brace} ossa, Romæ, ad Mariæ super-Minervam.
units.tr: 1. Bones of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, at Rome, at Santa Maria sopra Minerva.

units.la: 2. Arca sederis & 3. Virga Aaronis, {brace} Romæ ad Johannis Lateranensis.
units.tr: 2. Ark of the covenant and 3. Rod of Aaron, at Rome, at St John Lateran.

units.la: Virga Aaronis seorsim, Lutetiæ, ad sacri Sacelli.
units.tr: The Rod of Aaron separately, at Paris, at the Holy Chapel.

units.la: Cum hac ipsâ virgâ Aaronis, eadem esse affirmatur virga D. Martialis, ad Severini, apud Burdegalenses.
units.tr: It is also affirmed that the rod of St Martial is the same as this very rod of Aaron, at St Severinus, among the people of Bordeaux.

units.la: virga fragmentum, in Hispaniâ, ad Salvatoris.
units.tr: A fragment of the rod, in Spain, at the Saviour's church.

units.la: 4. Candelabrum Salomonis, Pragæ.
units.tr: 4. Candlestick of Solomon, at Prague.

units.la: BENEDICTUS PAPA, OB amorem & reverentiam S.Benedicti, de Sacrario Lateranensis palatii Gassinum anno 1023. misit has reliquias.
units.tr: Pope Benedict, out of love and reverence for St Benedict, sent these relics from the sacristy of the Lateran palace to Gassino in the year 1023.

units.la: De ligno Domini: de sanguine Domini: de vestimentis Domini: de lapide S. sepulchri: de velo Sanctæ Dei genitricis Mariæ: Et eòdem reliquiæ Apostolorum Petri & Pauli, Andreæ, Iohannis, Iacobi, Thomæ, Bartholomæi, Matthæi, Simonis, Iudæ, & Matthiæ. Spongia cum sanguine sancti Protomartyris Stephani, Laurentii, Stephani Papæ, Pelagii Papæ: Martini Episcopi, Prudentii, Iuliani, Augustini, Christophori, Æmiliani, Nicandri, & Marciani, Alexii, Anastasiæ, Eugeniæ, Iohannis & Pauli, quadraginta martyrum, & aliorum multorum locata sunt.
units.tr: Of the wood of the Lord; of the blood of the Lord; of the garments of the Lord; of a stone from the Holy Sepulchre; of the veil of the holy Mother of God, Mary. Also relics of the Apostles Peter and Paul, Andrew, John, James, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon, Jude and Matthias. A sponge with the blood of the holy protomartyr Stephen; of Lawrence, Pope Stephen, Pope Pelagius, Martin the Bishop, Prudentius, Julian, Augustine, Christopher, Emilian, Nicander and Marcian, Alexius, Anastasia, Eugenia, John and Paul, of the forty martyrs, and of many others, have been placed here.

units.la: In altari S. Iohannis habetur,
units.tr: On the altar of St John there is:

units.la: Spongia, quæ fuit Christo porrecta cum aceto: ex oleo de candela sancti sepulchri, quæ per singulos annos modo valde mirabili, die sancti Sabbathi Paschalis, videntibus cunctis accenditur: de manna sepulchri S. Iohannis Evangelistæ: de aqua Iordanis, ex eo loco, ubi baptizatus est Dominus, S. Laurentii, Sebastiani, aliorumque multorum.
units.tr: A sponge which was offered to Christ with vinegar; oil from the lamp of the Holy Sepulchre, which every year on the holy Easter Saturday is lit in a most wonderful manner, with everyone watching; manna from the tomb of St John the Evangelist; water of the Jordan from the place where the Lord was baptized; of St Lawrence, Sebastian and many others.

units.la: In altari S. Mariæ, habetur
units.tr: On the altar of St Mary there is:

units.la: De Sepulchro ipsius: de reliquiis martyrum Dionysii Episcopi, Cæsarii Diaconi, Stephani Papæ, Primi & Feliciani.
units.tr: Of his sepulchre; of relics of the martyrs Dionysius the Bishop, Caesarius the Deacon, Pope Stephen, Primus and Felicianus.

units.la: In altari S. Gregorii.
units.tr: On the altar of St Gregory.

units.tr: Of the garment of St Mary, of the clothing of the Apostles Peter and Paul, and relics of the holy forty martyrs, Pancras, Valentine, Hilary, Bishop Martin; and of the dalmatic of St Ambrose.

units.la: In turri argentea, quæ est in arcu majore, reliquiæ iftæ funt pofitæ:

units.la: Lignum Domini, de lapide S. fepulchri.
units.tr: Wood of the Lord; of a stone from the Holy Sepulchre.

units.la: In fingularum columnarum ipfius Eccle- fiæ capitellis inclufæ,
units.tr: Enclosed in the capitals of each of the church's columns:

units.la: Reliquiæ Sanctorum Philippi & Iacobi, Iohannis & Pauli, Nicandri & Martiani, Cornelii & Cypriani, Cryni, Maximi, Sebaftiani, Phocæ, Eutychii, quadraginta martyrum: de capillis S. Remigii Episcopi.
units.tr: Relics of the saints Philip and James, John and Paul, Nicander and Marcian, Cornelius and Cyprian, Crispin, Maximus, Sebastian, Phocas, Eutychius, and the forty martyrs; of the hairs of St Remigius the Bishop.

units.la: In quatuor angelis Campanarii.
units.tr: In the four angels of the bell tower.

units.la: De lapide S. Sepulchri: de Geftimentis S. Mariæ, de lapide fepulchri ejus, fanctorum apoftolorum Iacobi, Philippi, Bartholomæi: Martini Episcopi.
units.tr: Of a stone from the Holy Sepulchre; of the garments of St Mary, of a stone from her tomb, of the holy Apostles James, Philip and Bartholomew; of Martin the Bishop.

units.la: In Cruce Campanarii.
units.tr: In the cross of the bell tower.

units.la: Lignum Domini, de capite S. Baptiftæ: Bartholomæi Apoftoli, Cyriaci Diaconi.
units.tr: Wood of the Lord; of the head of St John the Baptist; of the Apostle Bartholomew and Cyriacus the Deacon.

units.la: In frontispicio Ecclesiæ, in cruce ænea.
units.tr: In the front of the church, in the bronze cross.

units.la: Lignum Domini, de lapide S. Sepulchri, Mauri abbatis, & Sanctorum martyrum Iohannis & Pauli.
units.tr: Wood of the Lord; of a stone from the Holy Sepulchre; of Abbot Maurus, and of the holy martyrs John and Paul.

units.tr: In the Cassinese territory, at St Stephen's, in the year 1103, on the Nones of November.

Matthæi, Matthiæ, Bartholomæi, Stephani protomartyris, Laurentii, Vincentii, Sebaftiani, Cyriaci, duodecim fratrum, Cosmæ & Damiani, Lucia & Geminiani, Mariæ & Marthæ, Tiburtii & Valeriani, Georgii, Hippolytii, Martini Turonensis. nensis, Stephani, Calixti. Iacobo majori: de sepulchro Mariæ: decem millium militum: de præsepi Domini bis: de loco nativitatis Domini: de carne beata Elisabeth: de S. Mauricio & sociis: de S. Maria Magdalena, S. Hieronymi: de monte Calvaria, de cella Maria Virginis, in qua Angelus annunciavit Incarnationem Christi, S. Iohannis Baptista: de omnibus Sanctis aliquid, de S. Hedwigis, 2. frustula resina.

units.la: Plura commemorare desinô. Satiraq; fuerit, ista hactenus recensuisse. Etsi enim longe ista pluribus exemplis declarari possent: at piget me tamen tædetq; istiusmodi Monachorum comentis recensendis immorari diutius.
units.tr: I stop recounting more. It will be enough to have listed these so far. Even though these matters could be shown by far more examples, I am nevertheless weary and loath to linger longer over the recounting of such inventions of the monks.

units.la: Quod spero & opto, Lector Christiane, facile ex hactenus recitatis conjicere licebit, quàm horrenda Idololatria in regno Pontificio, tum ab ipsis Doctoribus, (quin seductoribus verius) tum à misera & culpa partem maximam ductorum cœcorum cœcutiente plebeculâ, impiâ & in Deum blasphemâ Sanctorum invocatione, committatur.
units.tr: Which I hope and wish, Christian reader, you will easily be able to gather from what has been recited so far: how horrible the idolatry is in the Papist realm, committed both by the teachers themselves (or rather, seducers) and by the common crowd, wretched and largely to blame, the greater part of blind men led by the blind, in an impious invocation of the saints that blasphemes God.

units.la: Nihil etiam addubito, quin luce meridiana clarius inde appareat, non nisi horum merito, Sanctifierificulis Papisticis hoc attribui, quòd consecra-tione superstitiosâ ipsos non tam Magos, & in-cantatores, quàm daemones, artium istarum au-tores imitentur.
units.tr: I do not doubt at all that it is clearer than the midday light that from this it appears that this is attributed, not without the merit of these men, to the Papist little priests, because by superstitious consecration they imitate not so much magicians and enchanters as the demons, the authors of those arts.

units.la: Speeadem ducor, quicunq; in harum pagel-larum lectione inciderit, nullo labore intelliges, Deos atq; Divas longè penè plures à Papistis Pa-tronos rerum in totâ hac universitate fermè o-mnium designari; idq; ad ipsum modum, ut ipsos etiam Ethnicos superasse videri possint.
units.tr: I am led by the same hope: whoever comes upon the reading of these little pages will understand without any effort that almost all the gods and goddesses, far more in number than the Papists have, are designated as patrons of things in this whole universe; and in the very same manner, so that they may seem to have surpassed even the heathens themselves.

units.la: De Reliquiis Sanctorum taceo. Siquidem res ea in propatulo est, si vel leviter, & quod dici so-let, obiter saltem, tabellam nostram inspexeris, ut nullus dubitem, quin illius lectio, risum tibi, non culpâ tamen meâ, sed superstitiosorum & impudentissimorum Monachorum vitio, unâ cum piâ execratione motura sit.
units.tr: I say nothing of the relics of the saints. For that matter lies in plain view, if you only glance, and as they say, merely in passing, at our little table, so that I have no doubt that its reading will move you to laughter, yet not through any fault of mine, but through the fault of superstitious and most shameless monks, together with pious execration.

units.la: Quod reliquum est, bene te valere jubeo, & Deum ex animo precor, tibi largiri dignetur di-lectionem Christi, & odium Papae, qui verus An-tichristus Diaboli se filium probat, mendax ipse & homicida, & Jesuitis, ipsis quoq; mendacibus atq; homicidiis, ac proinde Diabolis incarnatis, vel maximè, Patronis utitur. Id quod olim ab Ecclesia Graeca factitatum accepimus, qua Jo-hanni XXII. Papa totidem verbis rescripsit:
units.tr: As for the rest, I bid you farewell, and I earnestly pray God that He may deign to grant you the love of Christ and hatred of the Pope, who proves himself the true Antichrist, son of the Devil, a liar and murderer himself, and who makes use, above all, of the Jesuits, who are themselves liars and murderers, and therefore incarnate devils, as patrons. This is what we have learned was once done by the Greek Church, which wrote back to Pope John XXII in just these words:

units.la: Potentiam tuam summam circa tuos subditos firmi-ter credimus: superbiam tuam summam tolerare non possumus: avaritiam satiare non valemus. Diabolus tecum: quia Dominus nobiscum. Et omnis populus dicat, Amen.
units.tr: We firmly believe in your great power over your subjects; we cannot tolerate your great pride; we are not able to satisfy your greed. The Devil be with you, for the Lord is with us. And let all the people say, Amen.
